#2391. « Déchiré par la douleur » : Tragédie en Espagne, Tenerife annonce le décès de Jesús de Miguel Alameda

Le football espagnol est sous le choc ce mardi 3 novembre 2026. Le CD Tenerife a officialisé le décès de son attaquant Jesús de Miguel Alameda, survenu à 8h00 à l'âge de 30 ans, suite à un choc survenu lundi soir avec le gardien de l'équipe adverse.

Le drame est survenu lors d'un match de la 12e journée de deuxième division espagnole (LaLiga Hypermotion), disputé le lundi 2 novembre 2026 sur la pelouse du stade Heliodoro Rodríguez López. Alors que les deux équipes se neutralisaient dans une fin de match sous tension (2-2), la rencontre face au FC Andorra a été définitivement interrompue dans le temps additionnel suite à un choc très violent entre l'attaquant de Tenerife Jesús de Miguel Alameda et le gardien du FC Andorra Jesús Owono.

Le club de Tenerife a pris la parole ce mardi matin pour annoncer la terrible nouvelle. La formation espagnole a partagé sa profonde détresse face à la perte brutale de son avant-centre. À travers un communiqué officiel publié sur X, le club a tenu à exprimer toute sa tristesse et son soutien à la famille du joueur :

L'accident s'est produit dans le temps additionnel de cette rencontre indécise. Parti en contre sur un long dégagement, Jesús de Miguel a été heurté de plein fouet au niveau du haut du corps dans le rond central par une sortie aérienne non maîtrisée du gardien andorran Jesús Owono, dont le genou droit a percuté l'attaquant. Un choc particulièrement violent.

Face à la dangerosité de l'action, l'arbitre de la rencontre a immédiatement expulsé le gardien Jesús Owono d'un carton rouge direct pour usage d'une force excessive. D'ailleurs, selon la Cadena Cope, le portier était très affecté par les conséquences de son intervention. Le match a ensuite été définitivement interrompu afin de permettre l'intervention des secours et l'évacuation rapide du joueur.

Jesús de Miguel s'est effondré inerte au sol et a subi un arrêt cardiorespiratoire sur la pelouse avant d'être pris en charge en urgence. L'attaquant a fait l'objet d'une réanimation cardio-pulmonaire pratiquée par les services médicaux à l'intérieur de l'ambulance, lui permettant de respirer à nouveau par lui-même tout en restant inconscient.

Jesús de Miguel a ensuite été admis en soins intensifs à l'Hospital Universitario Nuestra Señora de Candelaria à Santa Cruz de Tenerife dans un état jugé stable mais grave. Toutefois, la situation s'est assombrie quelques heures plus tard. Dans la nuit de lundi à mardi, le CD Tenerife avait publié un message d'alerte sur X indiquant : « L’état médical de Jesus de Miguel s’est aggravé sur le plan neurologique. Plus d’informations dans les prochaines heures. »

Au-delà des espoirs suscités par les premiers gestes de secours, le joueur de 30 ans s'est éteint au petit matin des suites de ces complications neurologiques.

#2390. « Un changement est nécessaire » : West Ham ne perd pas de temps et décide de se séparer de Nuno Espirito Santo

West Ham United a officialisé ce mardi 3 novembre 2026 le limogeage avec effet immédiat de son entraîneur principal Nuno Espírito Santo. Le club londonien a décidé de trancher dans le vif après un début de saison particulièrement poussif en Championship.

Arrivé en septembre 2025 avec un contrat de trois ans, le technicien de 52 ans n'avait pas pu empêcher la relégation des Hammers à l'issue de la saison 2025-2026. Maintenu pour guider la remontée, Nuno Espírito Santo laisse l'équipe dans une position inconfortable. Après 13 journées de Championship, West Ham ne compte que six victoires et pointe à la huitième place du classement, à six points du leader Middlesbrough. Un bilan insuffisant.

Le sort de l'entraîneur portugais s'est scellé lors de deux revers consécutifs subis à domicile au London Stadium, face à Southampton (2-3) puis contre West Bromwich Albion (1-3). Deux contre-performances de trop pour la direction. Le co-propriétaire David Sullivan souhaitait déjà se séparer de Nuno Espírito Santo l'été dernier, mais l'actionnaire principal Daniel Kretinsky avait choisi de le maintenir. Le club s'était d'ailleurs offert Arne Engels pour 22 millions de livres en provenance du Celtic, un montant record pour la Championship. Nuno Espírito Santo s'en va sur un bilan de 19 victoires, 15 nuls et 19 défaites en 53 matchs dirigés. L'entraîneur adjoint Rui Pedro Silva et l'entraîneur des gardiens Rui Barbosa quittent également leurs fonctions au sein du club.

Au-delà des résultats comptables, la fracture s'est matérialisée dans les travées du London Stadium. Pendant et après la défaite contre West Bromwich Albion, les supporters des Hammers ont clairement manifesté leur colère. Une rupture consommée avec le public. Présent en conférence de presse après le revers face à West Bromwich Albion, Nuno Espírito Santo avait tenté d'éteindre l'incendie :

Pour parer au plus pressé, West Ham a confié l'intérim à un trio composé de Mark Noble, Steve Potts et Gerard Prenderville. Toutefois, la succession avance rapidement en coulisses. Selon les révélations de David Ornstein, le club a conclu un accord avec Scott Parker, 46 ans, pour succéder à Nuno Espírito Santo. Les dirigeants londoniens espèrent qu'il sera en poste pour le déplacement à Cardiff et que Mark Noble intégrera son futur staff.

West Ham United dispute son prochain match ce mercredi 4 novembre 2026 sur la pelouse de Cardiff City, dans le cadre de la 14e journée de Championship.

#2389. Portugal : Grande première pour le fils de Cristiano Ronaldo !

C’est une étape majeure dans la jeune carrière de Cristiano Ronaldo Júnior. Lundi 2 novembre 2026, la Fédération portugaise de football a officialisé la présence de l'attaquant de 16 ans dans la liste des U17 pour disputer les éliminatoires de l'Euro 2027.

Le sélectionneur portugais Filipe Ramos a retenu le fils de Cristiano Ronaldo dans une liste de 23 joueurs dévoilée le lundi 2 novembre 2026 par la FPF. Évoluant au sein des catégories de jeunes d'Al-Nassr en Arabie saoudite, le joueur polyvalent, capable d'évoluer en pointe comme sur les ailes, totalise 3 buts en 7 apparitions cette saison sous les couleurs du club saoudien. Une belle marque de confiance. Le fils aîné de Cristiano Ronaldo franchit ainsi un palier très attendu en intégrant pour la première fois cette catégorie d'âge.

Cette arrivée chez les moins de 17 ans vient récompenser un parcours déjà très abouti avec les équipes de jeunes de la Seleção. En effet, Cristiano Ronaldo Jr avait fêté ses grands débuts internationaux le 13 mai 2025 avec les U15, catégorie avec laquelle il s'était illustré en remportant le tournoi Vlatko Markovic grâce à un doublé en finale. Promu chez les U16 dès le 30 octobre 2025, il y a compilé 3 buts en 9 matches et remporté deux compétitions, jusqu'à sa dernière sortie le 24 mai 2026. Au total, son bilan s'élève à 13 sélections et 5 buts avec le Portugal.

Même si son avenir en sélection senior n'est pas encore définitivement scellé au regard des règles de la FIFA, Cristiano Ronaldo Jr confirme sa fidélité au maillot portugais. L'attaquant de 16 ans disposait pourtant de plusieurs opportunités sur la scène internationale, puisqu'il était potentiellement sélectionnable par quatre autres nations. Né en Californie, il pouvait prétendre défendre les couleurs des États-Unis, mais aussi de l'Espagne en raison d'une résidence de plus de trois ans, de l'Angleterre après le passage de son père à Manchester, ou encore du Cap-Vert grâce aux origines de sa grand-mère paternelle. Toutefois, le joueur poursuit son chemin sous la tunique portugaise.

Le stage de préparation débutera dès le 6 novembre 2026 au centre fédéral de la Cidade do Futebol, à Oeiras dans la banlieue de Lisbonne. Pour accéder au tour suivant des qualifications de l'Euro U17 2027, le Portugal devra terminer parmi les deux premiers du groupe 6 lors des trois matches prévus à domicile contre l'Andorre le 11 novembre, la Bulgarie le 14 novembre et la Serbie le 17 novembre 2026. Au-delà des U17, le regard se tourne aussi vers Cristiano Ronaldo senior (41 ans). Après avoir purgé une suspension de 30 jours et 255 euros d'amende suite à un désaccord avec Jorge Jesus, son retour est attendu selon la presse portugaise dans la liste de l'équipe A qui sera annoncée le vendredi 6 novembre 2026.

#2388. Jack Grealish has let his team-mates down: This self-inflicted episode shows he lacks the hard graft and humility so desired by David Moyes - and the team were better off without him, writes LEWIS STEELE

Published: 17:58 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 09:36 EDT, 30 October 2026

Hard graft, humility and fighting for team-mates: three qualities not shown by a certain Jack Grealish this week.

They are also a trio of traits demanded by the Premier League's most experienced boss, David Moyes, who banished the once £100million man Grealish to the naughty step for missing training without permission.

News of his latest act of ill-discipline dominated every conversation on the Merseyside waterfront before this full-blooded contest with Newcastle but Grealish was not missed a jot as his youthful and energetic replacements put on a show.

Goals from James Garner, Hayden Hackney and Thierno Barry were enough to send Moyes and Co to the Carabao Cup quarter-final and within sight of their first trophy since 1995, something the 63-year-old boss and these loyal fans crave above anything.

Moyes made the decision to drop and fine Grealish alongside chief executive Angus Kinnear. It is unknown if he will return for Monday's league game, also against Newcastle. The boss would not comment on the situation but said he supported the club decision to drop him.

'The one thing about Everton is that we have got really good values behind it,' he said. 'All the players stand up to the values and accept the values, on the pitch and off the pitch.

Jack Grealish let his Everton team-mates down, with the star suffering another setback

'From that point of view, I think the players did a brilliant job. It's a small squad we have got, we are limited in some areas but we are doing our best to keep challenging. You can see what it meant to the supporters, this is a big moment for them. There's humility about us tonight.'

Giant-slayers Fleetwood Town are up next. Given the way they toppled champions Arsenal on Tuesday, that will be no easy feat, but a trip to Highbury is all that stands between the Toffees and a first domestic cup semi-final since 2015-16.

Newcastle, meanwhile, look a pale imitation of the great team that beat Liverpool to win this competition in 2025 and the jury remains out on Matthias Jaissle. He lambasted his side's lack of maturity and said: 'It is shocking and it is frustrating as well.

'You need to be more mature and more clinical in these situations. Just clear it. It is a learning process but we don't have the time, we need to learn fast, especially with these young lads which is not an excuse any more.'

Fans around the country have tended to see the Carabao Cup as a chance to save some money in recent years and Everton supporters have grumbled at Moyes and former boss Sean Dyche for having a similar attitude with line-ups.

But a full house of 51,894 here – including 8,000 of the travelling Toon army – indicated that both teams were taking this seriously. Both mid-table with inconsistent form, this was a real chance for success.

Even the Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, knew that and was in attendance alongside his wife Marie-France. There was an obvious joke to be made around this week's budget, which has given a helping hand to those in need this winter.

Given the Grealish-shaped hole in Moyes's team and the obvious lack of numbers in multiple positions, the Everton top brass might have fancied getting in Burnham's ear to get the chancellor's phone number and ask for a leg-up too.

Hackney volleyed in his first goal for the club following his summer move from Middlesbrough

Thierno Barry added Everton's third in the second half to set-up a tie against Fleetwood Town

Matthias Jaissle's side will seek revenge when the sides meet again in the league on Monday

Prime Minister Andy Burnham was among those celebrating as Everton bid to end their trophy drought

Moyes has had to muddle through the season with a dearth of outfielders following a botched transfer window, but he has made the best of a tricky situation – one that was not helped by Grealish's actions.

Any frustration at those off-the-field issues was parked on the night, though, as Everton found themselves two ahead at half-time. It was a scoreline to leave Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle cursing after a string of missed chances.

EVERTON (4-2-3-1): Pickford 7; Rohl 6, Tarkowski 7, O'Brien 7, Mykolenko 7 (Maitland-Niles 86); Hackney 8, Garner 7; Dibling 7 (Johnson 77), Dewsbury-Hall 8 (Norgaard 86), George 8 (Alcaraz 77); Barry 7.

Subs not used: Travers, King, Keane, Armstrong, Graham.

Scorers: Garner 34, Hackney 45, Barry 69.

Booked: Hackney, Dewsbury-Hall, Mykolenko, Pickford, Tarkowski.

NEWCASTLE (4-2-3-1): Hornicek 5; Dedic 5, Schar 5, Burn 6, Hall 6; Gonzalez 5 (Steur 81), Ramsey 5 (Joelinton 46); Murphy 5 (Toure 67, 6), Willock 5, Barnes 7 (Elanga 46, 6); Osula 5 (Wissa 46, 6).

Subs not used: Pope, Botman, Bamba, Thiaw.

As it was, Everton weathered the storm thanks to Jordan Pickford and several last-ditch blocks.

Despite Newcastle's territorial advantages, the Toffees settled and were first to strike on 34 minutes. It came through Grealish's direct replacement for a starting berth, Tyrique George, winning possession and, via Hackney, feeding Garner to pass into the far corner.

Hackney soon turned from provider to goal-scorer, although referee Farai Hallam might claim an assist. Good officiating saw him play an advantage when Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall was hauled down when charging goalwards.

Barry picked up a loose ball and fed Hackney who volleyed home, making it look easy when he could have easily fired over the bar. Seconds earlier, Harvey Barnes had been denied by Pickford but Newcastle were undone by a motoring counter-attack.

Moyes would be delighted with the two goals but arguably more buoyed by the defensive rearguard that followed. Jaissle responded by throwing on three half-time changes in Yoane Wissa, Joelinton and Anthony Elanga.

None of them worked as Everton played with their hearts on their sleeves in a warrior-like defensive display that had this new stadium rocking like rarely before. James Tarkowski put his body on the line and Sunderland lad Pickford made several inspired stops.

Barry put the icing on the cake on 69 minutes when Garner robbed Amar Dedic of possession and Dewsbury-Hall teed up the No9 to finish with composure and help his team one giant step closer to ending that trophy drought.

No Grealish? No problem. The Manchester City loanee, who showed his admirable side earlier in the day when he gave £10,000 to help an ill fan, has let his team-mates down with this latest episode.

But with a collection of young talents thriving, mixed with some soldier-like experienced heads and a boss with an appetite for silverware, Everton do not need Grealish right now.

This night was one to forget for him and Jaissle's work-in-progress Newcastle, who are a shadow of the halcyon days of Eddie Howe's cup-winning side, despite pulling one back late on through captain Dan Burn's header.

Everton fans including Mr Burnham, meanwhile, will have March 21 and a potential final at Wembley circled in their diaries.

#2387. Conferenza Gattuso: "Sono contento di dare una gioia ai tifosi. Condizioni di Zaccagni?..."

Il mister Gennaro Gattuso ha rilasciato delle dichiarazioni in conferenza stampa al termine dell'incontro Lazio-Cagliari

Il mister Gennaro Gattuso ha rilasciato delle dichiarazioni in conferenza stampa al termine dell'incontro Lazio-Cagliari

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Oggi mi hanno sorpreso. Sinceramente, un punto me lo portavo a casa ed ero pure contento. Sono stati loro, la volevano vincere a tutti i costi. I cambi ci hanno dato energia, veemenza, voglia. Quattro giorni fa qui ha giocato la Roma contro il Cagliari,c he ha avuto quattro palle gol. Sapevo che avrebbero giocato così, non siamo stati bravi. Dovevamo fare meglio a destra, nel secondo tempo abbiamo fatto meglio e abbiamo sviluppato di più. Chi è entrato ci ha dato una grande mano. Se abbiamo vinto è merito dei ragazzi per la mentalità, la voglia, lo spirito. Hanno fatto di tutto per vincere. La classifica conta poco, mancano dodici punti all'obiettivo. Se non vincevi oggi, stavamo tutti là. Non si può sbagliare niente. Pensiamo partita dopo partita, andiamo alla ricerca di fare qualcosa di diverso. Ci sono squadre e allenatori molto preparati, ce l'hanno incaratata un po' e noi eravamo sulle gambe. Questa l'abbiamo pagata, ma siamo stati bravi a rimanere in partita e a fare un grande lavoro mentalmente. Taylor ha salvato due contrpiedi ribaltando l'azione per segnare, ce l'ho ancora negli occhi. Io ricordo sempre a tutti i ragazzi, che smanettano e leggono su internet, che il alvoro paga ed è giusto. Ho giocato tanto anche io, volevo essere sempre coerente e quando lo sei i compagni ti fanno diventare leader. Se oggi la gente è entrata in questo modo è perché lavora bene, quello che semini poi raccogli. Questo è quello che mi rende più orgoglioso ora, non la classifica. Sono giocatori che danno tutto per i loro compagni.

C'è grande rispetto per i giocatori, ma vogliamo fare determinate cose e ci può stare una giornata no. Mi sembrava giusto in quel momento mettere dentro forze fresche. Non facevamo male all'avversario, anzi arrivavamo poco sulle seconde palle. Belahyane oggi non ha fatto una grande partita ma ci sta, è giusto così. Cataldi poteva darci qualcosa in più. Nuno non ha fatto la sua miglior partita, Zac ha preso una botta, Provstgaard ha fatto fatica... Se prendo queste decisioni è perché ho giocatori vivi che mi danno la sicurezza di metterli in campo. In queste tre partite me la sono rischiata, ho fatto partire quasi sempre gli stessi. Ci sta pagare qualcosa. Io l'ho pensata così.

Io leggo poco, mi sono chiuso dentro Formello dal primo giorno. Quello che ho avvertito dal mio staff è che ci sono persone che i stanno dando la vita. Nel centro sportivo ci sono tanti veri laziali, una famiglia. È gente che esulta, che sta male quando le cose non vanno bene. Quando abbiamo perso col Mantova sembrava un funerale, feci una riunione con tutti dicendo che il morto si piange quando si deve piangere, che era successo qualcosa di grave ma che dovevamo continuare con lo stesso entusiasmo del ritiro. Dal primo giorno la squadra ha lavorato in una maniera incredibile, con grande senso di appartenza. Sembra che ci conoiscamo tutti da anni. Quello che succedeva fuori non sapevo nulla, sapevo che non ci potevano applaudire per la sconfitta in Coppa Italia. Io ho solo lavorato con i miei ragazzi provando a fare qualcosa di diverso, smontando quello che si è fatto l'anno scorso. I primi artefici di tutto quello che sta succedendo è solo merito dei giocatori.

Zaccagni ha preso una botta. Gli devo fare i complimenti, ha avuto un lutto ieri sera, il fratello di sua madre che era molto giovane e ha avuto un brutto male. Oggi non stava bene, era molto legato. Chapeau a lui, si  è messo a disposizione e ha giocato. Questo fa capire l'ambiente che si è creato. Ha preso una 'vecchietta' non dovrebbe essere un problema muscolare. Condoglianze a tutta la famiglia.

Quando vedi prima del Milan quello che hanno fatto i tifosi, prima del Parma, contro il Sassuolo allo stadio sembrava una festa scudetto, con dodici mila persone allo stadio. Anche oggi erano in 13mila, stanno aumentando. Per me è qualcosa di incredibile, chi viene allo stadio in questo momento è un eroe. A me piacciono queste cose, vivo per questa roba qua. Vivo la mia vita per avere il formicolìo allo stomaco, perché solo allora incido. Ho sempre vissuto così. Sono contento che stiamo dando una gioia a tutti quanti. Ho toccato con mano tre-quattro eventi incredibile, qui c'è grande passione e voglia. Il problema più grande è che sono coerenti, è difficile fargli cambiare idea. Noi dobbiamo solo continuare.

#2386. Stuttgart left frustrated in Istanbul as Batrakov double proves costly

A ferocious atmosphere greeted Stuttgart at RAMS Park, with Atakan Karazor picking up a yellow card inside the opening minute after catching Mario Lemina in midfield.

But, despite the hosts' early intensity, it would be the visitors who almost took the lead in the eighth minute. Chris Führich and Maximilian Mittelstädt combined well down the left to find Jamie Leweling, whose effort remarkably struck both posts before bouncing clear.

Galatasaray then made the visitors pay four minutes later, as Jeff Chabot's attempted clearance fell to Aleksey Batrakov just to the right of the penalty spot, before the Russian fired past Fabian Bredlow, who got a strong hand to the ball and should perhaps have done better.

Just three minutes later, Batrakov had his second, latching onto a pass from Davinson Sánchez before slipping the ball through Bredlow's legs to double Galatasaray's advantage.

Stuttgart's miserable opening continued when Karazor was forced off through injury, with youngster Yanik Spalt coming on in his place, before Galatasaray nearly added a third in the 22nd minute, with Bredlow denying Batrakov his hat-trick and Viktor Osimhen firing the rebound over the crossbar.

Tempers flared with around ten minutes remaining before the break, as Barış Alper Yılmaz sent Führich tumbling off the pitch, sparking a confrontation involving players and members of both coaching staffs.

Führich, heavily involved throughout the half, came close to pulling one back in the 42nd minute, curling an effort toward the far corner after cutting inside Roland Sallai, only for Uğurcan Çakır to get a slight touch and turn the ball narrowly wide.

In the second half, the intensity from the visitors increased, with Führich continuing to have a superb game down the left for VfB.

Seeking control again, Galatasaray turned to Rafa Leao for their own energy on their respective left flank, but it was Stuttgart who remained in the ascendancy.

The biggest moment yet for Die Schwaben came just after 75 minutes, when Deniz Undav rattled the bar from the middle of the box, before Führich found the net from range with a curling effort.

However, the Stuttgart hope would be short-lived, with referee Chris Kavanagh announcing that the goal had been ruled out for offside against skipper Undav.

Undav would remain at the heart of things for the visitors, sending Dženan Pejčinović through on goal in the 86th minute, before the summer signing failed to beat Çakır inside the box, as his wait for a goal outside of the DFB-Pokal goes on, rather summing up the frustrating evening for Stuttgart.

And after all of that, it ended 2-0 to Galatasaray, who had to hold on at times in the second half, but were more than worth the three points after such a threatening first-half performance.

Now, Stuttgart turn their attention to Saturday's clash with Bremen, while they have to wait until the end of the month for their next Champions League clash, when they travel to Inter Milan on 25 November.

#2384. Führich reflects on missed turning point in Galatasaray defeat

Stuttgart suffered their first defeat of their Champions League campaign in Istanbul, with Aleksey Batrakov scoring twice in the opening 15 minutes to secure a 2-0 win for Galatasaray.

VfB had made an encouraging start, with Jamie Leweling striking both posts with the same effort after just eight minutes.

The visitors then improved considerably after the interval, and thought they had found a route back into the contest when Chris Führich found the net from range, only for his effort to be ruled out for an offside against Deniz Undav.

Speaking to DAZN after the final whistle, the 28-year-old reflected on a frustrating evening in Istanbul.

“We invested a great deal. We started exactly as we had planned, with a huge chance for Jamie. If that goes in, it's obviously a completely different situation,” Führich explained.

"Then we conceded the first goal because we were a little too passive, and suddenly there's an energy here that you have to withstand.

"The second goal came straight afterwards, which was very bitter.

“We recovered quite well. I think we played a good game in the second half, with lots of chances and a few situations we could have played out better. But in the end, we were missing the goal.”

The German international was Stuttgart's best player on the night, and was particularly disappointed that his second-half strike was disallowed, believing that it could have provided Die Schwaben with a way back into the contest.

"It's a shame about the offside goal. I think that could have been another turning point, but it wasn't to be.

“We gave everything, put everything into the game, and I think we can still take a lot of positives away from here.”

#2383. The Bushtucker dressing room! 'Woke' football club to make players change in a sea of 60 HOUSEPLANTS 'to reduce stress' - after banning meat pies and making their kit vegan

Published: 11:42 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 11:44 EDT, 30 October 2026

Forest Green Rovers' changing room has undergone a dramatic transformation and been left looking more like an I'm A Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here! set.

The National League football club, renowned for their quirky and unconventional approach and often branded the world's most 'woke' team, have installed more than 60 plants in a bid to improve the players' mental health.

Environmentalist owner Dale Vince – who is worth around £100million – has had his club team up with Plants & Flowers Foundation Holland and a psychologist in a bid to help the squad relax in what can be a high-pressure environment.

Footage of the new-look changing room shows greenery everywhere, with the lockers themselves filled by vegetation.

While it may appear to be Rovers' latest wacky publicity stunt, the club insist there is science behind their re-design.

A statement on the carbon-neutral football club's website explained: '30% of Brits report that having living houseplants in a room noticeably lowers their stress levels and restores a sense of calm.

Forest Green Rovers have installed 60 plants in their changing room to reduce stress

The club are renowned for their environmental practices and quirky schemes

'Despite this, ‘plant paranoia’ is holding many back, with over a quarter of Brits (27%) put off by buying greenery because they are terrified the plants will die despite their best efforts.

'To prove that introducing greenery doesn't have to be a high-stress commitment, Plants & Flowers Foundation Holland is testing the theory in one of the most notoriously stressful indoor environments possible: an elite football changing room.'

The move coincides with International Stress Awareness Week ahead of their fixture against Harrogate and Dr Josephine Perry, a sports psychologist, said: 'Living greenery acts as a natural buffer, actively reducing nervous system arousal, which helps sharpen our cognitive abilities, allowing us to focus and perform better.

'Adding greenery to high-pressure spaces is one of the simplest, low-effort and accessible habits anyone can adopt to stay in control when the pressure mounts.'

Vince posted a video on X on Friday morning explaining: 'Up early this morning doing TV interviews. I'll show you what it's all about, it's in the changing room, all about plants. There's a little bit about Peterborough as well, the news that we have begun a legal process for the tapping up of our ex-manager Robbie Savage. That's the day so far, plants and what would you call it... hassle.'

He then moves into the newly decorated changing room and says: 'Here it is, chock full of plants. Quite chilling, really.'

Regarding the Savage lawsuit, Peterborough chairman Darragh MacAnthony previously denied that his side had made an illegal approach. Vince told Sky Sports on Friday: 'We're suing Peterborough and Robbie Savage for two million quid which was the buyout clause we were cheated out of and that process started last week.'

Controversial owner Vince, praised by some for his eco-focus and dismissed by others for what they perceive as 'woke' management, has found his club in the spotlight on numerous occasions for their unorthodox practices.

Their kits are made from recycled, sustainable materials and are officially certified as vegan.

The food in the canteen is completely vegan, with players also provided with vegan meals to take with them to away matches. Meat is completely off the menu and everything provided to players, fans and staff is plant based.

The players are seen in their new environment, with plants in each locker space

Rovers' pitch is maintained without chemical pesticides, herbicides, or synthetic fertilizers and cut using solar-powered mowers.

There's even a urine filtration system from the away toilets that is used to irrigate and water the turf.

There are also plans to build a new stadium made of timber with the lowest carbon footprint of any ground in world football. The club also promote cycling to matches and have electric charging points at the ground.

Vince, an eco tycoon who made his money in renewable energy, came under fire earlier this year after the club often branded the world's 'wokeist' made the decision to scrap their women's team, hardly the most progressive move.

The Gloucestershire-based outfit are spending their third consecutive season in the fifth tier, having failed to achieve promotion back to League Two at the first time of asking.

The club reached a record high of League One in 2022 but suffered consecutive relegations, ending their seven-year stint in the English Football League in 2024.

Vince has chosen not to directly replace Savage, who left on October 2, instead opting for a three-man coaching team from existing staff.

#2381. PREMIER LEAGUE LIVE: Xabi Alonso on Estevao's future with Chelsea, Roberto De Zerbi confirms James Maddison IS available for Tottenham - and Andoni Iraola on why Liverpool fans can dream

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER and JACK GAUGHAN and MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER and LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER

Published: 11:16 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 12:04 EDT, 30 October 2026

It's another action-packed Premier League weekend ahead and the managers have been having their say. Follow the best of it here with Daily Mail Sport...

Xabi Alonso insists there are zero talks being held inside Chelsea about allowing Estevao to leave in January on loan for game time, despite the Brazilian wonderkid struggling for chances to impress.

The 19-year-old stayed sat on the bench during Chelsea’s Carabao Cup shootout-loss to Liverpool on Wednesday. In the Premier League, he has been a late substitute six times, and unused twice. It has seen questions asked of Alonso’s plan for a highly-promising talent.

There is no shortage of rivals who would be willing to take Estevao temporarily. As revealed by Daily Mail Sport this week, multiple clubs at home and abroad are watching his situation.

Before Manchester United visit Stamford Bridge for Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off, Alonso was asked if they would consider finding him a temporary home in this winter window.

‘No, no, no,’ Alonso said. ‘No discussions about that. The season is long and there will be moments for everyone. It's a process for the team, for Este, for myself, but I'm sure that in the season, he will have his games, his minutes. We are still early in the season, but he will be there.

Xabi Alonso insists Chelsea are not discussing sending Estevao out on loan in January

‘It's not about attitude. It's been about the context of games, it's been about the start of the season, and he's a great guy. We are still in October and he will be important.’

Chelsea fans feel as if they have heard this before, and then watched as he failed to come on as a substitute in their Carabao Cup trip to Liverpool. The Blues signed Estevao from Palmeiras for £29million rising to £55m, and he is tied down to a deal lasting into the 2030s.

He had some magic moments in his first season, including scoring a stoppage-time winner against Liverpool in the Premier League and upstaging Lamine Yamal of Barcelona in the Champions League. His lack of opportunities this term has come as a surprise to supporters, who sang his name at Anfield, and led to speculation in Brazil that the youngster is frustrated.

‘It is no secret that all players want to be on the pitch,’ Alonso added. ‘When any of them haven't had enough minutes because of my decision, I have to take the responsibility for that, that they are not as happy as they could be. But everyone has to be ready because in any game, they could be important, they could be part of the team, and Este, his training and his attitude has been good.

‘We are back in Premier League mode, and that is, for me, the main competition for us this year, and it's a big one. It's one that we didn't have that much time to prepare, but it's really important after the last home game that we had (a 2-0 loss to Tottenham).’

Meanwhile, Maxence Lacroix has a hamstring injury which will sideline him for several weeks. Moises Caicedo and Pep Chavarria are fit to face United, but Jorrel Hato is injured. Goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez may return sooner than expected – perhaps even before the international break – as Alonso said: ‘In case he's ready to play, he will need a face mask probably.’

Enzo Maresca has shrugged off Fabian Hurzeler’s thirst for revenge and the suggestion that Manchester City were lucky to beat Brighton in midweek as the managers face off for the second time in four days.

City progressed to the Carabao Cup quarter finals via penalties on Wednesday night, with the Brighton boss insistent that they had created more than enough to knock out the holders.

Maresca’s side are looking to open up an eight-point gap with the Seagulls, who are flying high in third. Hurzeler has confessed to being a ‘bad loser’ but has moved on from Wednesday night.

‘Revenge is more about him [Hurzeler] and not about us,’ the Italian said. ‘This is what he said. Every manager can say something different.

Enzo Maresca does not feel that his side were merely lucky to beat Brighton in midweek

‘It depends on what you see with your eyes. But I respect what he said. Probably the reason why it's so difficult to play against them is because they are always front foot, aggressive and their attack is also very good.’

Instead of returning to the south coast between fixtures, Brighton have remained in Manchester through the week and trained locally on Friday.

Maresca added: ‘If you see the Premier League games they have played, they scored three, four, five goals against any team. That's why I was so happy after Wednesday.

‘It's because yes, they scored two goals, they had some more chances. We also created chances. But we knew that it was a difficult test for us. We dealt quite well.’

Meanwhile, Maresca has claimed that no City star has a guaranteed place in his team despite revealing that shootout hero deputy Geronimo Rulli is not rivalling Gianluigi Donnarumma for the No 1 spot.

‘I think one thing is to say that in this moment Gigio is plus 10 others,’ he said. ‘And another thing is to say undroppable. Yes, there are two different things. There is no player who is undroppable. But in this moment it is Gigio plus 10. In this moment I see it like this.’

Tottenham playmaker James Maddison is available for Saturday’s visit of Crystal Palace despite an injury scare during the victory at Chelsea.

Maddison sparked more fitness fears when he limped off in the 51st minute of Spurs’ 2-0 victory at Chelsea.

After Maddison had endured a slow start to the campaign with caution preached over his fitness following a May return from anterior cruciate ligament damage, his substitution last Saturday looked to be another setback.

But, ahead of the Palace game, Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi said: 'James is available. This week he didn’t work like the other players, but for tomorrow he is available and he is a special player for us. A special player because of the character and he has unique characteristics.

James Maddison is available for Tottenham despite an injury scare suffered against Chelsea

'For James Maddison or the players who are coming from a long injury, they have to work more than the other players, but he has already four or five weeks he is working very hard and consistently.'

'So, I think it’s not a problem if he loses two days (training), but then we have to analyse if we take risk or not.

'If we take risk like Pedro Porro (against Aston Villa) or (Dejan) Kulusevski.

'We are lucky to have a big squad and it’s important to not take risk with new injuries.'

Andoni Iraola is happy for Liverpool fans to start dreaming of a Premier League title challenge ahead of Sunday’s clash with champions Arsenal, but insisted it is too early for him to start looking at the table.

Victory at Anfield would see Liverpool move to within three points of the Gunners as they look to continue a five-match winning run in all competitions, but Iraola said his focus remains on improvements in performances early in his reign.

'It is still October,' Iraola said. 'We have to take one game at a time and I always say the reference is more or less when we’ve played against each other once so halfway through the season. That’s when you can start to look at the standings.

'Right now, we are in a position where we need to improve and keep getting better.'

Liverpool supporters are able to dream of winning the Premier League - but Andoni Iraola isn't getting ahead of himself

But when asked if he welcomed the growing optimism amongst Liverpool supporters, Iraola added: 'For fans, it is good if they have expectations or they think we can win.'

Arsenal moved level with Manchester City at the top of the table last weekend with a 2-0 win over Everton, but were then on the wrong end of a huge cup upset in midweek, dumped out of the Carabao Cup when they were beaten on penalties by League Two Fleetwood.

'We know Arsenal and how good they are,' Iraola said. 'They have very good players, working a lot in synchronicity and we have to be ready for that challenge.

'It’s going to be a demanding game but we also trust our players, trust ourselves and in the good atmosphere we will for sure have on Sunday. I hope we will be at level to win this game.'

#2380. Hoeneß left with mixed emotions after frustrating Galatasaray defeat

Stuttgart suffered their first defeat of the Champions League campaign on Tuesday evening, with two goals from Aleksey Batrakov inside the opening 15 minutes proving decisive in a 2-0 victory for Turkish champions Galatasaray.

However, the visitors were left wondering what might have been, having created plenty of chances throughout the contest.

Jamie Leweling remarkably struck both posts with the same effort before Galatasaray took the lead, while Deniz Undav also hit the woodwork after the interval, and Chris Führich eventually found the net, only for his effort to be ruled out for offside.

Speaking to DAZN after the final whistle, boss Sebastian Hoeneß struggled to hide his frustration at the manner of the defeat.

"I think we had a good chance to take the lead, a very good chance," he explained.

"We'd already had one or two really good breakthroughs down the wing before that. We got into the final third, we looked dangerous. I had the feeling that the game was just starting to swing our way.

"And then, in exactly that phase, looking back, you have to say that's where we lost the game. We conceded two goals.

Despite the early setback, Stuttgart did continue to threaten, particularly during a much-improved second-half performance.

Hoeneß was full of praise for his players' response as a result, but he admitted their failure to find a breakthrough remained difficult to accept.

"In the second half, I can only take my hat off to the performance the boys showed. They left everything out on the pitch.

“It would have been very interesting to see what would have happened if we'd scored a goal, and there were enough opportunities.”

"It's starting to add up a little. Dženan [Pejčinović] had another chance, Tiago Tomas had another chance. There were other really good opportunities as well.

"But of course, there were also those three or four minutes when we conceded the goals. From my point of view, they were Galatasaray's first shots on goal. I don't think Fabi [Bredlow] had anything to save before that. Both went in, and then it becomes incredibly difficult."

Nevertheless, Hoeneß was determined to recognise the efforts of his squad on their travels to Istanbul.

"I'm proud of the boys for the performance they showed, for the way they delivered what they'd set out to do in this atmosphere.

"On the other hand, when you look at how the game went, it's also very, very frustrating that we've lost."

Stuttgart remain on seven points from their opening four Champions League fixtures, having previously made an encouraging start to the league phase.

#2378. Hearts' Riccarton Three - 20 years on: The dressing-room rebellion that pulled back the curtain on the madness of Vladimir Romanov's Tynecastle reign and altered the club's trajectory for generations to come

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 13:23 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 13:51 EDT, 30 October 2026

Only those individuals who’d been living in a cave for a year or so would have believed that all was well in Hearts’ world when they recorded a storied triumph over Hibs at Hampden 20 years ago.

A thumping four-nil win in the Scottish Cup semi-final on April 2, 2006, came courtesy of Paul Hartley’s hat-trick with Edgaras Jankauskas also getting in on the act.

As if there wasn’t enough for the maroon hordes to gloat about that afternoon, Ivan Sproule and Gary Smith were sent off for Tony Mowbray’s team.

With lower-league Gretna awaiting Hearts in the final, it should have felt like the good times were rolling. And, to an extent, they were.

The following month, the Gorgie men would beat Aberdeen to wrap up second place in the top flight and earn a place in the Champions League qualifiers.

With Gretna beaten on penalties ten days later, an open-top bus wove its way through the streets of the capital with the old trophy being shown off.

Paul Hartley, Steven Pressley and Craig Gordon hit out at the club's ownership in October 2006

Only six months earlier, Hearts had thumped rivals Hibs in the Scottish Cup semi-final

But the jubilant scenes were a distortion of the real picture. Vladimir Romanov, the Russian-Lithuanian business leader, had bought into the club in February 2005, becoming the majority shareholder eight months later.

He promised lavish investment to establish Hearts not only as the dominant club in Scotland, but as a European force to be reckoned with. Many supporters wearing Cossack hats lapped it up and were disinclined to look beyond the bluff and the bluster — or examine the price tag.

Those with a stronger grasp of the situation saw Romanov for what he was: An erratic egomaniac who’d be ruinous for the club in the longer term. The only question was how quickly it would take for it all to come crashing down.

It hardly required inside knowledge to appreciate that his eccentricities were going to test the patience of Hearts supporters from the get-go.

Despite the side sitting on top of the league after winning their first eight games of the 2005-06 season, Romanov sacked manager George Burley with chief executive Phil Anderton also fired.

Graham Rix, a convicted sex offender, was hired as Burley’s replacement before Valdas Ivanauskas was brought in on an interim basis in March 2006.

The former FBK Kaunas coach was given the full-time gig after winning the cup only to be put on sick leave with stress at the start of the following season.

Ivanauskas’ temporary replacement, Eduard Malofeev, the sporting director, barely spoke a word of English.

The preposterous turnover of managers was just the tip of the iceberg, though.

Rumours abounded that Romanov was in charge of team selection and would often fax in his line-up before kick-off — a matter Rix subsequently confirmed as being true. Players who were fit were routinely shunted to the sidelines for no reason.

At the owner’s behest, a mysterious woman from Eastern Europe joined the physio department. Brandishing a divination stick, she claimed to be able to identify injuries before they happened.

Accustomed to training in mornings throughout their careers, players were told to report for work in evenings — with no explanation. One recalled a session in the dark winding down with a wheelbarrow race.

For many, the final straw arrived when Romanov started to deliver his own motivational team talks.

It may have had the veneer of a professional football club, but it was a circus.

‘The place was an absolute shambles,’ said defender and future Hearts manager Robbie Neilson.

Behind the scenes, the senior players spoke privately about their deepening concerns and contemplated going public with them.

After weeks of procrastinating, they agreed that doing nothing was no longer an option. And so, on October 27, 2006 — just six months after that routing of Hibs — ‘The Riccarton Three’ were born.

Vladimir Romanov promised  Hearts fans that the club would dominate Scottish football

Hearts had lost at home to Kilmarnock the previous Saturday and were scheduled to play Dunfermline at Tynecastle the following day.

The press pack which descended on the training ground inside Heriot-Watt University was larger than normal on that cold morning for a reason. They’d been tipped off that something remarkable would unfold. ‘Bring your popcorn,’ wrote a message from one of the squad.

With Malofeev elsewhere in the building and the rest of the squad sitting in a dressing room, at 12.02pm the doors to the seminar room opened and the show began.

In walked Hartley and Craig Gordon, stony-faced. Between them, beanie hat on his head and holding a piece of paper, was captain Steven Pressley.

By the time the trio took their place at a table filled with microphones, it was clear that the next few minutes were going to blow the doors off the club. This was a dressing room revolution.

‘It was the crossing of the Rubicon,’ said Neilson. ‘As soon as you did that there was no way back.’

Despite knowing that he was unleashing a verbal grenade, Pressley delivered the words with complete calmness.

‘Chaps, just to make you aware that I’m going to make a statement and we’ll answer no questions,’ he said.

‘This is a statement on behalf of a number of the players.

‘I have tried along with the coaching staff and certain colleagues to implement the correct values and disciplines, but it has become an impossible task.

‘There is only so much a coaching staff, a captain, and certain colleagues can do without the full backing, direction, and coherence of the manager and those running the football club.

‘While, publicly, I have expressed the need for unity behind the scenes, I have made my concerns abundantly clear.

‘The last two years have been very testing for the players. Together, we have faced a number of challenges and worked hard at retaining some degree of unity.

George Burley was sacked by Romanov despite winning his first eight top-flight fixtures

‘However, due to the circumstances, morale, understandably, is not good and there is significant unrest within the dressing room.’

Pressley didn’t mention Romanov by name but he didn’t have to. Hartley and Gordon remained silent throughout the address.

And with that, they rose and left, the hush in the room in sharp contrast with the chatter of a normal post-match conference.

Although even the most experienced journalists present were stunned at what they’d witnessed, they knew this much: Nothing would ever be the same again.

Predictably, the fallout was nuclear. Seething with what he saw on Sky Sports bulletins elsewhere in the building, Romanov addressed the entire squad and told them they’d be sold if they didn’t beat Dunfermline. The game ended 1-1.

The three actually started the match. Malofeev gave a strange post-match interview where he angrily insisted there were no problems at the club and the players could say what they liked because it was a ‘democracy’.

A short time later, the actions of Romanov would prove this was not the case.

Pressley was dropped for the game against Falkirk on November 13, was an unused substitute against Rangers on November 19, was then stripped of the captaincy and left the club on December 9 ahead of a January switch to Celtic.

Bizarrely, on the day he was told he’d no future at Hearts, he was offered the assistant manager’s job.

‘I was probably seen as the figurehead of the club at the time,’ he later said. ‘Everybody leaned on me to try and get things done, or get answers within the club.

‘The treatment of some individuals was horrendous. The honesty, the transparency, all the things that I think are really important in the foundations of a club — they were being disregarded.’

Hartley was a substitute against Falkirk and also moved to Parkhead in the January for £1.1million.

Gordon, the most valuable asset, was dropped for away games with Dundee United and Rangers, but remained at the club until he joined Sunderland for £9m in the summer.

As for Malofeev? Hearts didn’t win a game under him. He stayed in charge until Ivanauskas resumed his duties in late November.

With Hearts knocked out of the Scottish Cup by Dunfermline in the New Year, a game in which Gordon was a substitute, Ivanauskas then made way for Anatoliy Korobochka, the latest director of football to be promoted to head coach.

Despite an upturn in results, Aberdeen claimed third place ahead of the Tynecastle side. So much for winning the title.

While the Riccarton Three were never going to topple Romanov purely by speaking out against him, their actions ensured he was never viewed in the same light again by supporters.

Eduard Malofeev failed to win a single match during his short spell in the Tynecastle dugout

When Stephen Frail was made manager in January 2008, he was able to demand that he would have full responsibility for team selection.

By the following year, Romanov had ceded the day-to-day running to Campbell Ogilvie. His visits to Tynecastle became increasingly less frequent.

No doubt, this had much to do with what he knew was coming down the track.

Although Hearts did defeat Hibs 5-1 in the 2012 Scottish Cup Final, the recklessness of the Romanov years was catching up with the club.

The following year, the collapse of his Lithuania-based Ukio Bankas triggered Hearts calling in the administrators who uncovered debts of £15m. A 15-point deduction and relegation followed.

Were it not for the mobilisation of the Foundation of Hearts and the largesse of Ann Budge, one of Scotland’s great sporting institutions would have gone under.

From the rubble, the club was rebuilt. With Tony Bloom involved these days, there’s an authenticity to the current talk of Hearts winning major honours, perhaps even the title one day.

As their supporters prepare to march on Hampden again tomorrow to face Hibs, the part of all of those who stood on the right side of history won’t be forgotten.

#2376. Emergenza Napoli, un azzurro espulso con la Juventus: salta la sfida contro la Lazio

Un calciatore del Napoli ha rimediato un cartellino rosso nel corso della gara contro la Juventus e dovrà saltare l'incontro con la Lazio

La sfida dell'Allianz Stadium contro la Juventus si è rivelata subito complicata per il Napoli, sceso in campo con una formazione dettata dall'emergenza. Tra i tanti infortuni e problemi fisici che hanno ridotto la rosa, il mister Massimiliano Allegri è stato costretto a ridisegnare il reparto arretrato lanciando dal primo minuto la coppia centrale formata da Marín e Marianucci.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

La partita del difensore azzurro si è purtroppo chiusa prima dello scadere dei 90 minuti a causa di un cartellino rosso. Già ammonito nel corso del primo tempo per un intervento falloso, infatti, Marianucci ha rimediato un secondo giallo al 75° minuto della ripresa a causa di uno step-on-foot. Un'espulsione inevitabile per il direttore di gara che ha lasciato il Napoli in inferiorità numerica proprio nel momento più delicato del match, subito dopo la rete dello svantaggio firmata da Alajbegović.

Oltre al danno immediato sul campo di Torino, il rosso rimediato costa caro a Marianucci anche in vista del prossimo turno di campionato. Un'assenza pesante che obbliga lo staff tecnico a correre nuovamente ai ripari, costringendo il tecnico a studiare nuove soluzioni d'emergenza.

#2375. Demirovic addresses Galatasaray links after Champions League defeat

Ermedin Demirovic has insisted that his only focus was on three points as Stuttgart faced Galatasaray.

The Bosnian international was heavily linked with a move to the Turkish champions over the summer before ultimately deciding to stay in Stuttgart.

He then came up against his former suitors at RAMS Park on Tuesday evening, but was unable to prevent a first defeat of the Champions League campaign, with Aleksey Batrakov scoring twice in a 2-0 win for Galatasaray.

Speaking to DAZN after the final whistle, the 28-year-old was asked whether he had viewed the occasion as an opportunity to make another impression on the Lions.

"I didn't really see it as an opportunity to present myself here," said the striker.

"I wanted to play a good game for VfB, I wanted to win the match. I would have loved to score a goal and help the team in that way.

"That's why I didn't think about it all, about presenting myself here.

“Of course, there was contact, and I have a lot of respect for the club, but nevertheless, I wanted to win this game.”

Demirovic also admitted that he had never experienced an atmosphere quite like the one inside RAMS Park, with VfB subjected to relentless noise throughout the evening.

"It was a very special game in general. It was my first time playing in Turkey, and the atmosphere was really something I'd never experienced before. That kind of noise, that kind of support.

“Nevertheless, it was a Champions League game that we wanted to win, that our team wanted to win. Unfortunately, it didn't work out in the end, but we'll keep going.”

#2372. Cup semi-final triumph over rivals Hearts would be the ideal moment to pick up first win as Hibs boss, admits Marink Reedijk

By ANTHONY BROWN, PRESS ASSOCIATION SPORT

Published: 14:00 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 14:01 EDT, 30 October 2026

Marink Reedijk is relishing a “special match” as he aims to belatedly ignite his Hibernian reign with victory over high-flying city rivals Hearts in Sunday’s Premier Sports Cup semi-final.

After three defeats and a draw in his first four matches in charge of the Hibs, the Dutchman goes into his first Edinburgh derby eyeing a first win since succeeding David Gray in September.

Hearts, third in the Premiership, have won all four previous meetings between the two Capital clubs at Hampden, including the 2012 Scottish Cup final, and Reedijk has been made well aware of the importance of the derby during his five weeks in Edinburgh.

“It’s a special match in several ways,” said Reedijk, who revealed that experienced striker Martin Boyle will return after illness.

“This is the type of match you look forward to because it’s not only the derby, it’s also a semi-final, and it’s one step away from a final, so that is a double way of excitement.

“You don’t need to ask anyone here about the derby because they will tell you, and this is also the beautiful thing about it. And we have someone in our staff (former Hibs player Guillaume Beuzelin) who experienced a few, and therefore, of course, he told us about it and he prepared us for what we can expect.”

Marink Reedijk is hoping to pick up his first win as Hibernian boss in the Premier Sports Cup

Hibs celebrate opening the scoring at St Mirren in midweek but had to settle for a 1-1 draw

After the joy of leading Beveren to an unbeaten title triumph in the Belgian second tier last season, Reedijk has found himself struggling for results during a testing start to his Hibs tenure.

“It is interesting because everybody recognises last year with Beveren, but in the beginning at Beveren, we had the same sort of spells,” he said.

“The only thing which is different is that I had a start where we had a pre-season, and you could already put some things in place (in friendlies), and here I started immediately with competitive matches.

“But I have been in these situations as well with Beveren, and we focused on the things we did, and trusted the way we did it, and focused on not only the results.

“I know the results are important, but if the result is not there, is the performance there? And if the performance is there, then it’s a matter of time.

“The performances are getting better and better and better, and therefore, like in Beveren, I think if you keep on progressing, the results will come.”

Reedijk will come up against one of his Beveren ‘Invincibles’ from last season in goalkeeper Beau Reus, who joined Hearts in the summer.

“It’s a special connection,” said the Hibs boss. “We will always be linked – not only him and me, but the whole team. Together for the rest of our lives, because of the performance of last year.

“However, since Wednesday evening, I don’t feel this at the moment. It will be after Sunday night that this feeling comes back again, because I want to win the match. He is someone who will always be part of my journey.”

#2369. Domani ti svegli e sei Scaroni. Richiameresti Maldini? Albertini risponde: "Sì! Poi non so se Paolo accetterebbe"

La frattura tra il Milan attuale e Paolo Maldini è sempre, inevitabilmente, motivo di discussione nel mondo rossonero. Durante un'intervista al Corriere dello Sport a Demetrio Albertini viene fatta una domanda decisamente particolare a riguardo:

Se domattina ti alzassi e fossi Paolo Scaroni, lo richiameresti Maldini?

“Io Maldini lo richiamerei, poi non so se Paolo accetterebbe. Però io lo chiamerei. Paolo fuori dal calcio e fuori dal Milan… Non mi piace vederlo a casa. Può dare tanto. Poi dopo non so, le scelte le deve fare lui”.

Invece, se fossi Paolo Maldini a che condizioni torneresti al Milan?

“Non lo so. Io e Paolo non abbiamo lavorato insieme nel post carriera. Quando eravamo collaborativi all’interno della squadra, Capitano e vice capitano, comunque siamo stati tanti anni in nazionale e quindi so che lavori ha e che professionista è. Per quanto riguarda il fuori campo le condizioni non le conosco. Su questo non ho mai avuto la fortuna di lavorare con lui”.

Il contrattualizzare l’avere carta bianca lo puoi prevedere in futuro oppure non ti appartiene?

“Non mi appartiene perché oggettivamente le dinamiche di una squadra, di una società, di una proprietà e di un’azienda le conosco. Alla fine si parla anche di quello. E quindi oggettivamente una mediazione la devi trovare. Però, come ho detto, è un qualcosa che ti dà l’esperienza di poter lavorare in un gruppo”.

#2368. Heidenheim legend Frank Schmidt announces shock departure

Heidenheim have confirmed that Frank Schmidt's remarkable spell as head coach will come to an end next summer.

The 52-year-old has decided against extending his contract beyond June 2027, bringing an end to one of the longest managerial reigns in German football.

In a club announcement, it was confirmed that Schmidt informed Heidenheim CEO Holger Sanwald of his decision during a personal meeting on Monday, despite the club's efforts to convince him to stay.

Explaining his decision, Schmidt said he had been considering his future for several weeks and wanted to give Heidenheim sufficient time to plan for his successor.

"After almost 20 years as head coach of FCH, I simply want to take a break," Schmidt explained in a statement released by the club.

The German coach insisted he had made no plans for what comes next, with his immediate focus remaining on the rest of the campaign.

He added that he was determined to give everything until the final game of the season, insisting that Heidenheim's "last chapter is not over yet."

Schmidt took charge of his hometown club in September 2007, initially on an interim basis, when Heidenheim were playing in the fifth tier of German football.

What followed was a remarkable rise through the divisions, culminating in promotion to the Bundesliga for the first time in 2023.

Under Schmidt, Heidenheim went on to qualify for European football in their debut Bundesliga campaign, competing in the UEFA Conference League the following season.

Although their three-year stay in the top flight ended with relegation earlier this calendar year, Schmidt remained in charge for a 20th consecutive season.

Sanwald described the decision as "a turning point for our entire club" and admitted that Heidenheim's remarkable progress would not have been possible without Schmidt.

The Heidenheim CEO also confirmed that the club would now begin its search for a successor, having unsuccessfully attempted to persuade Schmidt to extend his stay.

The Swabian side currently sit sixth in the 2. Bundesliga, although they have gone five competitive matches without a victory following Saturday's 2-1 defeat in Baden against Karlsruhe.

Schmidt's side return to action against Hannover on Sunday, with 24 league matches remaining before one of German football's most extraordinary managerial partnerships comes to an end.

#2365. Disturbi alimentari, il libro di Perinetti ispira ddl per rafforzare Percorso Lilla

(ANSA) - ROMA, 03 NOV - Una proposta di disegno di legge per "rafforzare il Percorso Lilla attraverso una maggiore formazione degli operatori sanitari. La proposta interviene su accoglienza, identificazione precoce dei disturbi dell'alimentazione e sulla continuità terapeutica". Lo ha annunciato il senatore Filippo Melchiorre, durante la presentazione del libro "Quello che non ho visto arrivare" di Giorgio Perinetti, direttore sportivo di lungo corso, dedicato a sua figlia Emanuela, scomparsa il 29 novembre 2023 a 34 anni per una forma acuta di anoressia, che si è tenuta nella Sala "Caduti di Nassirya" in Senato. "Una legge da sola non può risolvere un problema così complesso, serve parlarne senza pregiudizio dobbiamo fare in modo che la prevenzione e la presa in carico diventino obiettivo concreti", prosegue Melchiorre.

Una proposta di legge che punta, quindi, ad aiutare le famiglie che si trovano in situazioni come quella vissuta da Perinetti con il direttore sportivo che ha sottolineato come "questo rappresenta il punto più alto raggiunto. Non potevo fare nulla per costringere mia figlia a curarsi perché non avevo gli strumenti. Non c'è una normativa che possa impedire a una ragazza ricoverata di firmare per uscire dalla clinica. Spero si possa pensare a qualcosa che possa aiutare altre come mia figlia a farcela". Presente anche Marcello Gemmato, Sottosegretario di Stato alla Salute, che ha concluso ammettendo come "il tema è fare in modo che tutte le strutture del sistema sanitario pubblico possano diagnosticare in tempi rapidi la patologia per minimizzarne gli effetti". (ANSA).

#2364. Under-fire Dons boss Stephen Robinson isn't seeking any assurances from club chiefs over his job

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 13:48 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 14:02 EDT, 30 October 2026

Aberdeen boss Stephen Robinson insists he has not sought any assurances over his position from chairman Dave Cormack despite a woeful run of form.

A 1-0 home defeat to Falkirk on Wednesday night left the Dons slumped in ninth position in the Premiership table with just one win in their last five matches.

A section of the Pittodrie crowd turned on Robinson and his players and booed them off the pitch after another insipid display.

Heading into today’s Premier Sports Cup semi-final clash with Rangers at Hampden, there have been some suggestions that Robinson’s position could be under serious threat.

Whilst accepting the criticism from fans, the under-fire boss insisted it has been business as usual in terms of his conversations with Cormack and new chief executive Adrian Bevington.

‘No, I’m not seeking any assurances,’ said Robinson. ‘I have just had my normal conversations.

Under-fire Dons boss Robinson is not seeking assurances from club hierarchy over his job

‘I speak to the chairman once a week and I speak to Adrian once a week. That’s no different than any other week.

‘So, no, there’s been nothing different. We know the results over the last couple of weeks haven’t been good enough.

‘No one is getting away from that fact and ultimately we deserve the criticism we got. I deserve the criticism, I don’t hide behind that. And I don’t try to throw players under the bus.

‘The players know it needs to be better and they are all in that together. There are no factions, there are no people going off on their own, everyone wants to turn that around.

‘I know given time, this can be very successful. But I also live in the real world. You need to get results that give yourself longevity.

‘Certainly, everybody wants time, but you don’t get given time in football. We’re all well aware of that and results are what dictates that. And what a place to start at Hampden.’

Ahead of this evening’s clash at Hampden, Robinson believes it will be the perfect opportunity for Aberdeen to turn their season around if they can beat Rangers.

Robinson was typically animated during a match that saw his team lose 1-0 to Falkirk

He also claimed that all of the pressure will be on Rangers, given the expectation on them to beat an Aberdeen side who have toiled for much of the season.

‘You haven’t got time to feel sorry for yourself, if there is a moment to put it right a semi final at Hampden is that time,’ he added.

‘As a footballer you always get another chance, sometimes as a manager you don’t and what a chance it is to go to Hampden, a full house with a big support with us. It is certainly the right place to do it and we believe we can.

‘Every semi-final that I’ve been in with Motherwell and St Mirren, we were not expected to win. So I know how to motivate teams and the staff know how to get teams to believe.

‘It’s certainly an opportunity. All the pressure will be on Rangers, and the expectation will be on Rangers.’

Earlier this week, Rangers boss Derek McInnes, who spent eight years with the Dons, backed Robinson to succeed at Pittodrie if he is given time to turn it around.

‘Until you are in this position, you don’t realise how difficult things are and the parameters you have to work under, Derek obviously does,’ added Robinson.

‘I have nothing but total respect for him. He is one of the top managers in the country. Everybody wants time but you don’t get given time in football, we are all well aware of that and results are what dictates that.

‘We face a really good Rangers side. Derek’s built a really good squad, a really big, athletic, strong squad. We are coming up against a team that are in form, a team that are winning football matches.

‘We know that we have to be better than what we are. I’ve been to semi-finals before and I’ve always been the underdog. No doubt that would be exactly the same, rightly. It’s up to us to turn that around.’

Robinson's under-performing Dons team are languishing ninth in Premiership table

On team news, Robinson added: ‘We’ve got a problem at the back, of course, that’s been well documented, with Lewis Mayo, Mats Knoester and Dan Happe. Dan is suspended, but he’s actually ill as well, so he’s got the virus.

‘Kristers Tobers has had a little bit of a setback. There’s a little bit of swelling on his knee, so he won’t be available for selection tomorrow. Chris Cadden won’t be available tomorrow either.

‘We haven’t had to seek our troubles, but again, as I always say, somebody’s misfortune is somebody else’s opportunity.

‘It’s a chance for people who maybe haven’t had opportunities, or people who haven’t been fit, to stand up and be counted. As I said, there’s no better stage than Hampden to do that.

‘It’s a mild hamstring injury (Cadden’s injury). We’re hoping he could be fit for the Hibs game, but at this early stage, it’s still very hard to say. We just know he won’t be available with the quick turnaround for Saturday.’

#2362. Karl and Laimer on target as Bayern Munich cruise past Atlético Madrid

Looking to get back to winning ways in Europe after drawing 1-1 with Stuttgart last time out, Atlético Madrid made a lively start as Bayern visited the Metropolitano, with talisman Julian Alvarez curling an effort narrowly wide of Manuel Neuer's far post inside three minutes.

Bayern then quickly took control, but despite enjoying over 70 per cent of the ball in the opening 20 minutes, they failed to register a shot, while Atléti midfielder Pablo Barrios saw a deflected effort fly just over.

Lennart Karl threatened midway through the half, firing over from the edge of the box, while Kane put an effort just wide following a delivery from Konrad Laimer.

On the half-hour mark, the hosts should have taken the lead, with Alexander Sørloth handed a chance he will not want to see again, with the Norwegian unable to sort his feet out following a ball to the back stick from Marc Pubill.

And after both sides failed to manage a shot on target before the break, Joshua Kimmich finally tested Jan Oblak shortly after the restart, before Karl broke the deadlock in the 54th minute.

Robin Le Normand appeared to have the ball under control near the penalty spot after blocking an effort from Tom Bischof, but the youngster then stole possession from behind the Spanish defender and fired the visitors into the lead.

Koke, Ademola Lookman and Lee Kang-in would come on for the hosts five minutes later, and Los Colchoneros began to find their feet after the changes, with Marcos Llorente forcing Neuer into his first save of the evening in the 67th minute.

Goalscorer Karl was replaced by Nathaniel Brown shortly afterwards, before Kane went close to doubling Bayern's advantage, only for the flag to be raised after the England captain lifted an effort narrowly over after rounding the onrushing Oblak.

Bayern would double their lead in the 74th minute, when Laimer hammered in off the crossbar from a tight angle following a beautifully clipped ball from Kane.

In the ascendancy and carrying a two-goal lead, the record German champions were well on track to pick up their first Champions League win since the opening week triumph against Bodø/Glimt.

Bayern did think they had a third in the 82nd minute, when Dayot Upamecano headed home from a corner, before the effort was ruled out for a foul, and left-back Brown then had a chance to extend the lead, only to be denied by Oblak on the angle.

Seeing out the win, Bayern take three points back to Munich with them and turn their European form back around after successive draws, while attention now turns to Saturday's trip to Mainz.

#2358. Guys like Makhanya and Sterling should feel welcome to speak the truth more often if Rangers are to finally throw off their serial losers tag

Published: 14:15 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 15:19 EDT, 30 October 2026

Olwethu Makhanya is shaping up to be everything Rangers needed in their search for defensive reinforcements in the summer.

A solid presence at the back, a young and hungry talent very much on the up and a leader with real personality.

If it didn’t look so likely that someone will come in before long and offer the Ibrox board the chance to make a healthy profit on the £3million they paid to Philadelphia Union for the 22-year-old, you’d put him down as a nailed-on future captain.

He’s helping set the standards required if Rangers are to overhaul arch-rivals Celtic in the title race and was absolutely spot-on after rescuing an ill-deserved point with a late equaliser at Tynecastle on Wednesday when bemoaning a lack of character at the start of the second half and the fact Hearts worked harder and showed more desire.

It’s the kind of honesty many Ibrox sides of recent years have needed. A public kick up the backside for underperforming team-mates, the footballing equivalent of getting the whip out and a necessary form of assurance for frustrated supporters that there is at least someone inside the dressing room who feels the way they feel, who wants what they want.

It’s why it is to be hoped that manager Derek McInnes’ remarks the morning after were not some attempt to gently slap down the South African.

Defender Olwethu Makhanya questioned the character of this Rangers squad midweek

McInnes, of course, is entitled to his own opinion about the reserves of character within his squad. Maybe he did disagree with Makhanya’s version of events, or his questioning of the side’s resilience.

Alternative viewpoints delivered respectfully are fine. More than fine. They are a sign of a healthy workplace.

It just felt like it was all skirting a little too close to a chastisement of the big centre-back’s comments.

And whether that was the intention or not, being seen to chastise a player whose sentiments are clearly coming from the right place, from a burning desire to make a club with one league crown in 15 years be successful again, is not necessarily the right course of action to take.

It happened, if you remember, with Dujon Sterling back in Philippe Clement’s first season as boss when an April collapse that involved a home draw with Celtic, a 3-2 loss at Ross County and a stalemate at Dundee pretty much killed off hopes of lifting the title.

‘We owe ourselves a performance… because we have been s**t the past three games,’ said Sterling in the aftermath at Dens Park. ‘We are fighting for a title and the way we are playing, it is as if we are not playing for anything. It’s like the season is dead and it is a dead-rubber game.’

It felt like a cry from the heart, a desperate plea to those around him to breathe life into a dying campaign. It was a truth that had to be told.

Clement, meanwhile, was already well on the way to losing the plot at that point, claiming his side were ‘moral winners’ after snatching that draw with Celtic thanks to a late goal and insisting that he was happy his side ‘bossed it’ at Dens.

Criticising Sterling afterwards just made him look even more like he didn’t get it, had lost all sight of what being at Rangers — or any club that has to win at all costs — was about.

‘It’s the words of a player who is disappointed because we lost points and maybe lacks a bit of experience in that way,’ stated the Belgian waffler. ‘That’s things for young players to learn and become better in. It’s more talking out of frustration.’

Manager Derek McInnes disagreed with Makhanya's comments following the Hearts game

That’s the standard response from football persons, of course. The whole business, for some time, has revolved around young players having it battered into them that it’s better to say nothing, to drone on dead-eyed through interviews, bat everything away, put their personality on the bonfire, ‘don’t get too up or too down’.

It’s nonsense, though. McInnes honed his trade in a Nine-In-A-Row Rangers dressing room full of huge characters who built unbreakable bonds while still being able to dig each other out, demand more, be confrontational.

Sure, it happened more behind doors than in the public gaze, but things are different now from the way they were 30 years ago. Social media has changed the landscape so drastically. Fan narratives do drive boardroom decisions and that has arguably been clearer at Ibrox in recent times than anywhere.

There’s a concern still living just under the surface among a large number of Rangers fans that there is an ingrained loser mentality at their club and plenty of evidence to back that up.

Admittedly, the playing staff has changed drastically since then, but it is impossible to forget Billy Dodds reflecting on his time as a first-team coach for interim boss Barry Ferguson and talking about how 70 per cent of signings had been wrong and that the dressing room had a number of weak characters who couldn’t handle adversity.

Even before Danny Rohl left for Red Bull Salzburg last season, he talked about players being ‘too lazy to recover’ in key moments. He also spoke about how some of the squad were ‘very quiet’ when he first took over.

Supporters of Rangers, treated to some amount of failure and in-house claptrap over the last decade or more, need to see evidence that those on the field care the way they do.

The kind of frank analysis delivered by Makhanya — in a calm and considered way, it should be said — need not be the negative so many inside football are programmed to think.

If anything, seeing guys wear their hearts on their sleeve can serve to strengthen the relationship between fans and their favourites in difficult times.

The modern-day audience have had enough of failing players promising to learn lessons and move on. At outfits judged on league titles and facing pressure to win every week, learning lessons is the last thing on the agenda. You really ought to know what needs done by that stage.

Rangers have drawn two of their last three and currently trail leaders Celtic by four points

Punters want to see the real people behind the branding, measure their minerals. And we’re on about more than just those cringeworthy features on club TV where players quiz each other on whether they prefer Jaffa Cakes or KitKats while playing a game of ping-pong. It’s showing a bit of what’s really inside, being properly authentic, that resonates.

In fairness to McInnes, his messaging as Rangers boss has generally been good so far. He didn’t shy away from the paucity of those performances in losing in Europe to Jagiellonia Bialystok and Jablonec.

He hasn’t indulged in deflection. He confronted the speculation that was already beginning to swirl about his future after that Jablonec catastrophe, handled it well and steered the side to safer ground with two excellent back-to-back wins against Celtic.

He has been honest and upfront and entirely understanding of the expectations that rest upon his shoulders.

His team is still guilty of switching off in games. Centre-back Manny Fernandez, although the manager must back him publicly, is the epitome of that.

His players still have to show they can be consistent enough to prevail against a Celtic side that is most definitely there for the taking. They need to keep the pedal to the metal and to deliver 90-minute performances or, at least, maintain control throughout.

It is a squad light on trophies on the CV and with a number of younger players. It is going to need regular reminders as this race plays out.

If Makhanya or Sterling or anyone else want to take it upon themselves to put those reminders out there, it shouldn’t be regarded as a bad thing. And it definitely shouldn’t be discouraged.
