#2355. Lazio, tre punti sulla seconda: in Europa solo l’Arsenal tiene il passo

I Gunners precedono il Manchester City; negli altri tre campionati citati il distacco dalla seconda è di due punti.

La Lazio ha tre punti di vantaggio sulla seconda in classifica: nessuna capolista dei cinque maggiori campionati europei presenta un margine superiore. L’unica squadra che eguaglia i biancocelesti è l’Arsenal, anch’esso avanti di tre punti rispetto alla propria inseguitrice. Negli altri campionati presi in esame, il distacco tra prima e seconda è di due punti.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Il dato riguarda il vantaggio della squadra al primo posto su quella immediatamente alle sue spalle. Sotto questo aspetto la Lazio condivide il margine più ampio tra le capoliste considerate: i suoi tre punti di vantaggio trovano un solo equivalente, quello dell’Arsenal. Barcellona, PSG e Dortmund guidano invece le rispettive classifiche con un punto di margine in meno rispetto ai biancocelesti.

Il riferimento è alle prime due posizioni nei cinque maggiori campionati europei. Per la Lazio il confronto mette quindi insieme il suo distacco sulla seconda e quelli registrati in Spagna, Francia, Germania e Inghilterra. Il primato dei biancocelesti è richiamato anche in un contenuto dedicato a Reja, che dichiara: «Vedere la Lazio prima mi riempie di gioia. Non deve porsi limiti».

In Spagna, secondo quanto riportato da Sportmediaset.mediaset.it,  il Barcellona è a più due sull’Atletico Madrid. La formazione che occupa la prima posizione precede dunque la seconda con un vantaggio inferiore di un punto a quello della Lazio. Il confronto tra le due capoliste mostra margini diversi: tre punti per i biancocelesti, due per il Barcellona.

La stessa distanza si registra in Francia, dove il PSG conserva due punti sul Lille. Anche in Bundesliga il Dortmund precede il Friburgo di due punti. Barcellona, PSG e Dortmund hanno così il medesimo vantaggio sulle rispettive inseguitrici, mentre la Lazio dispone di un punto in più di margine sulla seconda. Il quadro dei distacchi nei tre campionati è quindi uniforme: ciascuna delle loro capoliste è avanti di due punti.

#2353. Laimer praises Bayern's belief after Atlético win and makes bold Karl prediction

Bayern Munich secured an impressive victory in the Spanish capital on Tuesday evening, with second-half goals from Lennart Karl and Konrad Laimer earning the Bavarians all three points.

Speaking to Amazon Prime after the match, Laimer was delighted with Bayern's performance, particularly given the questions surrounding the squad in recent weeks.

"We went into the game knowing what we're capable of. There has been a lot written about us and everything surrounding the team, but we have big confidence in our squad and the players we have," the Austrian said.

"I think we showed that over the full 90 minutes today: the way we can play football and the way we want to play.

"Ultimately, I think we could even have scored a few more goals. It was a thoroughly deserved win against a good team."

Laimer also reserved special praise for 18-year-old Lennart Karl, who opened the scoring in the 54th minute after winning possession inside the Atléti penalty area.

"I'm really happy for the boy. He stays calm, he wants to improve, he works hard and today he was rewarded for it.

"He showed that real fighting spirit. He tracks back, wins the ball back and then somehow manages to smash it into the net.

"He's young and still has a lot to learn. He still needs to take another step forward, but he's on a fantastic path. I'm absolutely delighted for him, and I think he has a great career ahead of him."

Laimer then discussed his stunner in the second half, which came after an excellent pass from Harry Kane, revealing that his teammates had joked about how long he took to shoot.

"The boys asked me, 'Why did you take so long to shoot?' I thought I'd take a bit more time this time before doing something too quickly, as I sometimes do, only for it not to come off properly.

"Ultimately, Harry played an outstanding pass. I controlled it, looked up to see if there was anything else I could do, and then simply finished it with a clean, composed strike.

"Sometimes you can tell as soon as the ball leaves your foot whether it's going to be a good one or not. And I immediately thought, 'Oh, yes, that feels really good!'"

After getting back to winning ways in Europe, Bayern now turn their attention to Saturday's trip to Mainz, where they will be looking to go into the international break with three points under their belt.

#2349. Champions League, stasera Feyenoord-Inter: ecco tutte le curiosità sulla partita del de Kuip

Champions League, stasera Feyenoord-Inter: ecco tutte le curiosità sulla partita del de Kuip

Installa la nostra App gratuita e accedi più velocemente alle notizie

Mentre navighi nell'app, scorri il dito da sinistra a destra dello schermo per tornare alle pagine precedenti

Si avvicina una nuova tappa del cammino europeo dell'Inter: i nerazzurri saranno impegnati a Rotterdam contro il Feyenoord martedì 3 novembre alle ore 21:00. La sfida tra la squadra di Chivu e quella di van Bronckhorst, valida per la quarta giornata di League Phase della Champions League 2026/27, vedrà affrontarsi due squadre appaiate nella classifica generale a quota 3 punti dopo tre partite giocate. L'Inter, dopo le due sconfitte contro Real Madrid e Club Brugge, ha battuto lo Shakhtar a San Siro grazie alla rete di Carlos Augusto, mentre gli olandesi hanno perso nelle due trasferte disputate a Barcellona (5-1) e a Siviglia contro il Betis (1-0), trovando la vittoria al "De Kuip" contro il Como, sconfitto 3-2.

Una sfida che in Champions League è già andata in scena nella fase a eliminazione diretta della stagione 2024/25, con i nerazzurri che hanno avuto la meglio centrando la qualificazione ai quarti, e che ha vissuto incroci anche in Coppa Uefa e in amichevole. Quello contro il Feyenoord sarà il 23° confronto dell'Inter contro una squadra olandese in competizioni ufficiali: il bilancio conta 12 vittorie nerazzurre, 5 pareggi e 5 sconfitte. In attesa della sfida del "De Kuip", ecco precedenti, curiosità e intrecci tra Inter e Feyenoord.

Sette vittorie e quattro pareggi in undici giornate di campionato, primo posto in classifica a quota 25 punti, con 33 gol segnati e 12 subiti. Il Feyenoord ha iniziato la stagione in modo decisamente positivo in Eredivisie, ma è reduce da due pareggi nelle ultime due uscite in campionato: dopo l'1-1 in casa del PSV Eindhoven è arrivato quello interno contro il Fortuna Sittard, con il gol del pari ospite arrivato a cinque minuti dalla fine. Diverso il rendimento in Champions League, dove gli uomini di Van Bronckhorst hanno raccolto tre punti in tre partite, frutto dei k.o. esterni con Barcellona e Betis e il successo casalingo contro il Como. Nel match contro la squadra di Fabregas, giocato davanti al proprio pubblico, gli olandesi sono stati trascinati dalle giocate di Moussa e di Zechiel. Il primo, ala destra veloce e abile nell'uno contro uno, ama convergere sul sinistro e cercare la conclusione: proprio con un'azione del genere ha innescato il terzo gol del Feyenoord, con il suo mancino deviato che è entrato in porta dopo l'ultimo tocco di Sanchez. Il secondo, invece, è un centrocampista dinamico dagli ottimi tempi di inserimento, qualità nello stretto e capacità balistica: abilità che ha messo in mostra in occasione della rete del pari contro il Como, girandosi in un fazzoletto e concludendo dal limite dell'area.

#2346. Neuer makes Champions League final admission after Bayern's Atlético triumph

Bayern Munich captain Manuel Neuer was full of praise for his side after their 2-0 victory over Atlético Madrid, with goals from Lennart Karl and Konrad Laimer securing all three points in the Spanish capital.

The 40-year-old returned between the posts after missing Bayern's previous three matches through injury, while assistant coach Aaron Danks took charge in the absence of Vincent Kompany.

Speaking to Amazon Prime after the final whistle, Neuer felt Bayern had been in complete control despite their recent injury problems.

"I'd say it was total dominance from the first minute to the 93rd. Whatever Atlético threw at us, we always had an answer.

"And we're incredibly happy, especially considering the circumstances and the fact that we've had to make some adjustments due to injuries and everything that's happened at FC Bayern in recent days.

"But I think we stuck together, gave everything we had, and made sure we could enjoy a team performance like this today. It was exceptional."

The Bayern captain also acknowledged that not everyone had expected such a convincing performance against Diego Simeone's side, particularly away from home.

"We always stick together, stand united and have an answer to everything. I think there were probably some people who doubted whether we could go away to a good team and get a result today, especially given how difficult it is to win here.

"Atlético are also just two points behind Barça in the league. So not everyone necessarily expected this. To deliver a performance like that and respond to those doubts is sensational."

Atléti's Metropolitano will also host the Champions League final on 5 June 2027, potentially offering Neuer the opportunity to finish his career on Europe's biggest stage if Bayern were to make the final at the end of the season.

Asked whether the stadium would be a fitting venue to play his final match should he decide to retire at the end of the season, Neuer responded: "Yes, absolutely. And perhaps winning here now is also a good omen.

"Of course, it's a tough, challenging road for all of us, for all the teams who are usually favourites and contenders to make it to the final here.

"We believe we can do it. We have what it takes, and we'll give everything to make it happen."

#2345. Giordano: “Abbiamo preso un gol da polli, ma la reazione è stata forte”

Bruno Giordano esalta il carattere della Lazio, il trascinatore Isaksen e i cambi.

La Lazio si gode il primato in classifica e Bruno Giordano intervenuto ai microfoni di Radiosei, analizza questo momento d'oro biancoceleste. Secondo l'ex bomber, la squadra sa vincere e soffrire grazie alla crescita della personalità  di Isaksen. Nonostante la stanchezza e i problemi tattici, la maturità mentale e i cambi azzeccati di Gattuso fanno la differenza.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Vittoria meritata. Non si può pretendere di giocare sempre come a Torino o a Reggio Emilia. La partita si era messa male, abbiamo preso un gol da polli, ma la reazione è stata forte; la squadra si è aggrappata ad Isaksen, che in questo momento sta trascinando il gruppo. Squadra un po' stanca che appunto si è aggrappata a lui, va sfruttato il suo momento. Il risultato assume anche più valore in questi casi, quando non tutto va al 100%.  Isaksen sta crescendo anche in personalità. Sotto l'aspetto del gioco non mi meraviglia, lo abbiamo visto in Europa contro di noi, i suoi colpi li ha. Ora sta prendendo sicurezza, i compagni lo cercano e questo lui lo avverte e gli dà tranquillità. Il gol di ieri è difficile e bellissimo, lui spesso li fa belli; mi ricordo poche reti sue brutte. Il modo di giocare e la fiducia del tecnico stanno facendo la differenza. Ho sempre detto che non sapeva gestire i 90', faceva mezz'ora bene poi calava, ora invece arriva alla fine come se fosse il 70' e questo è un valore aggiunto.

Taylor è un giocatore dinamico, tecnico, completo. L'uscita di Fadera è stata un bene per noi, ci stava mettendo in difficoltà; è stato un vantaggio che abbiamo saputo sfruttare.  Serve la maturità per capire che non tutte le partite posso andare allo stesso modo, c'è stata pazienza ieri e non è facile perché a volte ti puoi innervosire. La Lazio mi ha dato l'impressione che sta maturando anche sotto questo suo aspetto, ha la consapevolezza che anche se va in svantaggio può poi vincere.  I cambi della Lazio? Si vedeva che alcuni calciatori, soprattutto quelli sostituiti, erano stanchi. L'allenatore deve fare delle scelte e mettere a disposizione i migliori del momento. Tavares era un po' affaticato rispetto alle gare precedenti, Frattesi giocava troppo vicino ai difensori centrali del Cagliari e così mancava qualcosa in mezzo al campo. Ci può stare, rientra tutto nella logica delle cose.

#2340. 'We're not in Disneyland!': Mikel Arteta fires warning at Arsenal wonderboy Max Dowman, 16, after red card - and says it's not his first offence... as he admits Fleetwood loss left him 'p***ed off'

Published: 10:24 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 15:26 EDT, 30 October 2026

Mikel Arteta has told 16-year-old Max Dowman 'we are not in Disneyland' as he insists his age does not give him a free pass following his red card against Fleetwood.

Dowman was sent off in the 86th minute of Arsenal's shock Carabao Cup defeat by Fleetwood on Tuesday after kicking out in retaliation to a challenge by Harrison Neal.

It was the second time he has been sent off this this month, having also seen red while representing England's Under-19s.

After the club's appeal was rejected by the FA, Dowman will now miss Arsenal's Premier League matches against Liverpool, Hull City and Newcastle.

As the teenager left the field, manager Mikel Arteta gave him a scathing look and uttered a few words to the attacker, understood to be: 'Get to the changing room, Max.'

And on Friday he suggested Dowman should have kept his cool under provocation.

Arsenal star Max Dowman (second from right) looks shocked after the referee shows him a red card at Fleetwood Town

Manager Mikel Arteta has words with the distraught youngster as he leaves the field

Arteta said: ‘I haven't seen the reaction to my reaction. But you have to understand the context, the relationship that I have with him and what we discussed just before we went out.

‘You want to always have the best reaction, the beautiful one. But do you want to see the reaction of his team-mates when they have to play with the 10 men, you want to see that? What do you expect?

‘I don't know. Or the England (Under 16) ones, they are his age, 16, the same. What is their reaction?

‘Whether it’s right or wrong, that's the reaction. And the reaction when I don't win, you know what is? I’m p***** off big time.

‘We have to be ready for that, this is the environment and this is the reality. Otherwise we are in Disneyland. We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League at this level.

‘We look after him so much that you cannot imagine, and at the same time we are going to be demanding that anybody continues to earn the right to play. Otherwise what are the rest of the boys going to tell me? It needs to be fair, that's all.’

He further explained that his touchline reaction was borne out of frustration having told Dowman to not react to such a scenario before the game.

‘I thought we discussed that before the game,’ the Spaniard said. ‘It was related to what could happen. Not only the red, but the 10 seconds before, the way he (Dowman) comes to receive the ball, what kind of ball that is, and after that if he gets tackled, what happens next. Exactly that.’

Arteta revealed he had spoken with Dowman about the incident. 'I had a talk with him yesterday,' he said. 'No issue at all. I've done it, so I try to prevent that.

'That's why I'm so protective of these things, and especially with young players, because we have made those mistakes. And you know how much you can get punished and how much it can change what happens next.'

On the FA’s decision to reject the Gunners’ red card appeal, he said: ‘Very disappointed, to be fair. Especially with the reckless tackles that he received, and then his reaction is minimal in relation to the action.

‘(We’re) disappointed that it's not been overturned after looking at the action back.

‘We have put every argument on the table to make a case for it. Not only the action, but when you look back at it in slow motion, the previous action and Max's action, it's clear that obviously we have a very different opinion.

‘And on top of that, I think you have to read the context of the player, the age.’

The severity of the challenge is also an issue for Arteta. ‘It could have been really bad, yeah,’ he said. ‘And we are lucky today that he hasn't had a broken foot. That's clear.’

#2339. Pioli: “Ci sono stati momenti in cui mi hanno chiamato tutti. Anche la Roma”

L’ex allenatore della Fiorentina racconta del motivo per cui andò ad allenare l’Al Nassr e di quando fu chiamato dalla Roma e dalla Nazionale

Stefano Pioli ex allenatore biancoceleste ha legato una delle pagine più esaltanti della sua carriera proprio alla panchina della Lazio, condotta nel 2014-2015 a uno straordinario terzo posto e a una finale di Coppa Italia persa contro la Juve. L’apice della sua carriera il tecnico lo  ha raggiunto con lo storico scudetto vinto alla guida del Milan nel 2022. Il tecnico è stato  intervistato per Sky Sport, raccontando di quando fu vicino alla Roma e alla Nazionale.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Ci sono stati momenti in cui mi hanno chiamato tutti. Anche la Roma, ma mi era appena arrivato il contratto dell’Al Nassr, ma non mi sono pentito di andare in Arabia. Volevo un’esperienza fuori. Hanno inciso l’aspetto economico e la possibilità di allenare Cristiano Ronaldo. Anche la panchina della Nazionale l’ho sfiorata e non da moltissimo.

Nell’estate del 2025 Pioli torna a Firenze dopo esserci stato sia da allenatore tra 1989-95 che da allenatore tra il 2017-19. Purtroppo per il tecnico la sua seconda esperienza nella Fiorentina si è rivelata estremamente negativa: nelle prime 10 partite di campionato la squadra non ha mai vinto, raccogliendo appena 4 pareggi, subendo 6 sconfitte e totalizzando solo 4 punti. Un avvio da record negativo che ha portato inevitabilmente all'esonero il 4 novembre 2025.

#2333. O'Neill hits out at critics as Celtic boss issues surprising response to McGregor's midweek comments

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 15:03 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 15:30 EDT, 30 October 2026

Celtic manager Martin O’Neill has claimed some of the club’s critics are only seeking to cause division within the camp.

On the back of a 2-2 draw with Dundee United earlier this week, Celtic skipper Callum McGregor claimed they are playing like a basketball team who lack control in matches.

McGregor also appeared to question the fact that Celtic started the match effectively with three strikers across the frontline in Kasper Hogh, Camilo Duran and Callum Osmand.

‘It’s not really having a nailed-on profile for each of the positions,’ said McGregor. ‘The players behave like a winger, or they behave like a striker.

‘You can get away with it for a few games but if it’s a striker playing as a winger, you are going to get that behaviour a lot of the time.

‘You’ve got enough quality so you can score goals and get away with it. But we have to try to get the team functioning the way it should.

O'Neill is satisfied with Celtic's start to the season despite criticism over performances

‘Then that will alleviate all the other problems that we are encountering, where it becomes a bit like basketball, you lose control and spend the next 15 minutes trying to get possession back.’

At half-time in the game against United at Parkhead, O’Neill took Hogh off and reverted to a more traditional system with Jota and Haissem Hassan coming on as wingers to replace the misfiring Dane and Osmand.

Celtic eventually fought back to claim a point, but McGregor’s comments became the subject of much scrutiny.

It is not the first time a senior player has spoken out this season, with Cameron Carter-Vickers claiming that Celtic’s style of play was ‘random’ after the Old Firm defeats to Rangers.

O’Neill insists he actually agrees with McGregor’s comments — but has vowed to find a solution at the top end of the pitch.

The veteran boss also appeared to snipe back at some of the critics who have claimed that there is unrest among the squad.

‘I’ve said this to you before, I totally agree that Osmand is actually really a centre-forward,’ said O’Neill when asked about McGregor’s verdict.

‘I’ve said it at the press conference, that he is essentially a centre-forward who probably would play off somebody strong alongside him.

‘I'm not so sure that he could lead the line on his own. And that Duran is really a centre-forward.

‘So the players are getting to know each other. It’s really as simple as that. So I’m in total agreement with Callum. We’ll sort it out.

The manager admits that the likes of Camilo Duran are currently being played out of position

‘We seem to be doing okay domestically, trying to sort it out.

‘There’s a few players that haven’t had a chance. [Jordan] Lotomba hasn’t had a chance yet to play. There’ll be moments, absolutely.

‘Young [Joel] Van Den Berg has trained today. So over the course of the next number of weeks, between now and Christmas, I think everybody will be on the field of play.

‘And then it’s a matter of establishing right positions as much as possible.

‘Players have played out of position before. I don’t know whether it was a big issue when young Osmand came on in the Benfica game and set us alight.

‘I come in here [to the press conference] every single week and I’m most of the time pretty buoyed by things.

‘Don’t try and throw a lot of divides in. At the end of the day, we’re doing fine.

‘A lot of lads here didn’t even do pre-season with us. A number of players came in quite late on, so it will take time for us.

‘So we need to hang in there, and at this minute I think we’re hanging in.’

With Rangers playing Aberdeen in the semi-finals of the Premier Sports Cup, Celtic travel to Falkirk tomorrow knowing that a victory would send them seven points clear of their Old Firm rivals.

O'Neill added: ‘I think we’ve done fine, we’re leading the league with a four-point gap at this minute, which is nothing at all at this stage of the season.

‘We fought back and retrieved those kind of leads on a couple of occasions last season.

‘We’ll try and get a result or two in European football which would be nice, but domestically we’ve been fine.

‘Falkirk had a bit of a stodgy start, but they are flying now, so we know it’ll be a difficult game for us.’

#2329. Pastore: "Inter non ha fuoriclasse. Lautaro e Calhanoglu grandi giocatori, ma manca il campione"

Pastore: "Inter non ha fuoriclasse. Lautaro e Calhanoglu grandi giocatori, ma manca il campione"

Installa la nostra App gratuita e accedi più velocemente alle notizie

Mentre navighi nell'app, scorri il dito da sinistra a destra dello schermo per tornare alle pagine precedenti

Scegli Fcinter1908.it come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui

Il giornalista Giuseppe Pastore, durante Fontana di Trevi, ha parlato dell'atteggiamento dell'Inter e della rosa nerazzurra

Non stiamo evocando che volino gli stracci, anzi per me l'Inter aveva inconsciamente bisogno di uno schiaffone e lo ha preso. Feyenoord-Inter e Inter-Como saranno partite molto decisive per capire se l'Inter ha davvero cambiato questo chip. Chivu mi pare che non stia riuscendo a farsi capire. Ci sta provando in tutti i modi, ma i giocatori, qualche giocatore, anche Thuram lo ha detto oggi. Sappiamo di aver sbagliato. Però il sapere di aver sbagliato non porta a correggere l'atteggiamento. E questo è il problema.

Bisognerebbe parlare dei problemi, degli errori di Chivu. Secondo me molti giocatori dell'Inter e anche un po' l'allenatore, l'allenatore sa di non essere ancora un grande allenatore. Perché Chivu come curriculum in questo momento non vale neanche a Amorim oltre ai suoi colleghi in Champions League. È un allenatore che sta facendo un percorso. E quindi ci sta che sbagli e sbaglierà.

Penso che molti giocatori dell'Inter attuale debbano dirsi continuamente a se stessi: io non sono un grande giocatore, anche se lo sono, perché l'Inter non ha fuoriclasse secondo me. Ne ha uno che ha però 38 anni che è Mkhitaryan, che lo è stato ma chiaramente la carta d'identità gli gioca un po' contro. Ha alcuni grandi giocatori che sono Lautaro, Calhanoglu, ha tanti ottimi giocatori ma non il campione, il fuoriclasse che ha un rendimento costante in 50 partite su 50 non ce l'ha.

Siccome molti dei giocatori lì, alcuni giocatori dell'Inter secondo me questa cosa ogni tanto hanno bisogno di sentirsela dire, è bene che se la dicano proprio perché l'atteggiamento del basso profilo che non è soltanto una posa ma è qualcosa che il grande giocatore ha dentro di sé. Non voglio citare altri nomi di giocatori che hanno fatto di questo profilo uno stile di vita, un simbolo.

Per me l'Inter rimane la favorita per il campionato, per lo scudetto. Una squadra che può ancora arrivare nei primi otto in Champions. Però è una settimana chiave nella gestione. Perdere col Bruges ha fatto male al gruppo, ma la soluzione per me non è arretrare. Non è tenere uno più indietro, non è smettere, archiviare quell'atteggiamento molto coraggioso che ha mostrato nelle giornate. Perché l'Inter se arretra non lo sa fare molto bene, lo ha dimostrato nei primi dieci minuti del derby. È inutile. E anche contro il Bruges perché toglie anche entusiasmo, toglie anche un po' di coraggio alla squadra e al modo di giocare. Fossi in Chivu troverei il modo di tornare alle prime sei, sette partite stagionali accettando quei rischi ma dando alla squadra quel coraggio e quell'entusiasmo che sembrano aver un po' perso nelle ultime giornate.

#2328. Rambaudi: "Per me non cambia l’obiettivo, ma hai vinto bene una partita non facile..."

"Questo entusiasmo ti deve far crescere ancora di più nella mentalità..."

Intervenuto ai microfoni di Radio Sei, Rambaudi ha commentato la partita della Lazio contro il Cagliari.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Primo posto in solitaria? Per me non cambia l’obiettivo, ma hai vinto bene una partita non facile. Hai preso punti sulle inseguitrici, ti sei allontanato ancora dal settimo posto. L’hai letta bene, ad un certo punto poi queste gare devi sperare di non perderle, anche se stai dominando. Le squadre avversarie è normale che debbano mettere una pezza sulla sinistra ma la Lazio non è solo quello e la dimostrazione è il gol di Isaksen. Secondo me ieri è mancato, a parte il ritmo, l’apporto di giocatori importantissimi; se mi bloccano a sinistra, in mezzo o a destra devono lasciare qualcosa, e lì sono un po’ mancati Belahyane e Frattesi. Questo entusiasmo ti deve far crescere ancora di più nella mentalità, tolto questo la Lazio sta facendo cose straordinarie.

Isaksen mi è sempre piaciuto tanto, ho sempre detto che ha grandi qualità ma è timido, poco coraggioso. Sostengo da tempo che, trovando la chiave giusta, sarebbe diventato un grande giocatore e ora stiamo vedendo questo.

#2321. Andre Silva: "Mi è piaciuto giocare in Serie A, ho bei ricordi"

Andre Silva, attuale attaccante del Porto, domani sera ritroverà un avversario affrontato due volte nella breve e deludente esperienza al Milan in Serie A: il Napoli. Il centravanti portoghese, nella conferenza stampa di vigilia ha voluto raccontare e ricordare gli anni in Italia:

"Il mio passato in Italia? La Serie A è molto particolare rispetto a quella portoghese, è un po’ avanti. Mi è piaciuto molto giocare in Italia. Ci sono squadre che fanno gruppo e che giocano tutte insieme con tanta tattica. In Portogallo c’è un po’ di tutto, ma c’è molta differenza anche tra le squadre più forti. lo ero al Milan, ma la Juve era troppo forte, ora le cose sono cambiate un po’ ed ogni anno c’è una squadra nuova che sorprende. La Serie A mi è piaciuta tanto, ma adesso sono in Portogallo e c’è ancora tanto da fare. Rispetto agli anni scorsi il livello è più alto e più squadre sono più forti”.

In rossonero, Andre Silva ha collezionato 40 presenze ufficiali condite da 10 reti e due assist. Decisamente meglio e più positivo lo score e rendimento al Francoforte in Bundesliga: 71 presenze, 45 reti e 15 assist.

#2320. Bruno Fernandes has 'TARNISHED' his Man United legacy after his public criticism of Michael Carrick - and peace talks might be 'papering over the cracks', warns Alan Shearer

Published: 15:30 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 15:47 EDT, 30 October 2026

Alan Shearer has claimed that Bruno Fernandes has 'tarnished' his Manchester United legacy following his fallout with Michael Carrick over the last couple of weeks.

The Red Devils captain raised eyebrows when he questioned his manager's tactics after their side's 4-1 defeat by Como in the Champions League, and was subsequently left out of the team for their later loss against Bournemouth.

He spoke out just a matter of days after Lisandro Martinez had questioned United's activity behind the scenes, and left his United future in doubt.

That's according to all-time Premier League leading scorer Shearer, who claimed Fernandes' previous success is now marred.

'Fernandes is going to have to go out and perform, which he hasn't done for large parts this season,' Shearer told Betfair. 'I know he's been Man United’s go-to player for a long time now, he's been their best player, but it's no way for the captain to behave.

'He owes the manager a performance, he owes the club a performance, and he owes the fans a performance.'

Bruno Fernandes (right) has 'tarnished' his Manchester United legacy after criticising Michael Carrick (left), according to Alan Shearer

He added: 'I think he has tarnished his legacy at the club. I think the reaction that you saw at the end of the game against Bournemouth last week was pretty telling whose side the fans are on and it's Michael Carrick's, not Bruno Fernandes’, despite what he's done for the club.

'Whether that was part of him speaking to the manager and thinking, woah, I have got this wrong here. I don't know.'

Fernandes and Carrick held clear-the-air talks after the 3-0 Bournemouth loss, and many expect the midfielder to return to the side this weekend against Chelsea.

But it's unclear what will follow. Shearer, meanwhile, isn't convinced all is well.

'Fernandes and Carrick’s peace talks could’ve and probably should’ve happened before the game last week,' he added. 'Then there might not have been as much noise.

'Are they just papering over the cracks? I've been in a situation myself where I've not really got on with the manager in terms of Ruud Gullit and I guess you'd have to be on the inside to know what's really going on, but it would seem strange for him saying what he said, being left out and then being reinstated and then walking out as captain this week.

'It's not a good look, is it? It's pretty chaotic.'

Shearer suggested that crisis talks between Carrick and Fernandes may be 'papering over the cracks' amid the side's struggles

Old Trafford bosses decided not to sack Carrick with United in 16th place in the Premier League table, one point clear of the relegation zone.

The 45-year-old still faces a battle to improve results and performances and convince his employers that he remains the right person for the job.

Sources confirmed that Carrick has been given a second chance, and said that everyone is focused on showing a response on the pitch at Stamford Bridge following United’s worst start to a league season in 40 years.

The United boss was left in limbo after chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox held crisis talks on Monday with minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and co-chairmen Joel and Avram Glazer.

The first indications that Carrick had earned a reprieve came shortly before 8am on Tuesday when he arrived at Carrington dressed in a club tracksuit and oversaw training as the players returned after a day off.

He had also turned up at the training ground on Monday but was there to watch United’s Under-21s play in a behind-closed-doors game against Hull City alongside his No2 Steve Holland and Under-18s coach Darren Fletcher. He stayed for three hours before leaving with his son Jacey, a member of United’s Under-18s.

#2316. Calciomercato Napoli, Laurienté del Sassuolo possibile obiettivo di Manna

TMW riporta al centro del mercato Armand Laurienté, attaccante del Sassuolo, ancora seguito dal Napoli nel suo percorso e con molta probabilità tra i possibili protagonisti della sessione invernale. Il club partenopeo aveva già inserito il classe 1998 nella propria lista di obiettivi nella finestra invernale scorsa, senza però affondare il colpo. La situazione potrebbe evolversi nei prossimi mesi: sull’esterno ci sono anche l’Ipswich Town ei club turchi Fenerbahce, Besiktas e Trabzonspor. Nessuna delle proposte ricevute ha però convinto il Sassuolo, che ha fissato una valutazione di almeno 25 milioni di euro. Un anno fa l’esterno fu vicino al Sunderland. Il club neroverde, che ha rinnovato il giocatore lo scorso maggio fino al 2029, non sarebbe però intenzionato a perderlo a gennaio.

#2312. Lazio, la forza dei cambi e un aspetto da correggere: dentro il primato

Otto gol, sei marcatori e due successi diversi: la squadra di Gattuso trova nuove risorse, ma concede ancora nel primo tempo.

La Lazio prima in classifica ha mostrato due modi diversi di vincere nella stessa settimana. A Sassuolo ha segnato sei volte, contro il Cagliari ha dovuto aspettare l’83’ per completare la rimonta. Due partite che, lette insieme, aiutano a capire cosa stia sostenendo il rendimento della squadra di Gennaro Gattuso.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Il punto di partenza sono i 28 punti conquistati su 30 disponibili, con nove vittorie e un pareggio. Come certificato dalla Lega Serie A, si tratta della miglior partenza nella storia del club. Il confronto fra le ultime due gare aggiunge però qualcosa alla fotografia del primato: la capacità di trovare protagonisti e soluzioni differenti.

Il 6-2 contro il Sassuolo nasce da una partenza immediatamente produttiva. Taylor segna al 2’, Thorstvedt pareggia al 7’, poi Isaksen e Floriani Mussolini portano i biancocelesti sul 3-1 entro il 18’. La Lazio aveva dunque già costruito un doppio vantaggio prima dell’espulsione del centrocampista neroverde, arrivata al 31’.

La superiorità numerica resta un elemento da considerare nell’analisi del risultato. Non cancella quanto costruito prima, ma impedisce di leggere tutti i novanta minuti come un confronto nelle stesse condizioni. Dopo il momentaneo 2-3 di Esposito, Zaccagni ristabilisce le distanze prima dell’intervallo e Noslin completa il punteggio con una doppietta nella ripresa.

Contro il Cagliari, invece, la Lazio deve recuperare lo svantaggio firmato da Nzola. Isaksen pareggia al 36’, mentre la rete decisiva arriva soltanto nel finale con Pinamonti.

Il conteggio delle due gare restituisce otto gol e sei marcatori differenti: Taylor, Isaksen, Floriani Mussolini, Zaccagni, Noslin e Pinamonti. È un dato significativo sulla distribuzione delle reti. In questa settimana il risultato non è dipeso da un solo finalizzatore: hanno contribuito giocatori di reparti diversi, titolari e subentrati.

La vittoria sul Cagliari offre l’esempio più concreto del peso della panchina. Pinamonti e Pedraza, entrati entrambi al 55’, costruiscono l’azione del sorpasso: lo spagnolo serve il pallone che l’attaccante trasforma di testa all’83’. Con l’ingresso del centravanti, Noslin si sposta sulla fascia. Cambiano gli uomini e anche la disposizione offensiva. News

Come riportato da LazioPress.it nella conferenza del 1° novembre, Gattuso ha riconosciuto l’energia portata dai cambi, spiegando anche che la squadra aveva pagato qualcosa dopo aver schierato quasi sempre gli stessi nelle tre partite ravvicinate. La rimonta suggerisce quindi una risorsa importante: poter modificare una gara complicata attraverso le alternative disponibili.

Resta un aspetto sul quale lavorare. Tutti e tre i gol subiti nelle ultime due partite sono arrivati prima dell’intervallo, mentre entrambe le riprese si sono chiuse senza reti incassate. Due incontri non bastano a definire una tendenza, ma indicano una differenza da approfondire nella gestione delle fasi della gara.

La lettura del primato passa anche da qui: una Lazio capace di segnare con uomini diversi e di trovare risposte dalla panchina, che conserva margini di miglioramento. I risultati premiano il lavoro di Gattuso; il confronto fra Sassuolo e Cagliari mostra quanto contino anche le soluzioni a disposizione quando la partita prende una direzione inattesa.

#2308. With McGregor now questioning Celtic's approach, isn't it clear something is badly wrong there?

Published: 14:35 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 16:19 EDT, 30 October 2026

Celtic captain Callum McGregor talking about strikers playing as wingers and his team not having the right shape threw up all manner of issues.

One of them is that time is surely up for Kasper Hogh at centre-forward, £11million club-record signing or not.

When manager Martin O’Neill spoke to the media yesterday, he talked about Callum Osmand really being better through the middle than out on the left. A more pertinent point, though, is that it really doesn’t make sense any longer to keep playing Camilo Duran on the right.

There is, after all, a £9m man in reserve in Haissem Hassan who was signed to play out on that flank.

It just looks ever more like Celtic didn’t really think hard enough about what kind of way they wanted to play when they bought all these blokes.

What’s become clear is that it’s better if it doesn’t involve Hogh, now 13 games without a goal, unless there’s some masterplan to start sticking two up front. Even then, you’d be considering your options.

Callum McGregor was frustrated by his side's display in Wednesday's draw with Dundee Utd

There’s an argument O’Neill doesn’t play to the Dane’s strengths and that does hold water. However, Hogh has got to be able to adapt. If he can’t, what does it say about the decision, and whoever was ultimately responsible for it, to sign him in the first place?

What does a clever, senior figure such as McGregor joining Cameron Carter-Vickers in calling out the structure and organisation of the team say too?

Celtic might still be top of the table, but they’re all over the shop from top to bottom.

If Rangers can’t win the league this term, particularly given the fact they cannot possibly keep spending the way they have been without access to significant funds from UEFA competition, you do wonder when they ever will.

Hibs game looks like being D-day for Robinson at Dons

Aberdeen boss Stephen Robinson really started to bear the look of the condemned man in the wake of his side’s home defeat at the hands of Falkirk during the week.

The bullishness from earlier in the campaign had gone. He gave a thoroughly unconvincing answer on BBC when asked what progress, if any, had been made since the summer. He sounded like a bloke who knows he’s not far from the firing squad.

‘Ultimately, you have to get results,’ he said. ‘Otherwise, you know the inevitable.’

Unless it turns into a procession, a loss to Rangers in Saturday’s Premier Sports Cup semi-final is unlikely to seal his fate. The home game against Hibs next weekend, though, is a different kettle of fish entirely.

Time appears to be running out for Aberdeen manager Stephen Robinson to get things right

If the Dons are to be meeting any of their key performance indicators, they need to be better than Hibs. They need to be finishing above them in the top half of the table. And that’s the bare minimum.

What’s more, the Easter Road side are hardly in tip-top shape. Marink Reedijk’s time as head coach has got off to an underwhelming start. Sporting director Malky Mackay is under pressure over poor recruitment. They are there for the taking.

If Robinson can’t get the better of them at home ahead of an international break, a real time for the club to take stock, he’s in bother.

Those in the Red Army willing to make almost any sacrifice to see him nudged out the door should consider one thing, though.

If the management team get dumped, chances are first-team coach Stephen Craigan will be back all over our tellies and radios in his old role as media mouthpiece. And who really wants that?

#2302. Harry Kane beat Kylian Mbappe to the Ballon d'Or by one of the smallest margins EVER: Full results are revealed after England captain's triumph

Published: 17:30 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 17:33 EDT, 30 October 2026

Harry Kane beat Kylian Mbappe by a slender 28 point margin to be crowned as winner of the Ballon d'Or.

Kane claimed football's ultimate individual honour on Monday night, becoming the first Englishman to win since Michael Owen in 2001.

His success came off the back of a stunning year with Bayern Munich and England, with the forward netting a staggering 73 goals during the 2025-26 season.

Kane's goals spearheaded Bayern Munich's domestic Treble, while he also captained England to third place at the World Cup.

A full breakdown of the results has now been revealed, with Kane topping the vote by receiving 1,055 points from an international jury of 100 journalists.

Mbappe, who had also been seeking to win the award for the first time in his career, finished agonisingly short with the Real Madrid and France star receiving 1,027.

Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or by just a 28-point margin, the full vote breakdown has revealed

Kylian Mbappe narrowly missed out on winning the award for the first time in his career

The gap is shorter than the closely fought battle between Rodri and Vinicius Jr in 2024, with the Spaniard having triumphed on that occasion by just 41 points.

Lionel Messi's 2019 triumph over Virgil van Dijk is the narrowest margin of recent votes, with just seven points separating the pair.

Previously Matthias Sammer beat legendary Brazilian forward Ronaldo to the honour in 1996 by one point, with the same margin also seeing Sir Bobby Charlton beating Eusebio in 1966, when just 22 people voted.

In total, 40 of the voters had ranked Kane as their top choice, earning him 15 points each time, with Mbappe receiving 23 first place votes by comparison.

Kane was left out of the top ten by two journalists, while three overlooked Mbappe.

Lamine Yamal, who was widely viewed as a front-runner for the award alongside Kane and Mbappe, ultimately ended 174 points behind the winner.

Rodri and Messi completed the top five having earned 726 and 612 points respectively.

Since 2022, the current system is based on voting by a large panel of international journalists from the top 100 FIFA-ranked countries, and top 50 for the Ballon d'Or Feminin. Only a single journalist from each country in these rankings is given a vote.

Lamine Yamal ultimately ended in third place in the vote, finishing 174 points behind Kane

Kane and his wife Kate Goodland shared a kiss after he won the striker award (left) and Ballon d'Or (right) on Monday night

Each journalist must establish a ranking of top ten players from a list of 30 named players also designated by France Football.

A first place vote is worth 15 points, with the number reducing until tenth position, where players secure one point.

Voters are asked to take into account individual performances and their decisive and impressive character.

They are then requested to consider their collective role and the trophies won, before weighing up a player's class and fair play.

Kane had celebrated on Monday night with friends and family, including his wife Kate, after receiving the award at the London Palladium.

Kane made sure to pay tribute to Kate, who he married in 2019, after seeing off competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe to win.

He said: 'To my wife, Kate, my best friend. We've been through ups and downs for sure. You're my biggest supporter. I actually felt like you wanted this more than me myself.

'The anxious wait for us to find out, I know it's been horrible for you, here it is - we've done it! You always want the best for me, you sacrifice yourself to help me achieve my dreams, and I know they're your dreams as well, so it wouldn't be possible without you.

'This is a trophy that we celebrate, not me. This is me and you, it's all the family, all our close-knit team, so I just want to say thank you, I love you.

'Can't wait to enjoy this and celebrate tonight for sure. Love you.'

The couple share two daughters, Ivy and Vivienne, and two sons, Louis and Henry.

And Kane also made sure to reference them in his acceptance speech at the glitzy ceremony at the London Palladium.

'My kids sat home watching, it's definitely past your bedtime, especially as we're [the ceremony] a little later than we hoped,' he said. 'So to Ivy, Vivienne, Louis and Henry. You're the reason I do this.

'I don't think you'll fully maybe appreciate bringing this trophy home. I'll bring a few others home, but this one is a special one, so I can't wait to see you and celebrate with you.

'I want to set a good example being a father but also being a professional and what it means to work hard, what it means to believe in yourself. I love you very much.'

The couple are both from Walthamstow and Kate has been the rock by her husband's side for years.

Kate is a sports science graduate and professional fitness coach, with 382k followers on Instagram.

The couple posed for photos on the red carpet at the London Palladium Theatre

Kane proposed in the Bahamas in 2017 and they married two years later, now living happily in Bavaria where they have settled well since the striker elevated his game to another level, dominating the Bundesliga.

During his emotional address on stage, he also thanked his parents. He said: 'Wow, wow, wow. I am almost speechless. Being here in London has made it extra special. Made it a good omen for me tonight.

'Thank you to everyone who voted for me, I can imagine it was tough this year. Mum and dad, what a moment. All those years, the sacrifice, the support you gave me. Taking me to training, coming to watch me play. No matter where it was, even to this day you're there.

'All those traits you have given me have allowed me to be successful and be here tonight.'

And Kane got royal approval as he hit the summit of world football's personal awards from Prince William.

'Huge congratulations to Harry Kane on winning the Ballon d'Or!' William wrote in a post on Instagram. 'What a fantastic achievement and so deserved.

'A brilliant captain, a remarkable player and someone who has given football fans across the world so many unforgettable moments.'

#2292. At the moment of reckoning, England’s old anxiety took hold

All the years that have passed since those red shirts on a summer’s day at a long-gone Wembley Stadium – the humiliations, the occasional triumph, the plentiful servings of self-pity. For a short while in Atlanta it felt like that epoch might finally be ending and all it came down to was managing the last five minutes and whatever the beleaguered referee might add.

A place at a World Cup final was within England’s grasp, a mere 60 years since the last. But just as it loomed into view, already the players and their manager were tracing an old path. The man currently in charge of the England team might be German, the players might be of a generation finessed under bold new coaching ideas, but once more a familiar anxiety took hold. England were minutes from the prize. Yet team and manager were already obeying an old instinct to sabotage the moment.

England had been in retreat long before Lionel Messi served up for Enzo Fernández the goal that would level this World Cup semi-final, and then the second for Lautaro Martínez ,which would propel Argentina forward. Of course, Messi is Messi, and this Argentina team exist to exert his will on games by any means necessary. Yet, as ever, at the moment of reckoning, England demonstrated all the resistance of damp cardboard.

Thomas Tuchel once again reverted to the deep defensive position. Once again, the adapted five-man back line sat on the edge of their area. Against Mexico in the last 16, Tuchel was dismissive of any suggestion he had invited pressure, asking what other option he had with just 10 men. Against Norway in the quarter-finals he did the same, once Erling Haaland was off the pitch. Against Argentina, a team accustomed to playing with it all on the line, such a move was fatal.

Argentina are ahead! 😱A relentless spell of pressure sees Alexis Mac Allister hit the post before ANOTHER Lionel Messi assist sets up Lautaro Martinez to make it 2-1. pic.twitter.com/kVoNouFgKZ

Immediately the supporters in the stands in Atlanta, and in the streets and front rooms of England, recognised the mistake. The punditocracy on the BBC saw it, too. Former players Wayne Rooney and Joe Hart have been here before and treated this defeat much like revisiting a trauma. For the rest of us it was hard to miss: like staring into the face of the England team over the decades that have passed since 1966.

"The wait and the pain goes on for English football." 💔England's dream of reaching a first men's World Cup final since 1966 is over as Argentina make it six wins from six semi-final appearances 👏 pic.twitter.com/AEMHqqcYfI

Tuchel said that Argentina’s tactical changes as he saw them – two wide wingers, two central strikers – forced his hand. So too, he seemed to suggest, did the attitude of his players. He talked about them failing to be “active” as he called it, engaging their opposition and taking the game to them. But by this point those on the outside could see it more clearly than him.

This kind of retreat, to a greater or lesser degree, was the default position of so many England teams. England led against Brazil in 2002, Croatia in 2018, Italy in 2021. Sir Gareth Southgate, a man more criticised for a reluctance to make substitutions, never went into reverse quite as spectacularly as this. The record is now two World Cup semi-finals, and two European Championship finals in the last five tournaments. But that final step, or the penultimate one at the World Cup, is the primary English problem.

The recriminations from Atlanta will last for years, and as for the precious opportunity – who knows when it will come again?

Tuchel is part of this unfortunate history now, and defeats like this often suck reputations into the void. Afterwards he breezily turned over the page to Euro 2028, before England complete Saturday’s third-place play-off, although one feels that moving on will be more difficult than that.

After Fernández’s 85th-minute equaliser, Messi found the substitute Martínez at the back post for a winner seven minutes later. “There was blood in the water and we went for it,” Lionel Scaloni, the Argentina head coach, said. His team, to their credit, never gave up the chase.

They pursued that equaliser after Anthony Gordon’s 55th-minute goal, a fine finish after England launched a quick attack down the right that ended with Morgan Rogers sweeping the ball to the back post. England had just 12 per cent of the ball from that moment until Martínez’s 92nd-minute goal.

ENGLAND HAVE THE OPENER! 🤩Anthony Gordon puts the Three Lions ahead in the World Cup semi-final! pic.twitter.com/5fBlRcf1oI

This Argentina team are very hard to love, but you have to admire the tenacity with which they keep going. Around Messi is a fairly mixed bag of young talents and old boys clinging on. Their commitment to the cause, however, is not in doubt. They handle the moments of adversity better than most.

As for England, in the minutes that followed Gordon’s goal, Tuchel and his players seemed to make up their minds that what had sufficed for Norway and Mexico would work for Argentina.

He brought off Gordona after 72 minutes for Ezri Konsa and then Dan Burn and Nico O’Reilly came on for Reece James and Declan Rice. In the meantime, the game was following an inevitable path. There were nine attempts on the England goal, including the two that went in, after Gordon scored. Alexis Mac Allister somehow clipped a post with a header. Jordan Pickford made one of the saves of his life from the substitute Nicolás González. A post was struck again by Mac Allister before the second goal.

In other words: this goal was coming. This Argentina have some fine players, including Messi, Julián Alvarez, Fernández, Emiliano Martínez – but they are so much more than the sum of their parts. The game finished with the 38-year-old Nicolás Otamendi on the pitch. So too the MLS midfielder Rodrigo De Paul, as well as the right-back Gonzalo Montiel, 29, who did not make the grade on loan at Nottingham Forest.

“They were raised in an environment where they feared nothing,” Scaloni said of his players. “They don’t feel the weight on their shoulders.” In those painful last moments, Tuchel tried to reverse his earlier mistake by sending on Ivan Toney and Marcus Rashford, but the momentum had slipped away. England were beaten.

It had been intense from the start with the Argentine cynicism as high as ever. Elliot Anderson was targeted and eventually booked when Djed Spence nudged a charging Messi into the midfielder’s path. Spence was superb for much of the game, including a recovery tackle on Giuliano Simeone after the Gordon goal.

WHAT A TACKLE FROM DJED SPENCE 👊 pic.twitter.com/kyrHBS0tzX

At the critical moment when Messi prepared to cross for the Martínez goal, however, Spence seemed to feel a bolt of pain and could not react in time.

It was a gripping game, even without a single shot on target from either side in the first half. Ismail Elfath, the US referee for whom this game felt impossible at times, was slow to book Argentina players. They seemed to know who to target, in particular Jude Bellingham and Pickford. Bellingham had some fine moments in the first half but he struggled after the break.

England’s goal came 10 minutes after half-time, when the momentum had been with Argentina. Nicolás Tagliafico only just stopped Harry Kane’s long ball forward. From there Rice fed Rogers and the cross was perfect. At the back post, Gordon slipped past his man and guided it home, right-footed, at the back post.

In the aftermath England seemed to retreat. Tuchel said that he did not believe in a curse that afflicts England in the closing stages of such big knockout games. Of course, he was seeing it first hand for the first time – which, for the rest of us, is sadly not the case.

Thomas Müller: "I cannot believe and understand how England approached this game after they're leading. I cannot understand how they invited Argentina to play one cross after the other in perfect crossing positions" pic.twitter.com/Hm35pZfRwf

🚨 WATCH: Police rescue an Argentina fan in London after he was surrounded by England fans pic.twitter.com/ukDjubWuEV

[Reporter: Did the better team win?] “I don’t know. I thought we deserved to be 1-0 up. The momentum changed after that. They had nothing to lose and we suddenly played like we had a lot to lose. They took more and more risks and turned the game around in the last 20 minutes.

[Argentina had 88 per cent possession after Gordon’s goal] “It felt like that.” [What went wrong?] “We didn’t have enough possession to escape the pressure. We tried everything but couldn’t get hold of the ball. It’s like you’re dying a slow death. It started straight away after the goal and is the reason basically that we lost.”

“We were the better team until we cored then the mindset shifted, they took a lot of risks and have a lot of quality.

[You took Gordon off for Konsa at 71 minutes and sat deep] “We sat deep from when we scored the goal. Not after the substitutions. I take the responsibility. It’s easy to be a coach after the game. The result tells the story. No one can say what would have happened with other substitutions. I thought we needed a back five with all the crossing.

“We didn’t stop the second line coming through the gaps. We were not physical enough in these moments. It’s not about structure. You can play in any structure deep, you can defend in any structure if you’re active but we were too passive.

[Harry said he’d been here before, 1-0 up in the 2018 semi-final, 1-0 up in the Euro 2020 final] “I can’t speak about that I was not part of that.

“No regrets, we gave everything, that’s the bottom line. We gave everything. It’s difficult to accept because we hate to lose. We were very close. For the overall summary we have to wait a bit and digest it.

"I take the responsibility"Thomas Tuchel reacts as England's World Cup dream comes to an end following defeat to Argentina...🎙️ @gabrielclarke05 pic.twitter.com/Vrm071Zkd1

The FA extended Tuchel’s initial 18-month contract to the end of Euro 2028 last year. He was hired to be the ultimate “finisher”, focusing solely on the first team rather than all the other jobs as a figurehead for the elite pathway that Gareth Southgate filled. His job was specifically to get England over the line after two defeats in Euros finals, a World Cup semi and quarter.

Everyone deserves one tournament’s grace and he has gone farther than anyone bar Sir Alf, Sir Bobby and Sir Gareth. But when you talk so much about your players being brave, you also need to demonstrate your own courage. And clinging on for dear life, even if it worked in different circumstances against lesser opposition, is pusillanimous. Scaloni’s substitutions won the game for Argentina, Tuchel’s lost it for England.

Gutted. Tonight wasn't the result we all hoped for, but this England team has given it their all.The passion and energy they've shown representing the badge has made us all proud.

Gutted. England, you gave it everything and we are all so proud of you.Thank you to everyone on and off the pitch, for an incredible tournament. The fight and belief you have shown has inspired us all. The most complete England team in a tournament. Hold your heads high 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 W https://t.co/PDBNEsuVfS

“We are disappointed. We got so close but we got too passive after we scored and conceded a lot of chances. We could not turn possession around and juts conceded so, so many chances, crosses and shots.

“We were so, so close but we couldn’t keep the level up after we scored.

“I also made offensive substitutions in the last games to try to help the players. We decided to go to a back five because the gaps were too large but they kept crossing and crossing. We went to a back five to close the gaps in the air and win headers. We concedes so many crosses and chances after our goal so we tried to help. But the responsibility is on the coach and if it doesn’t go well it is easy to say it is wrong.

“Yeah [we wanted to go for a second goal] but it doesn’t help when you can’t get the ball. I didn’t think an offensive substitution [at that point] would help. We got more and more passive. We couldn’t keep balls, we couldn’t win balls. It was not a structural problem after the goal. We changed nothing [in the immediate aftermath] but I understand these are the discussions and millions of coaches after the game know better.

“We can discuss this [whether they invited pressure] but I have to make a decision. I have to analyse what I see on the pitch and take responsibility.”

[Any regrets?] “Not at the moment. The team gave everything and we were very, very close. We deserved to be 1-0 up. We played one of our better matches, maybe the best match [of the tournament] but we couldn’t bring it over the line. No regrets.

[Did we ever see the Thomas Tuchel England you wanted to see?] “I don’t have an answer for that question. I don’t know what it means. I think we saw the mentality throughout the matches. We played strong teams in the group, a lot of miles, a lot of travelling, we played at altitude, with 10 men, in the heat and we were very, very close. It is not the time to analyse the tournament. We went very close but lost a crucial match.”

In the celebrations on the final whistle, Argentina fans threw on a banner proclaiming: “Las Malvinas son Argentinas” declaring that the Falkland Islands will remain theirs. This win will potentially renew their demands to claim the Falklands as their own.

We will see if Fifa applies its regulations and fines the AFA.

Tuchel played his hand. He wanted to hang on. We were hanging on against Norway and Mexico but they haven’t got the same quality as Argentina.

He played his cards very early and it’s backfired. We were all praising him in previous games, now we will go the other way. He could have put more pace on. The players were physically and mentally done once Argentina got that first goal.

“Gutted for the boys, everyone. The team, the staff, the fans. We played a good game for the majority of it. Once we went 1-0 up we tried to hold on but at this level you can’t.

“The lads have given everything. Running, sweat, blood tears, whatever. So to fall short like we did today is just gutting.

“We struggled to get pressure on the ball [after scoring]. Whether it was them putting more men forward or us not being able to match them man for man it was juts wave after wave. Lads were putting blocks in but it wasn’t enough.

“The boys are always ready. The message after we went ahead was to go and get another one but when they got their two goals we tried to find something but we couldn’t get back into it.

“We had a lot of good moments, good matches in this tournament. Another semi-final. We keep knocking on the door. We need to find that missing piece in the final part of the tournament. We’re just missing that final piece.”

Wayne Rooney: “We go one-nil up and we go five at the back, we go six at the back. If you allow Argentina to come on to you, you’re in trouble. We surrendered. If you let players of that quality have the ball, you’re in trouble.”

Joe Hart: “Gareth Southgate will be sat at home, watching, and he was criticised for big games when England had the lead, I don’t see anything has changed. For Thomas Tuchel… that’s him saying he didn’t believe in his team and couldn’t land any more punches on Argentina.”

Micah Richards: “Tactically we all thought he got it wrong with his changes.”

Tonight the changes didn’t work. Argentina deserved their victory. Sadly, it’s deja vu for England when the moment of truth arrived.

They froze after scoring. As Joe Hart says, they went back to what they did against Mexico and Norway and packed the defence but Argentina are not Norway or Mexico. They have an indomitable spirit, experience and some great players. You can sit back against Mexico and Norway. You can’t withstand a 30-minute siege against a team like Argentina.

England have lost a third World Cup semi-final. Argentina were the better team. They took more risks, made positive substitutions and found the attacking incisiveness that England lacked all game, apart from when setting up Gordon’s goal.

England pump a long ball up to Dan Burn and Argentina knock it clear. It has come to this.

Rashford gets to the byline on the left and cuts back a cross that Argentina clear. Then Bellingham brings down Messi and Montiel taunts Bellingham when the free-kick was awarded.

England are huffing and puffing, pumping long throws and crosses into the box but without the precision they need.

You can’t say Argentina have not deserved it for their response. They have shown why they are world champions.

I’m afraid England have been sitting ducks ever since they scored.

Rashford and Toney are on for Spence and Stones as England have a throw on the right.

England 1 Argentina 2 (Lautaro Martinez) Gonzalez slides a pass inside from the left to Mac Allister who flays a shot into the foot of the right post. Spence slides into knock it away from Messi but Messi races out to the right to retrieve it and arc over a right-foot cross that Lautaro Martinez creeps between Konsa and Stones to bury with a forceful header.

Lautaro Martinez wins it for Argentina in stoppage time 🇦🇷 pic.twitter.com/7DQKq2DIhk

Bellingham tries to relieve the siege with a long solo run up the left but can’t keep it going.

Nine minutes of stoppage time are signalled after Stones receives treatment for a head injury sustained in a collision with his keeper. He has to go off for a minute.

The chances were coming. Tuchel made his big decisions, but the crosses kept coming into the box. It’s not a great strike for me. The keeper has to save it. Now it’s an awkward one tactically. Tuchel will have to make another change.

England have been under the cosh for the past 20 minutes and have switched to a packed defence. Can they switch back and regain some momentum.

England have got four centre-backs on the pitch. Tuchel has to re-balance this. His changes to try to see the game out were understandable, although they ultimately haven’t worked. England will take extra-time at the moment, because Argentina have the momentum.

England 1 Argentina 1 (Fernandez) Messi takes the corner short to De Paul who gives it back to the captain. Messi then drills a pass to Enzo Fernandez 22 yards out, right of centre. Pickford soars to his left to turn Fernandez’s shot over the bar.

This is a blow for Reece James and England. Has him hamstring gone again? We will find out for sure later, but here’s Big Dan Burn to try to get England over the line. Tuchel’s team have dropped very deep since going ahead and I’d worry about them finding a second wind if Argentina do manage to equalise.

O’Reilly and Burn come on for Rice and James. O’Reilly slots into midfield. Lautaro Martinez replaces Tagliafico.

Rogers mugs Messi in the tackle and bombs forward with Kane in tow but smacks his shot into a defender. Back come Argentina with a couple of crosses that force Anderson to head it off Mac Allister’s attempted bicycle klick and Kane to throw his body on the line to thwart Alvarez.

England are clinging on now and Messi clips a fantastic [ass with his left foot from the inside-right channel to the back post. Gonzalez peels off James and heads back across goal, looking for the far corner, but it drifts inches wide. Montiel drops to his haunches. Up goes the flag but it was mighty close and could have been overturned by VAR.

Moments later De Paul hammers an effort that Pickford saves low then gathers at the second attempt when Mac Allister was closing him down.

England are happy to soak up the pressure Argentina are trying to exert and attempt to hit them on the break but it’s nerve-racking.

De Paul’s swings in a cross with venomous whip and dip. Mac Allister gets up to head it powerfully into the heart of the left post. He had to score. Konsa picked the wrong man to mark.

England do go to five at the back with Konsa’s introduction for Gordon

Argentina send on De Paul, Otamendi and Montiel for Simeone, Molina and Lisandro Martinez.

Can England now stop Messi? This could be his last 25 minutes in international football and he is trying everything.

Argentina are coming. You can feel it as well as see it.

For then first time all day, Buenos Aires fell silent as Anthony Gordon put England in front.

Pickford saves England’s lead with a one-handed, scooped save from Gonzalez’s header, the sub artfully picked out by Messi’s cross. Is it too soon for Dan Burn and five at the back?

Fine pass from Kane opens up Argentina on England’s right and James feeds a pass across the 18-yard line to Rice. His attempted daisycutter of a shot turns into a pea-roller and is an easy save for Emi Martinez.

Stones stops the substitute’s first touch, a header back across goal, from reaching Alvarez with a crucial header.

Fernandez fires a shot over the bar after Argentina’s most sustained spell of possession of the match.

Even Victoria Beckham was up celebrating that England goal. She’d stayed in her seat against Norway, but was up hugging husband David when Gordon’s shot at the back post hit the back of the net.

Colossal sense of catharsis as Anthony Gordon, the calmest man in the building, propels England towards the World Cup final with an almost nonchalant finish from Morgan Rogers’ exquisite cross.

Argentina do not panic when behind and have started to play with more fluency as England let them have the ball. Kane shows remarkable composure in his own box to shield the ball from two attackers and see it into safe harbour.

The two wingers combine brilliantly! How long have we wanted more England attackers to come to the party in this World Cup? England needed something else tonight and they’ve got it big style.

Argentina were on the verge of equalising when a mistake allows Simeone to storm down the right and into the box. Just as he was about to pull the trigger on a shot, Spence hared back to slide in and knock the ball behind for a corner. Amazing.

That was a superb England move from the moment Tagliafico made a mess of clearing Kane’s long ball. Gordon’s finish right in the money. It was always going to have to be good. Let’s see how Argentina respond.

Molina’s cross from the right is ripe with menace but England see it off.

The two sides of Romero, an amazingly insouciant touch in the box a split-second before Gordon as about to steal the ball off him and a turn away from fanger. Then, moments later, he grabs Bellingham round the waist to stop him driving past and is belatedly booked.

England defend the corner taken by Messi short so that he can be played back in up the byline. Bellingham stands his ground and Messi cannot wriggle past him, finding only the brick wall of Bellingham’s torso.

That’s how to deal with Messi. Body in the way first, keep contact, steer him away from trouble. Superb from Bellingham.

Emi Martinez dwells on the ball, trying to invite the press. England stand off and eventually the keeper launches it. Simeone beats Guehi to flick it on and Alvarez drives past Spence and then shoots towards the near post. Pickford gets down low to beat it away.  Alvarez beats Spence to the rebound and has another go, smashing it into the side netting via a faint deflection.

The biggest cheer of the half here in the Fan Fest arena at the Palermo came when Messi was fouled by Elliot Anderson, prompting the 10,000 fans here to jump up and down to let no-one in doubt that they are English. Otherwise, it has been fairly muted. Perhaps they have been a bit embarrassed about the lack of cards. It suggests England are so far holding their own.

Rice, with one leg of his shorts hitched up, kicks off. No changes. The referee insists the kick-off be taken again as Anthony Gordon had crossed the line before the whistle. Pickford pumps a 70-yard pass up the middle, looking for Kane. Romero wins the header.

We wanted to be the aggressor, we wanted to be on the front foot and get after them – to show there was no inferiority complex and that we’re here to play in their half.

I think it worked until the water break. After that it was a bit more difficult for us to get the ball – they dropped Messi and Enzo [Fernandez] outside our block and got some possession. But it’s still absolutely OK, and the evolution for us is to take this dominance and turn it into bigger chances.

The more time we spend in their half, the more tired they’ll get.

A cagey half, which is to be expected given the stakes. I’ve been impressed with England. They’ve looked dangerous without creating any clear chances. Argentina have created nothing so far.

What’s encouraging is England look like they belong out there, going head-to-head with the world champions, and Elliot Anderson has been outstanding.

This has been the opposite of what the rest of the tournament has been for us. In previous matches there have been a lot of average performances and our two best players have shone. This time, England have played well as a collective while the two best players have been quiet. Bellingham and Kane might have their moment in the second half.

Too many fouls, too many stoppages by design. No shots on target. Both teams are scrapping but there has been very little quality. The foul count is 19, seven by England, 12 by Argentina.

Three shots on goal, none of them on target, just about sums up that first half. Both sides have had a player booked and Kane, Messi and Bellingham have all gone to the referee at the break. This has been scrappy and ill-tempered, but also pretty absorbing.

England work the free-kick to Gordon whose cross is deflected over the bar for a corner but the referee blows for half-time before it can be taken. Clive Thomas, at the age of 90, nods approvingly.

The signal goes up for three minutes of stoppage time, the absolute minimum.

Paredes is penalised for dangerous play for raising his studs in a challenge on James.

It is compelling to watch but not particularly elevating. Romero makes a good tackle on Bellingham. When he is in control of his emotions, he is a fine defender.

England have not made much from their dozen free-kicks. More haste less speed.

The referee sees Lisandro Martinez pulling Rogers’ shirt and finally acts.

FINALLY, this referee has remembered he can also book the players in the navy blue. Lisandro Martinez: yellow.

It’s become cat-and-mouse with Argentina getting more of the ball in the last ten minutes. The one worry is Messi is just starting to take possession much more with some great touches. He hasn’t hurt England yet, though. The hydration break stopped some momentum again, but Tuchel will be pleased overall so far.

Argentina defend the free-kick staunchly as Anderson cannot get above Tagliafico then Messi breaks, hangs on to the ball with sumptuous skill, beating Kane, Spence and Rice before Anderson launches himself at the No10 to stop him. Argentina surround the referee with the distaste of someone who had heard a guest break wind in front of the King. Eventually they get on with the free-kick. Messi tries to dribble straight down the middle, can’t do so but the ball breaks to Fernandez who fires a shot that scratches the top of the cross-bar. That was alarmingly close.
