#2259. Spain win World Cup in triumph of football over Argentine thuggery

Football 1 Felons 0. It took extra time to get there but, thank goodness, we got there. The sport prevailed. Spain won the World Cup and we are all better for that. Football is better for that. It desperately needed Spain to win this final. Anything else would have felt like a crime.

Even at the final whistle Argentina showed their thuggishness with Nahuel Molina throwing a punch at Rodri and coach Lionel Scaloni – usually so calm – getting involved. Leandro Paredes, who might want to try to play football rather than manhandle his opponents, grabbed Eric García by the throat and pushed over Gavi. What a sight.

Leandro Paredes was sent off after the final whistle amidst ugly scenes from some of the Argentina players 🔴Nahuel Molina also appeared to throw a punch towards one of the celebrating Spain players 😬 pic.twitter.com/LVItPtx08n

And Lionel Messi? For all the brilliance of the world’s greatest ever player – as England can sorely testify from the semi-final – his most memorable contribution was to try to get Spain’s Marc Cucurella sent off for covering his mouth.

That was in retribution after Enzo Fernández was rightly dismissed in added time of the regulation 90 minutes to become the third Argentina player to be sent off in a World Cup final, after two in 1990. They used the same dirty tactics as all those decades ago.

After he collected his runners-up medal there were tears from Messi, 39 now and surely at his last World Cup. But no one need cry for Argentina.

Now the deposed world champions, they deserved nothing because they did nothing, becoming the first World Cup finalists not to even have a shot until the 121st minute, when Giuliano Simeone fired over from a corner when they were frantically chasing the game.

It's a late, late chance missed for Argentina! 😱The ball drops to Giuliano Simeone in the middle of the box but he's leaning back and he sends the ball sailing over the bar. pic.twitter.com/TISiWHBLiE

Instead, they pushed and shoved, fouled and stood over opponents on the ground with a few choice words. And tried to pressurise the referee, as they had so successfully done against England. But at least this time the official, Slovenian Slavko Vincic, eventually intervened with Fernández’s red.

ENZO FERNANDEZ IS SENT OFF 🟥Argentina will play the rest of the World Cup final with 10 men after Fernandez got his second yellow for a very late tackle. pic.twitter.com/OZFDiTc2oV

In the first half, Argentina committed more fouls – nine – than they completed passes in the final third of the pitch – eight. This was nasty, depressing anti-football. And it got what it deserved.

The only goal came in the second period of extra time with Spain’s brilliant winger, Nico Williams, who should have started and made such a difference, cleverly heading back a Pedro Porro cross for another replacement, Ferran Torres, to lash high into the net. What a relief.

Ferran Torres rifles the ball into the roof of the net and Spain lead in extra-time 🇪🇸 pic.twitter.com/uzlNFQ8QUX

Spain should have won far more comfortably, but the European champions lived up to the claim made by their coach Luis de la Fuente and proved they are the best team in the world, having beaten the favourites France in the last four.

Spain won this tournament for the second time, 16 years after the first. Now there is just one nation chasing a “second star”, the one beaten by Argentina in Atlanta last Wednesday.

If England ever want to win this again then here is the blueprint. This is how the game should be played. Get the ball, keep the ball, love the ball, move the ball. Try to play. Be brave and stay brave. It is not complicated, but it requires a re-education.

Maybe one day English football will grow up and cherish ball-players of their own, rather than Manchester City signing Rodri, who was magnificent here until he tired, or Arsenal with Martín Zubimendi, who successfully replaced him.

Rodri was named player of the tournament, in recognition of the football his nation played and the 30-year-old’s importance to to their system. He is their heartbeat and metronome. England do not just need to find a Rodri, but cherish whoever that is.

Spain lift the World Cup for a second time! 🏆🏆🇪🇸 pic.twitter.com/d4DFJdjCj9

Argentina will point to the fact they lost three-quarters of their back four to injury. But that would be a diversionary tactic. Their approach was clear from the first whistle and did not deviate as they attempted to rough up Spain the way they did England.

Except Spain are more evasive because they pass the ball quicker and better than England. There is such a debate about possession-based football in the Premier League, the attempt by coaches, often unsuccessful, to replicate Pep Guardiola. But that is what the best teams do; the winning teams. Especially in international football. We need to reduce the pace and physicality and remember what the purpose of the game is. Thomas Tuchel got it wrong and should admit it.

Spain again showed the way as they did in beating England in the final of the last European Championship, and they will be the team to beat when it comes to retaining that crown in two years’ time. Which will largely be held in England.

This was not a great final. It was a hard watch, especially after the referee gave Argentina licence to play as they wanted as he somehow failed to book Alexis Mac Allister for a horrible lunging tackle on Dani Olmo. The ball was an afterthought for the Liverpool midfielder.

Alexis Mac Allister puts in a tackle on Dani Olmo but the referee doesn't reach for his pocket, much to the disappointment of Spain fans ❌ pic.twitter.com/v7F0973mOO

It prompted chants of “Fifatina” from the Spain fans; referencing the conspiracy theory that the governing body wanted Argentina, and more specifically Messi, to win it again.

Spain’s momentum was not helped by Argentina’s approach, or by the ridiculously long half-time break, with the spectacularly bad show, which lasted almost half an hour. But they kept striving forward.

Finally the chances came, late in normal time, with Torres heading straight at Emiliano Martínez, who also denied Pedri before Aymeric Laporte headed weakly. There were two more headers from Williams and Mikel Merino, all good chances.

The ball was in the net, from Williams, but those conspiracy theorists will have been in overdrive as it was ruled out for a non-existent foul on Nicolás Otamendi, who threw himself to the ground after contact with Merino.

Nico Williams thought he'd given Spain the lead in the World Cup final... but it's ruled out by the referee who spotted a foul.Do you think Spain were unlucky with that decision? pic.twitter.com/bc3RHRnoYy

But the goal did come and, with the world watching, justice was served. In this most controversial of World Cups, where the focus has sometimes been elsewhere, Spain won. Football won. Even if Argentina showed the final disrespect by turning their backs and failing to congratulate their opponents. Class against classlessness.

Spain lift the World Cup for a second time! 🏆🏆🇪🇸 pic.twitter.com/d4DFJdjCj9

Rodri was waiting for him to leave before he lifted it but he lingered a while on the edge of the group as Infantino tried to show the way off.

And go up in squad number order with David Raya first.

Perhaps it is the end. One would thing being 43 in 2030 would make it impossible to carry on until then.

The vitriol has dissipated and Spain give them a gracious round of applause. A silver medal isn’t so bad when most of the squad already have a gold one.

Spain’s captain, Rodri. Ballon d’Or winner in 2024, world and European champion.

Unai Simon who has kept seven clean sheets and conceded only one goal in the tournament.

Pau Cubarsi and it’s thoroughly deserved.

The referee Slavko Vincic retires after today.

Donald Trump and Gianni Infantino walk on together with Claudia Sheinbaum and Mark Carney behind. They are being booed, whether that’s for Infantion or Trump it’s hard to tell. Probably both.

A brief fight erupted immediately after the whistle, with punches thrown. One player went tumbling down in the chaos. Borja Iglesias also clashed with Lionel Scaloni.  It’s been just as ill-tempered from Argentina as the 1990 final, when they had two sent off in the second-half, Pedro Monzón and Gustavo Dezotti

Paredes swings a couple of punches at Spain players and some of his team-mates join in the pushing and slapping. Messi does not get involved and Scaloni has to come on to get him away.

Otamendi is in Rodri’s face complaining about something.

Cucurella pushes Paredes over and Argentina will have one last chance to pump it into the box. Spain win the header and the World Cup!

Argentina free-kick in their own half. Messi hangs it it up and Simon comes put to catch.

Argentina are on the attack but Tagliafico decides to shove Merino and gift-wraps a free-kick for Spain.

Messi’s corner inspires pinball and mayhem. The ball drops to Simeone on the volley and he hoofs it over from 12 yards as he fell backwards.

Williams with a cheap foul 10 yards inside the Spain half gives Argentina a free-kick. Messi plays a one two and dribbles down the right then sends Simeone to the byline to cross. Garcia slides in to beat Mac Allister and turn it behind for a corner.

Five minutes of stoppage time to come. Seems excessive to me.

The game resumes with a drop ball and Merino off the field. Yamal blocks the cross.

Messi has a pot shot from 20 yrads and hits Merino flush in the face, knocking him over. Much to Argentina’s disgust, the referee blows to stop the game for a head injury.

Williams breaks through down the left with perfect poise and then in a moment of slapstick, instead of shooting, he tries to chop it with his left but only chops it into his right foot and out for a goalkick.

Messi buys himself a corner, plays a one-two with Paredes and hooks his cross/shot on to the roof of the net.

Argentina have a free-kick for offside outside their own penalty area. Up go all the defenders and Martinez launches it towards the Argentina box. Spain win the header and Yamal sends Ferran Torres racing through the broken lines to thump a shot pas Martinez but he had jumped the gun, half a yard offside.

Mac Allister is booked for booting Merino who was quiet happy to take the bargain of sharp pain for the resulting free-kick

A waspish comment from Guy Mowbray about Scaloni packing his team with defensive substitutes now that they need a response. ‘Has he Tucheled himself?’

Spain 1 Argentina 0 (Ferran Torres) Deep cross from the right, Porro, I think. Williams nods it back from the byline on the left to keep it alive and put it on a plate for Ferran Torres who steered his volley into the roof of the net with the perfect blend of power and precision.

Ferran Torres rifles the ball into the roof of the net and Spain lead in extra-time 🇪🇸 pic.twitter.com/uzlNFQ8QUX

The breakthrough for Spain, and the crucial assist from Nico Williams. He has been a revelation in this game. A great substitute’s performance.

Tagliafico has to be lifted to his feet to start the half.

Argentina are scrapping in characteristic fashion, using every trick in the book. Spain just haven’t been good enough to get past them… yet. If they were to lose this on penalties, they will be kicking themselves for the next four years.

Argentina throw themselves on to the floor at the slightest touch to try to eat up more time.   One more minute to come.

Argentina’s bench goes loopy when the referee refuses to award a foul because Simeone had stopped deliberately to initiate contact with Cucurella whose eyes were on the ball as he tracked back to try to win a header. Scaloni’s reaction is over the top and he joins Paredes et al in the book.

Merino misses a golden chance with a free header from about right yards to the right of the penalty spot. The cross was perfect, the run was perfect and the connection was awful, smearing it wide.

Spain keep the tiki-taka rhythm in their build-up until Yamal decides to go for a worldie of a finish with a left-foot shot he would like to bend into the top left corner from the right but it keeps climbing until it hits the crowd.

Messi fouls Cubarsi and has a shot after the whistle that was off target.

The officials says Otamendi’s foot was trodden on. Didn’t look like it.

When you think you've won the World Cup 😬Luis de la Fuente experienced EVERY emotion after Spain's goal was disallowed pic.twitter.com/Fu9MlVXH7X

That’s very soft if he rules that out and backs up the referee. That seems a clear and obvious error to me. Otamendi dived and Martinez was not really touched by Merino before Williams slotted the ball in from 10 yards.

Lovely pass from Pedri, clipped from the inside-right to the inside-left as Williams stole in behind Otamendi but Otamendi managed to get a  flick on it that changed the trajectory slightly and Williams could not adjust to reach it with his forehead.

Seems nailed on for Argentina to win on penalties with Martinez the hero once more.

Argentina are going to have to do more with less in extra-time, and it’s a huge task. Pedri and Merino have really made a difference. Paredes is one yellow and another half. This is the opportunity for Spain. They have tortured a very resilient Argentina side for 100 minutes. They have got them down to ten men. Penalties would be a huge achievement for Argentina now.

Spain kick off and resume their patient probing. Spain could make two more subs, Argentina one.

While Cubarsi was receiving treatment Cuvurella was speaking to Messi and briefly touched his mouth. Up went Messi’s right arm and immediately told the referee to send him off but common sense prevailed.

Yamal takes it, and gets it over the wall but Emi Martinez soars to his left to turn it behind. And that’s the end of normal time.

Spain free-kick 22 yards out just right of centre for Paredes’ foul on Ferran Torres.

Simon triggers a counter-attack and Spain outnumber Argentina with Williams, Merino and Yamal. Williams drives down the right and spurns the urgings of Yamal to pas to him on the left of the box, then hammers a shot straight at Martinez who bats it away. Argentina launch it and Cubarsi picks up the ball, getting to it in front of Enzo who brings him down, arriving late.

That’s a second yellow card and off he trots but not until he has protested for 90 seconds with all his team-mates in support. It was a naield on yellow. Serves him right for his eralier dissent.

Enzo Fernandez’s red card - the first of his two yellows was for dissent. When you need to make as many fouls as he was always going to have to do in this game, it’s such a waste to pick one up for backchat. Not much sympathy beyond the borders of Argentina one suspects.

Enzo Fernandez clatters into Pau Cubarsi and gets a second booking 🟥Argentina are down to 10 men right before full-time... pic.twitter.com/aTij7bxqJO

Messi takes it short then receives the return pass and runs at the heart of the defence but is tackled. The ball ricochets out to Simeone down the right but his cross is so near Simon he could throw his cap on it as he dived.

Messi lays it off to Molina down the right then runs into Laporte who stands his ground. Free-kick to Argentina, 30 yards out.

Four minutes of stoppage time to come. Seems low given the number of fouls and substitutions.

Argentina win a series of tackles around the penalty area as Spain keep probing. But they cannot do anything with the ball and Spain pin them straight back. Rodri, to try to break the deadlock/tedium, lines up a shot from 25 yards and blazes over.

Merino spins a left-foot chip up the inside-right channel. Ferran Torres tacks over and tries to take it on the half-volley as it dropped over his shoulder but scuffed it into the hoardings.

This is an absolute dog of a game. It’s like 2010 and parts of 2014. But still Spain cannot pick the lock.

Enzo bundles Merino over while the Arsenal forward was shielding the ball and making a back for the foul. Spain move it forward to Ferran Torres who earns a throw-in on the right for his enterprising run.

Enzo Fernandez is booked for protesting when a challenge on him was not deemed a foul. He compounds his initial offence by applauding the referee who turns a blind eye to that show of dissent.

Porro lengthens his stride down the right and Tagliafico knocks it out for a throw-in. Spain work it down the line and cross for Laporte at the back post but he is very tightly marked by Medina who gets his body in the way and the effort loops harmlessly at Martinez.

It would be rather unfortunate if the second World Cup final on US soil went the same way as the first: a 0-0 draw at the Pasadena Rose Bowl 32 years ago, remembered almost only for Roberto Baggio’s penalty miss. Serena Williams looks less than enthralled, perhaps pining for a repeat of the tennis score England served up in Miami.

Cubarsi, who set up Spain’s winner in the Belgium game with a shot, almost does so again with one from 22 yards that dips and wobbles. Martinez dives to his right to block and his defenders make sure no one can pounce on the rebound. Argentina slow the game right down from the restart.

So many Spain shots hit straight at Martinez. They’re really pushing now.

Another Spain shot arrows down Martinez’s throat, this time from Pedri.

Paredes wipes Merino out when challenging for a header but he’s OK despite the heavy fall. Paredes won the ball so it was perfectly OK.

Argentina have now used all five subs and among them three of their four original defenders are off – including both centre-backs. They will surely have ‘a moment’ at some point but it’s been a long time coming.

Clever pass from Mac Allister sends Tagliafico free down the left but he hasn’t got the legs to beat Porro and doubles back. Simeone is played down the other wing and, with four in support, passes it straight to Baena.

Such a surprise that Romero goes down during that sustained period of pressure and prompts the hydration break. Argentina defending for their lives. The new factor was Emi Martinez flapping. Argentina have done very well to get to this stage at 0-0 given Spain’s domination. Yamal has struggled to get into the box and commit defenders. I think thatmay well tip it if he can do so.

Argentina make their final two substitutions:

Tagliafico tells Martinez he will deal with a deep cross but then heads behind when under no pressure. Yamal takes the corner to the near post again. It’s easily won by Argentina who head it back out to the winger. His second cross is better this time too and Ferran Torres heads it from eight yards straight at Martinez.

Yamal’s low corner is knocked back to him from the near post and his second attempt, a spinning, dipping menace, is headed behind by Paredes.

The ref plays advantage and allows Spain to pile forward after a foul and Dani Olmo shoots from 20 yards. The shot again dips in front of Emi Martinez and it squirts out of his grasp and goes behind for a corner.

Yamal whacks it into the wall and Argentina scramble it away for a throw-in of their own.

Ferran Torres → OyarzabalPedri → Fabian Ruiz.

Spain have a free-kick about 23 yards out, right of centre after Paredes kicked Porro on the Achilles. Yamal, Oyarzabal and Baena stand over it.

Montiel’s alertness stops Spain tearing a hole down the right of the attack and then switching it for Cucurella’s run into the box with another passing move of mesmerising movement. Montiel lunges in to put the ball behind before Cucurella can shoot. The corner comes to naught and Montiel’s race is run.

A gloriously slick move from Spain after Simon diddles Alvarez who was trying to press him. He passes calmly to Cubarsi who drives forward and they go bam-bam-bam from Ruiz to Olmo up to Oyarzabal who drives towards the box, shapes to shoot and instead threads it through to Olmo ahead of him for the return. But Olmo’s lay-off to Oyarzabal is blocked by Romero and Mac Allister.

Paredes dips his shoulder into Rodri’s back who goes down like a sack of spuds. Dani Olmo hares over to tell Paredes to leave his captain alone and Paredes shives him over too. The second offence draws the yellow card out of the ref’s pocket.

Rodri made sure that Paredes got that yellow card. One can only admire the dedication. Paredes only came on at half-time.

Argentina, who have had a day’s less rest, are poised to send on two more subs. Baena bumps into Montiel after the latter had released the ball and concedes a free-kick.

Laporte races across to the left of his defence with Cucurella upfield and slides in to tackle Montiel, putting the ball behind for a corner. Messi takes on the right, looking for Mac Allister’s near-post run but the ball bobbles off the Liverpool midfielder into a Spain defender and back out for a goal-kick.

Paredes makes a mistake with his first touch, trying to play it across his defence from the left and gives it to Baena who takes a touch then puts his laces through a shot that wobbles a bit then bounces awkwardly in front of Martinez who manages to dive forward and gather.

The show is over and it’s time for some more Beckham-themed commercials. about 24 minutes elapsed by my reckoning.

‘I like a lot of them artists but I thought it was crap,’ says Wayne Rooney.

Shakira is one of Fifa’s go-to options, it seems. The ubiquitous Dai Dai is the fourth official song she has performed although her first since La La La in Brazil 2014. The song titles are not exactly Dylanesque.

We’ve passed the 15 minute mark on my stopwatch. At this point in every other World Cup final in history, the game would have restarted.

Introduced by Ted Lasso. Then it’s Shakira.

That wasn't on our bingo card 😅R9 and Ronaldinho drive Madonna through the tunnel for the Half-Time Show 👀 pic.twitter.com/Yy9eFKfz9z

Madonna is up on the big stadium screen being driven in a buggy by Ronaldo - the one that needs the Fifa cash, not that other one. Thus far, it seems that her much vaunted appearance in the half-time show does not include an in-person appearance although that could be a late twist.

With Madonna singing Music, flanked by the original Ronaldo and Ronaldinho. It has to be seen to be believed, particularly the expression on Il Fenomeno’s face.

They are followed by BTS and the Muppets.

Argentina will be pleased to have restricted Spain’s chances, but it will have been very hard work to make all those sprints out to the man in possession, in this direct sunshine. That will have taken a lot out of Argentina. They have also lost Lisandro Martinez, who cannot be fit. But they have been shown the usual leniency on bookings – after Martinez’s substitution, they have no yellow cards on the pitch. Half an hour at half-time works in Argentina’s favour. They will benefit from the longer recovery.

Fewest shots in a World Cup final’s first 45 minutes since 1966.

Messi dogs back to hound Fabian Ruiz and latches on when the ball runs loose. Oyarzabal telescopes out a leg to try to nick the ball out of his stride and boots him on the shin. Argentina free-kick.

Spain have been the better side but then again Argentina are like scorpions and can make a lethal strike at will. Their xG is 0.00 with no shots and no touches in Spain’s box but they won’t be fazed by that.

The first of four minutes of stoppage time begin with Simon again nipping off his line to boot the ball upfield after it was played over the top of Spain’s centre-backs.

Cucurella lashes a left-foot shot across goal and past the right post. Lisandro Martinez lies down straight afterwards and signals that he needs to come off.

The preface to the Lisandro Martinez booking was one of Argentina’s best moves. They got De Paul in a position to cross, as he did so many times against England. The difference was that this time Spain got to him quickly and stopped the cross. Then the break was on.

Lisandro Martinez is knows as ‘the butcher’ but I prefer to call him ‘the cash machine’. Bet on him to be booked first in a game and you’re quids in over a season.

Here he is booked for hacking Dani Olmo down after a Rodrigo De Paul cross was blocked.

Oyarzabal receives a cute Fabian Ruiz pass that Olmo had dnmmied to let run to the centre-forward but his daisycutter of a shot from 20 yards is easy meat for Emi Martinez.

Alex Baena drives in from the left wing, beats Montiel on his left shoulder to cut infield but then tries to thread a very difficult pass to Olmo when a shot looked the easier route to goal. But Argentina just can’t get out. Spain have kettled them in their final third. They’re not panicking though. It’s more of a redoubt for them than the sidege they inflicted on England.

Excellent sliding, recovery tackle by Montiel stops Cucurella racing past him and reaching the byline. It was both crisp and a cruncher.

Cucurella is caught offside as Spain trigger an attack after a spell of passing triangles and parallelograms down the left.

Rodri leans into Mac Allister who was making a crouching run trying to creep down the outside left. Over he goes and the ref blows for a free-kick which five seconds later results in a Spain free-kick when Alvarez taps Porro’s ankle.

Pausa para hidratarse! Very tidy from Spain. Great at moving the ball in those triangles and then opening up the pitch in a fresh direction. They will feel that Yamal should have taken that early chance. Olmo has had some superb touches with his back to goal but also a couple where he has given up possession too easily. Argentina get anxious when they can’t get on the ball for long periods and Spain have the capacity to ramp that up. Rodri looking absolutely on it in terms of fitness and touch. A regal bearing.

Cucurella high up the left is tackled by Enzo but Spain swarm around him like angry wasps and force him to whack a long ball that goes out for a Spain throw. Porro makes a hash of a crossfield pass but Cucurella bails him out by being alert and jumping in before Messi to head it back to Simon.

Spain press the free-kick forcing Argentina to knock it long. Rodri goes up to win the header and it catches Mac Allister’s arm before it lands. From the Spain free-kick Cubarsi leaves a back-pass to Simon short but the keeper is off his line in  a flash to ensure there’s no danage done as he launches it before Alvarez and Messi can pounce.

First hydration break after Rodri tugs Messi’s shirt to concede a free-kick in the Argentina half.

Cucurulla, one one of his raids down the left, earns his side a corner that Emi Martinez gobbles up.

“Fifa-tina” goes the Spanish chant as Mac Allister somehow escapes without even a booking for his agricultural challenge on Olmo.

Porro tackles Gonzalez in the nick of time and makes it look as though it wasn’t that important as he saunters off upfield. As Spain attack up the left Enzo hams up the pain of a collision with the leg of Dani Olmo something rotten to earn himself a free-kick

That Mac Allister foul on Olmo was to test the referee’s tolerance. Should have booked him.

A sumptuous piece of control from Yamal takes the breath away with his velvety touch killing a long pass. But it gets Spain nowhere.

Baenal puts his foreram into Messi’s back as the Argentina captain trapped the ball with his chest, levering him over. The Argentina fans, who are in the majority, howl in protest. The free-kick is about 45 yards out and Rodrigo De Paul pings a diagonal, flat at head height, looking for a run down the right of the box but the ball just skips away from Gonzalez.

Spain’s tempo is relentless. Mac Allister slides in late on Dani Olmo and escapes a yellow card. Olmo essentially kicked his foot but the lunge was designed to stop Spain’s playmaker running off down the right. Deserved a booking.

Spain corner on the right that they take long, too long and exchange it for a throw-in.

The ball rebounds out of the penalty area and Argentina break with Spain over-committing. Gonzalez moves it on quickly looking for Messi to run through but Simon races 20 yards outside his box, as he did against France, to sweep up.

The replay of Yamal’s first shot that was saved by Emi Martinez shows that it took a welcome deflection off Lisandro Martinez which helped Emi M reach it.

Spain have been superb in these opening eight minutes. They should be ahead already. Rodri and Olmo running the game. Argentina having to work so hard just to hold them at bay.

Yamal fizzes a pass towards the D from the right to Dani Olmo. It’s behind Olmo but takes a fortunate deflection and then Olmo feeds it back to him and he wraps his left instep around the shot, looking for the bottom left corner but bends it too close to Emi Martinez who saves it with his feet then smothers it. Rodrigo De Paul loses the ball cheaply when the keeper bowls it out to him and Yamal has another effort, lashing a shot that is blocked.

Enzo is sitting deepest of the Argentina midfielders, dropping between the centre-backs as Paredes did against England. There’s a decent breeze and both sides have enjoyed passing the ball around for a minute or so each. Montiel grabs Baena to stop him running past on halfway and Spain have a free-kick.

Rodri hits a pass just behind Porro and has to foul Gonzalez to stop him running away with the ball in midfield.

Michael Buffer ‘treats’ us to his rendition of the teams’ names and the countdown. Insufferable.

Right, at last, Argentina kick off and Spain snap into the press to smother the Argentina defence and win possession, sweeping ot around midfie;d and defence.

I suppose that’s not too bad given the overrun.

Marcha Real precedes Himno Nacional Argentino.

These extra rituals have a habit of demeaning everybody they involve. As if it were not painful enough to watch Robbie Williams – something of a veteran on the World Cup stage, having also performed at Russia 2018 and Qatar 2022 – sing the ‘Fifa anthem’, Tom Cruise is reading a script so unutterably vacuous it could have been drafted by Gianni Infantino himself.

Spain in red and navy, Argentina in their light blue and white home shirts with white shorts and socks.

Mario Kempes and Andres Iniesta bringing the World Cup trophy on to the pitch in a Louis Vuitton Fifa ‘trophy trunk’ just after Robbie Williams left in a shimmering blue Adidas tracksuit. This isn’t what Jules Rimet would have wanted.

A very long speech from Tom Cruise written presumably, by someone who has never met a football fan. “Football is a language spoken without words,” says Tom C. Having heard that speech, I only wish it were true. Mercifully drowned out by the end by the fans in the stadium.

Andres Iniesta and Mario Kempes raise the World Cup trophy and then put it back down to allow Tom Cruise to deliver his homily about celebrating each other through football or some such. .

He is singing it with Nicole Scherzinger and Laura Pausini and mugging at the camera as per. Thanks Chris Martin. Thanks very much.

They’re assembling what is already the second on-pitch temporary stage of the afternoon in the middle of the centrespot. What happens to all this stuff after the big day? Fifa eBay account?

“Everyone is invited to be part of the half-time show,” declares its ‘curator’, Coldplay’s Chris Martin. Even by his standard of vapid bromides, that is quite the claim to make at an event where even the nosebleed seats cost £10,000 apiece.

Wayne Rooney says “it will be comfortable for Spain”. Joe Hart thinks Argentina’s mettle and belief will see them through.

A central section of the VIP tier has been remoulded into what looks like a fully-encased shell. That would tally with the Secret Service’s previous take-no-chances measures at sporting events that Donald Trump has attended, such as last year’s Ryder Cup and this summer’s New York Knicks triumph in the NBA finals, placing the US president behind bulletproof Plexiglass.

Will apparently now feature Sesame Street, Madonna, Shakira and Coldplay? It’s not the Dagenham Girl Pipers, is it? And we’re threatened with Robbie Williams for the second part of the closing ceremony, too, before America the Beautiful and the US national anthem. Meanwhile, they have cleared the pitch for now:

ITV has opted to stay in Manhattan but the BBC, as it did for the semi-final, is in the stadium.

Spain Simón; Porro, Cubarsi, Laporte, Cucurella; Rodri, Ruiz Dani Olmo; Yamal, Oyarzabal, Baena.Substitutes  Raya, Pubill, Grimaldo, E García, Llorente, Merino, Torres, Gavi, Pino, J García, Williams, Zubimendi, Pedri, Muñoz, Iglesias.

Argentina E Martínez; Molina, Romero, Lisandro Martínez, Tagliafico; De Paul, Enzo Fernández, Mac Allister, González; Messi, Alvárez.Substitutes Musso, Senesi, Montiel, Barco, Lo Celso, Rulli, Palacios, Paredes, Almada, Simeone, Paz, Otamendi, López, Lautaro Martínez, Medina.

Spain players have been out on the MetLife pitch for the usual pre-warm-up walkabout but that won’t be happening for Argentina, who have only just arrived. The pitch has been covered, a stage erected and a drummer performance is taking place. It will all have to come off before the warm-ups. Then doubtless more ceremony pre-kick-off. That’s even before the estimated 30 minutes at half-time. In between, hopefully, we will see some football.

The MetLife pitch has now disappeared under the giant tarpaulin display (what happens to them after the tournament?) But looking at it earlier it looked very dry. The wrong shade of green, to my mind.

Stadium still half empty as World Cup closing ceremony begins. We also appear to be about 15 minutes behind schedule as drummers and breakdancers open show.

If Argentina win Lionel Scaloni would become only the second man to coach two World Cup-winning teams, following Italy’s Vittorio Pozzo who won it in 1934 and 1938.

If Spain win, coach Luis de la Fuente, 65, would become the oldest World Cup-winning head coach passing Vicente del Bosque, who was 59 when Spain won their first title in 2010.

Incidentally Spain have two teenagers in their starting XI, Pau Cubarsi and Lamie Yamal aged 19. Only three teenagers have played in World Cup finals before and all were winners – Pelé was 17 when Brazil beat the hosts Sweden in 1958, Beppe Bergomi was 18 when Italy beat West Germany in 1982, and Kylian Mbappé was 19 when France beat Croatia in 2018.

Rodrigo De Paul replaces Giuliano Simeone, Gonzalo Montiel comes in for Nahuel Molina and the biggest change of all, Nico González takes Leandro Paredes’ place.

Emi Martínez; Montiel, Romero, Lisandro Martínez, Tagliafico; De Paul, Enzo Fernández, Mac Allister, Nico González; Messi, Julián Alvarez.

🚨 𝗢𝗙𝗜𝗖𝗜𝗔𝗟 | Recordad sus nombres.Este es nuestro 𝗢𝗡𝗖𝗘 𝗜𝗡𝗜𝗖𝗜𝗔𝗟 para la 𝗙𝗜𝗡𝗔𝗟 𝗗𝗘𝗟 𝗠𝗨𝗡𝗗𝗜𝗔𝗟.#VamosEspaña | #CopaMundialFIFA pic.twitter.com/qb5HVPeOXl

Simón; Porro, Cubarsi, Laporte, Cucurella; Rodri, Dani Olmo, Fabián Ruiz; Yamal, Oyarzabal, Baena.

The guest of honour speaks. ‘Based on the numbers we will be requesting [to host] it again immediately:

President Trump spoke with @JennyTaft ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup Final@realDonaldTrump pic.twitter.com/Wk463lj1wU

Spanish fans in Madrid are BOUNCING! 🇪🇸👏 pic.twitter.com/cBf5m7wx6i

Who could forget John Motson walking us through the drama surrounding R9’s involvement in the 1998 final in Paris? Ronaldo would turn his and Brazil’s fortunes around four years later as his double downed Germany in Japan.

The legendary Brazilian striker is at the MetLife Stadium for this year’s final.

Argentina’s Luis Artime scored goals either side of Pirri’s second-half goal as La Albiceleste defeated Spain 2-1 in Group 2 of the 1966 World Cup.

Spain fell at the group stage while the South Americans progressed to the quarter-finals, where they were defeated by Sir Alf Ramsey’s England who went on to win the whole thing. At least we have that...

🏆 #FIFAWorldCup Argentina y España: un único antecedente mundialista que favorece a la Albiceleste 📣📖 https://t.co/flct4Bx8rY pic.twitter.com/OWUdJFvYfj

Donald Trump’s attendance at the World Cup final has prompted F-16 fighter jets and military marksmen to be drafted into the biggest sporting security operation in United States history.

A no-fly zone will be fiercely guarded, snipers will be on stadium roofs and thousands of FBI agents have been drafted in to support an unprecedented operation for a football match.

Significant delays for fans are guaranteed, the White House admitted, as it urged fans to arrive at the MetLife Stadium four hours before kick-off. The World Cup final is a “Level 1” special event – the highest possible security designation in the US.

Assessing the scale of the operation, Andrew Giuliani, the executive director of the White House Fifa Task Force, told Telegraph Sport the event is comparable to Trump’s State of the Union addresses and presidential inaugurations.

“It’s bigger than a Super Bowl, to be perfectly honest,” he said. To support New Jersey State Police, Giuliani said “we’ve layered on top many federal agencies”.

This is coming from a former team-mate of Cristiano Ronaldo, by the way... Do you agree with Rooney?

If Lionel Messi wins a second World Cup, is that the end of the 🐐debate? pic.twitter.com/2bqVLLLdMR

Tom Cruise may be known for his daring, but even he has abided by the authorities’ advice and arrived well before kick-off.

Naming every celebrity attending tonight’s match will be mission impossible, but you could not mistake this guy!

🇪🇸 ¡La AFICIÓN ESPAÑOLA, PRESENTE en NUEVA YORK a pocas horas de la FINAL! pic.twitter.com/dot1wtPoiR

Trump always causes chaos when he shows up at major sporting events – and there are already huge queues outside the MetLife.

The venue started letting fans in about 15 minutes ago, an hour earlier than originally planned to ease the pressure. But security-service checks at each gate have been causing delays and bottlenecks, which will probably get worse. Even some media and accredited staff arriving at the venue had been waiting for three hours or more. Getting everyone in on time for kick-off already looks like a challenge.

The stage is set for the @FIFAWorldCup 2026 Final 🏟️ pic.twitter.com/ISedMTWxKu

A giant Argentina shirt with the words “Thank you, Leo. You are a legend” is hung in front of Rosario’s national flag memorial before the World Cup final.

La Albiceleste have backed up their 2022 World Cup triumph with another deep run to the final. Scaloni’s side are only the sixth world champions to achieve the feat.

OK, OK... There’s no point ignoring the elephant in the room. There will be many here who, for one night only, consider themselves Spanish. So here are some pointers on nailing your new-found fandom.

Spain are in their second men’s World Cup final, hoping to add to their sole win in 2010, which came against the Netherlands in a game best remembered for Nigel de Jong kicking Xabi Alonso in the chest and a lot of vuvuzelas.

This time they beat favourites France 2-0 in the semi-final but have otherwise had a slow-burning low-flair tournament built on excellent defending. They drew with Cape Verde in the opening game, but have won every match since and conceded only one goal.

They are the chaps in red, not blue and white stripes.

Lamine Yamal, and that’s pronounced La-mean not La-mine. Barcelona winger and all-round magical starboy. Destined to be the subject of excitable “he turned [insert young age] just days ago!” commentary for at least the next two international tournaments, given his birthday of July 13, 2007. That makes him young enough to have once received a bath from Lionel Messi:

Hopefully this will be recreated on Sunday, perhaps in a vat of blue energy drink during one of the hydration breaks.

Rodri, evergreen Manchester City midfielder, Ballon d’Or winner, controller-in-chief of premium football matches. Benefiting from having missed most of the Premier League season with injury, so should have ample opportunities in New Jersey to execute his trademark death by a thousand passes.

On Friday, the Orquesta Estable del Colón – one of Argentina’s oldest symphony orchestras – ended their performance of Carl Orff’s Carmina Burana to deliver a rendition of Muchachos, a song often heard at Argentina matches, with the audience clapping along and joining in. A clip of the moment went viral on X, with president Javier Milei reposting it to his 4.4 million followers.

Ayer en el Palacio Libertad después del tremendo concierto de Carmina Burana, se pusieron a tocar MUCHACHOS. VAMOS SELECCIÓN CARAJO pic.twitter.com/6OVjB9SbCn

Slavko Vincic, the Slovenian referee, will take charge of the final. He was emotional when the announcement was made, and said: “So, first of all, a shock. Then happiness. I was shaking, so it’s an incredible honour to get the World Cup final. It’s something that.. it’s only a dream for a referee, for a young referee when they start. So, I’m very proud, very proud of myself, my team.”

Introducing your referee for the @FIFAWorldCup 2026 Final....🥁Congratulations, Slavko Vinčić! 👏 pic.twitter.com/OMLJ3oA31p

Vincic will be joined by kinsmen Tomaz Klancnik and Andraz Kovacic as his assistants and will becomes the first Slovenian to referee the World Cup’s showpiece event. The 46-year-old oversaw the 2024 Champions League final between Real Madrid and Borussia Dortmund, as well as the 2024 European Championship semi-final in which Spain defeated France.

He was also the man in the middle for Argentina’s most recent World Cup defeat, when Saudi Arabia shocked Lionel Scaloni’s side in Qatar...

Some words of support from Rafael Nadal, the 22-time tennis grand-slam champion, who is one of La Roja’s most notable fans. His uncle (not that one!) Miguel Ángel was capped 62 times by Spain and represented the country at three World Cup finals.

Nadal posted on X: “Ever since I was little, football has been one of my great passions. I’ve always enjoyed playing it, watching matches and supporting the national team.

“I can still remember the thrill of being in South Africa for the 2010 final. We will never forget it!

“Tomorrow we have another chance to enjoy one of those history-making matches against a team and country which I respect and admire a lot.

“Best of luck to the national team. Let’s go, Spain!”

Opta’s supercomputer has run the numbers and, after 25,000 simulations, Spain were victors 59.6 per cent of the time, with Argentina at 40.4 per cent. Interestingly, Opta had Spain as their pre-tournaments favourites (16.1 per cent), with Argentina fourth (10.4 per cent).

🇺🇸 🇦🇷 Times Square or Buenos Aires 🤯🤯#beINSPORTS #beINWC26 #beINWorldCup2026 #beINUSAWC26 pic.twitter.com/o0eRujgcrc

Andrés Iniesta, Spain’s 2010 World Cup hero, was Messi’s team-mate at Barcelona for 14 years during the club’s most successful period. Both players were graduates of the fabled La Masia academy.

On Messi’s powers at 39 years old, Iniesta told El País: “I would say the same as always, more or less, making the difference, being the protagonist, giving assists, scoring goals, doing what he’s done all his life. I believe that if he is still active at his age, it is because he continues to do so many things right – the way he takes care of himself, the way he lives for football, the people around him, and the fact that he maintains the passion and attitude to keep improving personally and helping his teammates improve.

“Argentina has a group of players who would run through a brick wall for him. He has fully earned the respect and standing he is given. For those who love football, seeing Leo in the form he is in right now is a joy.”

Spain’s ministry of defence wishes luck to Luis de la Fuente’s side before their match against Argentina with an impressive display in the traditional Rojigualda colours. Who will you be supporting tonight?

🕘 Quedan 24 horas… 🔴 Unos colores 🟡 Una bandera 🔴 Un país ⚽️Todos con la selección española⚽️🇪🇸 Vamos España!! pic.twitter.com/XIrf4EbniS

Lionel Messi last night shared a photograph of the Argentina squad and staff on his social media accounts, along with the caption: “The best part of all these years was never just the titles, but the entire journey. Sharing the day-to-day with this group, competing together, picking ourselves up during tough times, and enjoying every step of the way.

“Thank you to each of my teammates, the coaching staff, and everyone who works every day to ensure this national team remains a family.

“No matter what happens tomorrow, this group has already written a story we will never forget – one that no one can erase.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the 2026 World Cup final. Football’s finest talent descends on New Jersey for the showpiece event of this month-long North American sojourn, with places in sporting immortality on the line. Argentina are looking to become the third nation to win back-to-back World Cups while Spain – perhaps surprisingly – play only the second final in their history; the other being in 2010, when Andrés Iniesta’s extra-time winner against the Netherlands secured a breakthrough global crown for an era-defining Spain side. The two nations have only faced off once before at the World Cup: a 1966 group game at Villa Park which La Albiceleste won 2-1.

Just eight miles separate the MetLife Stadium and Broadway, and today the spotlight falls firmly on football’s leading protagonist, Lionel Messi, with this final potentially being his World Cup curtain call. The gilded Argentine appeared to have scaled the summit by lifting the trophy that had eluded him in Qatar, but he has returned and – at 39 – has dazzled on stages across the continent all summer. Winning a second World Cup would be to achieve something Diego Maradona could not, and would only cement his legend further. Kylian Mbappé’s double in last night’s madcap third-place play-off means Messi must score two to win the Golden Boot and reclaim sole ownership of the tournament’s all-time scoring record. There has been much intrigue in the match-up between himself and Lamine Yamal, the talented Spanish teenager treading a similar path at Barcelona, not least because of that remarkable photo-shoot 19 years ago. But to reduce this final to “Messi vs Yamal” would be to diminish the talents of players such as Rodri and Julián Alvarez who are match-winners in their own right.

This will be the first World Cup final contested between the reigning Copa América and European Championship winners, and the first disputed by two countries that share a language since the inaugural 1930 competition in Uruguay, when the hosts defeated Argentina. There are precious few shared aspects, though, between this year’s finalists’ route to New Jersey. While Spain have conceded just one goal in 630 minutes of football and controlled their semi-final against tournament favourites France, Argentina have huffed and puffed their way to the final. Extra-time was required against Cape Verde and Switzerland, and Lionel Scaloni’s side had to produce late heroics against Egypt and – grr – England.

Donald Trump will present the trophy to the winning team’s captain, and his attendance has prompted the biggest security operation in US sporting history. The US president will be joined in the stands and VIP boxes by a glut of A-listers, and I wish my colleague who will be guiding you through the match later the very best of luck in identifying them all. This new-look final will also have a 30-minute half-time show starring Madonna, Justin Bieber, Shakira, BTS, Burna Boy, Gustavo Dudamel and the PS22 Chorus featuring Coldplay. Plenty to look forward to ...I think.

#2258. Cragnotti critica la protesta dei tifosi Lazio all’Olimpico

L’ex presidente, tornato allo stadio per la vittoria sul Cagliari, distingue la contestazione a Lotito dal sostegno alla squadra.

Sergio Cragnotti non condivide la protesta dei tifosi Lazio che lascia vuoti gli spalti dell’Olimpico. L’ex presidente biancoceleste è tornato allo stadio per assistere alla vittoria contro il Cagliari e ha preso posizione sulla contestazione a Claudio Lotito. Sulla scelta di non sostenere la squadra in casa il suo giudizio è netto: «Sono in totale disaccordo».

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Cragnotti, intervistato da La Gazzetta dello Sport, non mette in discussione il diritto dei sostenitori di manifestare il proprio dissenso. «Le contestazioni ci possono stare, io ne ho subite anche di dure», ha spiegato. A non convincerlo è la decisione di lasciare vuoti gli spalti mentre la Lazio continua a vincere.

Per l’ex presidente, la contrarietà alla società dovrebbe trovare spazio in altre sedi, senza togliere ai calciatori l’appoggio del pubblico all’Olimpico. A suo giudizio, l’assenza dei tifosi rischia di penalizzare proprio i giocatori protagonisti di un avvio che considera straordinario.

Nel motivare la propria posizione, Cragnotti è tornato alle proteste vissute durante la sua presidenza. Tra gli episodi ricordati c’è la contestazione legata alla possibile cessione di Giuseppe Signori al Parma.

Furono momenti di forte tensione, ma, secondo il ricordo dell’ex presidente, i sostenitori non abbandonarono mai l’Olimpico. È questa la differenza che Cragnotti individua rispetto all’attuale forma di protesta: contestare la società senza far mancare la presenza allo stadio.

#2257. Infortuni Napoli, De Laurentiis telefona al responsabile dello staff medico

Il Mattino si sofferma sull’inizio del tour europeo del Napoli, costretto a far fronte alle proprie difficoltà determinate dai risultati conseguiti in campionato, dove la zona Champions dista ormai 9 punti e lo Scudetto 14. Il quotidiano riferisce della telefonata da parte del presidente Aurelio De Laurentiis al responsabile dello staff medico, il dottor Gennaro De Luca, in merito alla questione infortuni, altro aspetto che al pesa momento sul rendimento degli azzurri: “Che malinconia. E l’aria di Oporto, calda come le nostre belle estati di una volta, non c’entra nulla. Il Napoli ha scelto come quartier generale Vila Nova de Gaia, sulla riva sud del fiume Douro. ho avuto un altro lungo colloquio con il patron per spiegare il perché di questi infortuni uno dietro l’altro. Vieni in una catena di montaggio. In ogni caso, per la società la linea resta sempre quella della fiducia in Allegri e una frustatina ai giocatori. Ma la proprietà seguirà attentamente le prossime gare”.

#2256. Inter, Chivu: "Partita degna di ciò che rappresentiamo. Non abbiamo mai raccontato..."

Inter, Chivu: "Partita degna di ciò che rappresentiamo. Non abbiamo mai raccontato..."

Installa la nostra App gratuita e accedi più velocemente alle notizie

Mentre navighi nell'app, scorri il dito da sinistra a destra dello schermo per tornare alle pagine precedenti

Scegli Fcinter1908.it come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui

Triplice fischio di Feyenoord-Inter a Rotterdam. Cristian Chivu ha commentato anche in sala stampa quanto accaduto nei 90' di stasera. Qui le sue considerazioni, raccolte dall'inviato di Fcinter1908.it in Olanda: "Noi non abbiamo da dimostrare niente, sappiamo che le partite si possono perdere anche. Per i valori che abbiamo, per quello che abbiamo costruito negli anni, abbiamo fatto una partita seria e degna di quello che rappresentiamo. Abbiamo aggiunto qualcosa nell'organizzazione, nell'intensità e nel fare determinate cose in un campo non facile".

Visto la provincialità che chiedevi?"Ho visto una voglia pazza di accettare che a volte si può stare in un blocco basso, amarlo e avere cattiveria nel rubare qualche pallone. Sapevamo di averla dentro, non dovevamo andare a ricercarla troppo. E' una questione di determinazione, orgoglio e valore".

La prestazione di Spence ci ha fatto ricordare quanto l'Inter vista in estate l'abbiamo vista poco."Non siamo mai venuti a raccontare le nostre problematiche. Abbiamo una rosa competitiva, che nelle assenze sta cercando di dare sempre il massimo. Sappiamo cosa rappresentano gli infortunati per noi. Piano piano li stiamo recuperando, siamo tutti contenti perché abbiamo più possibilità di crescere come gruppo e come squadra".

E' una reazione o il recupero della normalità?"Per una sconfitta anche se è il derby non possiamo dimenticare quanto di buono abbiamo fatto. Per noi è stata un'opportunità di reagire dopo una partita non fatta a un certo livello. L'abbiamo colta, ci siamo messi in campo consapevoli di quello che abbiamo costruito negli anni e che a volte nel calcio le partite possono finire in maniera che nessuno di noi desidera. La cosa più importante è la continuità. La stagione è lunga, non si può sempre vincere".

Ieri hai detto: faremo una grande partita."I nostri confronti sono settimanali. Dopo ogni partita abbiamo confronti, ognuno esprime il suo parere. Sono fatto così, chiedo e mi confronto. Si analizzano le cose, si cercano di capire gli errori e analizzare le cose. Funziona sempre così da noi, era così anche prima. Il gruppo ha valori sani, sa stare insieme e ama determinate sfide. Ama allenarsi e migliorarsi".

#2254. Pinamonti segna e pesa: il 52% dei suoi gol è stato decisivo

Il gol al Cagliari aggiorna il bilancio: dal 2021/22, 26 delle sue 50 reti in Serie A hanno inciso sul risultato.

Non conta soltanto quanto segna un attaccante, ma anche quanto incidono le sue reti. Andrea Pinamonti offre una fotografia significativa sotto questo aspetto: dalla stagione 2021/22, il 52% dei suoi gol in Serie A è risultato decisivo.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Il centravanti ha realizzato 26 reti decisive su 50 complessive, contribuendo a un saldo di 38 punti. Nel conteggio rientra anche il gol del definitivo 2-1 della Lazio contro il Cagliari.

Il periodo analizzato parte dal 2021/22, stagione nella quale l’attaccante classe 1999 ha raggiunto per la prima volta la doppia cifra di reti in Serie A.

Da allora, più della metà dei suoi gol ha avuto un peso sul risultato. Il dato dei 38 punti va letto secondo il criterio indicato nella rilevazione: rappresenta la differenza rispetto ai punti che le sue squadre avrebbero ottenuto sottraendo le reti considerate decisive.

Una statistica che mette in evidenza l’incisività del centravanti e aggiunge una chiave di lettura al suo rendimento realizzativo.

Il contributo più consistente arriva dall’esperienza al Sassuolo: 25 gol complessivi, dei quali 13 decisivi, per un totale di 20 punti attribuiti alle sue marcature.

Con l’Empoli, Pinamonti ha invece firmato 13 reti: 7 decisive, con un’incidenza di 10 punti. Al Genoa, il bilancio riportato è di 10 gol, dei quali 5 decisivi, per 6 punti.

Tre esperienze che, insieme ai primi numeri in biancoceleste, compongono il totale delle 50 reti prese in esame.

Il capitolo Lazio conta finora 2 gol, con una rete decisiva e 2 punti attribuiti alle marcature dell’attaccante.

A incidere è il sigillo del 2-1 contro il Cagliari: sottraendo quella rete, il risultato sarebbe stato un pareggio. Da qui la differenza tra il punto della parità e i tre della vittoria.

Per Pinamonti, dunque, una rete che alimenta il bottino personale e soprattutto sposta il risultato della squadra. È proprio questo il filo conduttore della statistica: 26 volte su 50, i suoi gol hanno fatto la differenza.

Piotr Zielinski, calciatore dell'Inter, è intervenuto ai microfoni di Inter TV direttamente dal De Kuip di Rotterdam dopo la sfida, valida per la quarta giornata di Champions League contro il Feyenoord, vinta per 3-0 dalla formazione nerazzurra di Cristian Chivu.

"Le grandi squadre danno le risposte subito. Siamo felici di aver fatto una grande partita, tre punti importanti e siamo tutti felici".

#2251. Why Burnley gambled on Fabio Celestini, an unknown Swiss inspired by Che Guevara who boxes, dances and was an electrical engineer, to spark their season back to life - and why his new players are already worried about him

Published: 22:00 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 22:00 EDT, 30 October 2026

Not many football managers have a tattoo of Che Guevara, dance in their free time and speak five languages.

But they are just three quirks which add to the layers of intrigue around Burnley's new boss Fabio Celestini, an unknown Swiss tasked with saving the Clarets from double relegation and dropping into the third tier for the first time since 2000.

After four wins in the last year, with morale in the gutter, Burnley announced Celestini as Nicky Hayen's successor on Wednesday. Many fans will have dropped their marmalade. Who? Celestini's CV is promising but this is an almighty gamble and they cannot afford for things to go wrong.

The Clarets sit 22nd in the Championship and have won just one home game inside 90 minutes in 2026. Their summer was an unmitigated disaster – they had woeful pre-season results, went 71 days without a manager, sold last campaign's top scorer Zian Flemming on deadline day with no replacement, and their chief executive, James Holroyd, walked out in September after difficulties working alongside chairman Alan Pace.

The club is in £142million of debt, according to their latest accounts, with £13m in cash in the coffers. The phrase 'basket case' comes to mind.

Celestini's appointment falls squarely on the shoulders of new chief football officer Diego Lopez, another stranger to English football, and it is one Burnley's players are unsure about.

Fabio Celestini is facing an uphill battle to avoid relegation with Burnley, who sit 22nd in the Championship

Belgian boss Nicky Hayen lasted just 12 league matches - and won only once

Burnley have not been in the third tier since 2000 but are staring down the barrel of a second successive relegation

Daily Mail Sport understands that some members of the squad have reservations about Celestini's style of play – he has favoured a possession-based 4-2-3-1 throughout his career, a system which Hayen tried and failed to implement during his time in charge.

Many clubs have turned to outsiders and succeeded – just look at table-toppers Middlesbrough under Kim Hellberg – but the lack of Championship experience in Burnley's management structure leaves Celestini to navigate a steep learning curve without much support.

On the bright side, Celestini inherited a similarly shambolic case at Basel in October 2023 and thrived. The Swiss giants were bottom of the table and had had to cancel their goal of the month award, because they hadn't scored any. Celestini saved them from relegation, restored the feel-good factor by re-signing club legend Xherdan Shaqiri, and won them the league and cup double the following season.

The 50-year-old former Switzerland midfielder – who won 35 caps for his country and played against England's Golden Generation at Euro 2004 – also has a promotion on his ledger from his time at Lausanne and a Swiss Cup with Luzern. He also led Lugano into Europe and managed Sion.

'Celestini is a determined, ambitious personality, but he can also be a stubborn coach and that has caused issues at several clubs,' Swiss football expert Craig King (@FootballSwissEN on X) tells Daily Mail Sport.

'He is capable of providing clubs with a short-term bounce before it eventually deteriorates. He has strong ideas, but his stubbornness often tends to rub people the wrong way.

'It seems that inevitably, he loses control of his teams somewhere along the way and can never get them back on track.'

His time at Russian giants CSKA Moscow, last season after he left Basel, followed that trend.  He had found out about their interest on a holiday with his dancer wife, Fanny, in the Seychelles, and took the plunge, rocking up with a Spanish-speaking coaching coterie. He even appointed his wife to help edit video clips for analysis and support in aspects of communication, a club source tells Daily Mail Sport.

He enjoyed a strong start at CSKA – he won the Russian Super Cup in his first match and they led the Russian Premier League after 11 games. Going into the winter break, they were just four points off top in fourth.

'Fabio has done a tremendous job,' the club's general director Roman Babaev said during that hiatus. 'There was beautiful football.'

By the end of Celestini's tenure in May, Babaev was describing a 'lack of self-confidence and a lack of belief in their ability to turn the situation around'. He added: 'We agreed that things could only get worse – the head coach doubted the team was listening to him.'

Celestini won 35 caps for Switzerland and appeared against England at Euro 2004

Burnley are Celestini's eighth club as a manager, having left CSKA Moscow by mutual consent in May

What changed? Reports in Russia claimed that over the winter break, players had been unimpressed with the lack of physical and defensive work, with too much emphasis on attacking and set-pieces. They lost their first three games back after the break, suffered a humbling 4-0 thrashing by Krasnodar in the Russian Cup, and went winless in Celestini's final five matches in charge.

In the space of two months, everything had unravelled. After defender Moises was sent off in the drubbing at Krasnodar, Celestini reprimanded the player in the dressing room – but the Brazilian hit back, questioning his manager's competence in front of the team. Moises was subsequently suspended and the club took Celestini's side.

'I felt like something was missing, I wasn't feeling well, something wasn't right. Other players started saying they weren't feeling well,' Moises later reflected in the documentary We Are CSKA. 'To become a champion, you need to cleanse yourself of all dirt. I blurted it all out because I knew what was simmering inside us all.'

Celestini is still well thought of at CSKA and was always willing to take accountability rather than criticise his players publicly. Former manager Viktor Goncharenko claimed that he ultimately failed because he 'didn't find common ground with the CSKA veterans', such as legendary goalkeeper Igor Akinfeev, and didn't have enough Russian coaches. He left with the club sixth in the table.

Celestini's task now is to turn around a flailing Burnley. His first assignment will be on Saturday at Turf Moor against in-form Portsmouth. Based off how he describes himself, he does not come across as a disciplinarian. Celestini says he does not like implementing fines and is not a fan of throwing things across a dressing room.

'This kind of half-time behavior might only work once a season,' he once said. 'It's like an electric shock.'

At his heart Celestini appears to be an idealist. Earlier in his career he established a foundation to support players from underprivileged backgrounds and he set up a football school in Havana.

His tattoo of Cuban revolutionary Guevara cost 180 Swiss francs (£163). He has lost count of his tattoos by now, also inking his kids and a depiction of good triumphing over evil.

Celestini appears to be an idealist. Earlier in his career he established a foundation to support players from underprivileged backgrounds and he set up a football school in Havana

Daily Mail Sport understands some Burnley players have reservations about Celestini's possession-based 4-2-3-1, a system which Hayen failed to implement

'I started reading about (Guevara), studying him. My tattoo depicts him without his military beret. There are no political references,' he said. 'What attracts me to him is that he fought his whole life for those who had nothing to do with him, and I've also fought a lot in my life, so I decided to get it.'

Another of his heroes is Nelson Mandela: 'He also dedicated his entire life to his ideas. Anyone who fought for their ideals is important to me. I admire people who take the time to help others. I don’t consider myself a good person, but I’m not a hypocrite.'

Away from football, Celestini – who speaks Italian, French, Spanish, German and English – also dances with his wife and enjoys boxing. A former electrical draughtsman, he has a good work ethic and, we hear, made a strong push for the Burnley job.

A source at the Clarets, who were also interested in Rob Edwards and Carlos Corberan, insists that Celestini was their first choice. Now they are counting on him to deliver a minor miracle.

#2250. Bologna, 13 punti in sei gare con Palladino: meglio soltanto la Lazio

I rossoblù hanno vinto a San Siro contro il Milan e rimontato il Monza, interrompendo il digiuno casalingo.

Tredici punti in sei giornate: nel periodo considerato dall’arrivo di Raffaele Palladino, il Bologna avrebbe il secondo rendimento del campionato. Secondo quanto riportato da TuttoMercatoWeb, Davanti ai rossoblù ci sarebbe soltanto la Lazio. Il confronto riguarda le ultime sei gare, non la classifica complessiva di Serie A, nella quale il Bologna deve ancora recuperare terreno per avvicinarsi alle posizioni europee.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Subentrato a Domenico Tedesco sulla panchina rossoblù, Palladino ha dato continuità ai risultati di una squadra che nella prima parte della stagione aveva faticato a trovare una propria identità. I 13 punti del periodo preso in esame equivalgono a 2,16 punti a partita, un passo superato soltanto da quello della formazione biancoceleste.

Sei gare restano un intervallo limitato per formulare valutazioni definitive. Il rendimento, però, descrive il cambio di passo del Bologna e la sua maggiore capacità di raccogliere punti. Al dato si accompagnano prestazioni convincenti e successi che hanno segnato le ultime settimane dei rossoblù.

Tra le vittorie spicca il 4-2 a San Siro contro il Milan: per i rossoneri è stata fin qui l’unica sconfitta in Serie A. Il Bologna ha poi completato sabato sera la rimonta contro il Monza, mettendo fine al digiuno di successi in casa.

Il percorso di Palladino era iniziato con il pareggio contro il Torino e la sconfitta con l’Inter, risultati che non avevano portato una svolta immediata. Da Lecce in avanti, secondo la successione riportata, i rossoblù hanno raccolto quattro vittorie e un pareggio nelle cinque gare successive. Le ultime tre uscite si sono chiuse tutte con un successo.

#2249. RILEGGI LIVE – Farioli esalta il Napoli: “Una squadra fortissima, la rispettiamo. Sugli infortuni dico…”

Il tecnico del Porto Francesco Farioli ha parlato in conferenza stampa alla vigilia del match di Champions League contro il Napoli. Ecco le sue parole:

“Il Napoli ha tanti assenti, ma gli riconosciamo le qualità che sono sufficienti per collocare altri giocatori in campo, si tratta di una squadra molto competitiva, hanno vinto due titoli negli ultimi due anni e sono fortissimi. Noi vogliamo fare la nostra partita, arrivare in attacco e segnare”.

Poi ha proseguito: “Rispettiamo tanto il Napoli, da quando c’è De Laurentiis è stabilmente in Champions e ha vinto due scudetti negli ultimi anni. Infortuni Napoli? Ci siamo nei panni dello staff tecnico del Napoli e metteranno comunque una squadra piuttosto competitiva. Il nostro obiettivo è farci trovare pronti”.
