Lavelli blasts his shot down the middle, and Inter have won the Asahi Trophy!

The teenager sizes things up, and sends Donnarumma the other way.

A stuttering run, and Provedel beats it away.

Frattesi misses! Donnarumma stretches out and flings up his left arm for a great save.

Khusanov misses, firmly striking against the post.

Donnarumma dives to the right, the shot in the opposite direction.

Rayan Ait-Nouri misses! Spooned over the bar.

We’re onto the penalty shootout. The pressure builds for the Asahi Trophy.

Echeverri is fouled in midfield, he takes it quickly, but the move breaks down and Inter get back into position again. The end nears.

Three more minutes of this have been indicated.

Gonzalez finds McAidoo, and City look for room on the right. Inter sit back and stay compact.

The game has slowed to a near-halt. It seems everyone is resigned to penalties.

Ait-Nouri finds McAidoo’s run to the back post with a fabulous low cross, but the winger’s return ball is cut out by Provedel.

If McAidoo does not stay on at City for the season ahead, you’d expect plenty of sides to be looking to bring him in on loan.

Ait-Nouri is offside as he takes the ball on the left wing, and Inter have it back briefly.

McAidoo yet again gets forward and almost forces a cross past Provedel. The ball comes back to Sangare, but his effort is blocked. City are getting closer.

Khusanov is booked for a foul in midfield, and then is on hand to block a shot on the line as Inter fail to convert.

McAidoo, yet again. A shot to the far post, yet again. A miss, yet again. He looks dangerous though.

McAidoo repeats the trick, but this time he keeps his shot low and hits the bottom of the far post. The best moment of the half so far.

However, with the scores still level, it’s only 10 minutes from a penalty shootout.

McAidoo scoots into the box from the right and curls a shot wide of the far post.

Enzo makes another change 🔄 pic.twitter.com/afvwMFYlB9

Savinho slices a shot wildly high and wide. Changes are coming.

Reis claims to meet a corner at the back post, but it comes off an Inter player. The corner switches to the right, and this one is cleared, for now. City keep the ball and Ait-Nouri picks out Gonzalez’s run, and he strains to shin it over.

Lewis has the ball in the box after quick feet from Savinho with the assist, and he prods the ball at Provedel.

Foden and Semenyo off, Sangare and Echeverri on. Lewis is City’s new captain.

On the front foot 👊 pic.twitter.com/AZC7UXYXrj

Foden sends in a corner, and Reis hooks a volley against the bar as the ball drops. Gonzalez gets back up to his feet slowly after that phase of play, and then sits back down as he awaits treatment.

City are camped in Inter’s half now, which is an improvement on the last half where it was more even, territorially.

McAidoo is released down the inside left, he clears his marker and aims for Semenyo, but Bisseck clears for a corner.

Pavard goes down after he is caught late from Ait-Nouri, but he’s fine to continue.

More subs now  Topalovic replaces Stankovic. Provedel replaces Martinez in goal.

Savinho might be the most dangerous player for City today, a sentence that has rarely been true in the last couple of years. McAidoo whips in a cross, which Henrique clears under no pressure.

Reis and Alleyne are the central defenders. Ait-Nouri is on the left, and Khusanov the right.

Stankovic gets a yellow as Savinho sprints down the inside left away from Inter Milan players. McAidoo is then tripped by Augusto, who hurt himself doing so.

A decent enough corner from Foden who swings the ball close to the back post, but the goalkeeper Martinez is fouled as the ball comes in.

The full slate of City changes, as Lewis has a shot blocked when a corner is not properly cleared. Savinho stands a cross up, but it comes to nothing. Khusanov has a shot scrambled away.

Enzo makes 5️⃣ changes at the beginning of the second half 🔄Watch LIVE on CITY+ https://t.co/rVv0RHMeAC pic.twitter.com/TIrLvBlkN3

Reis and Mcaidoo, Ait-Nouri, Alleyne, and Gonzalez are on for City, with Gviardiol one of the players going off, as is Reijnders.

Frattesi, Henrique, Mosconi, Zielinski and Bastoni are the five Inter introductions, but there are more. Mkhitrayan has gone off, with Diouf, Idrrissou, and Augusto some of the exits too.

We go again. A billion subs have been made. So far, Frattesi is on. Let’s see what we know about the rest. Ait-Nouri is on.

It’s been more or less what you expect from a pre-season friendly in the humidity.

The players are yet to shake off their summer ice creams and really get sharp again, but there are some flashes of ability here and there.

Reijnders releases Semenyo, the Dutchman plays the ball into Savinho, who dances to the byline, pulls it back, but it’s then cleared from Bisseck.

That’s it for the half, and the action restarts in 15 minutes.

Savinho wriggles into the box but just fails to find Semenyo.

Mkhitaryan concedes a foul on Lewis in midfeild, and the half appears to be drifting to a bloodless close.

Savinho, maybe in his last game for City, brings the ball high up the right but then City are forced all the way back to Donnarumma.

City are not panicked by keeping the ball, and they look for a fresh opening.

Foden commits his own foul in midfield, this time on Mkhitaryan. There are a few minutes left before half-time, at which point we may see a few changes from both sides given the early stage of pre-season.

Foden swings in a corner that Savinho briefly keeps alive before Diouf clears, and Dimarco cannot quite reach the ball before it’s played back to Donnarumma.

Barella fouls Reijnders in midfield, but it’s nothing vicious.

Semenyo clips in a dangerous-looking cross from the left wing, but it’s deflected behind for a corner on the right.

Foden is tugged down in midfield, with the City man still failing to show much of his talent in the new season.

Mkhitaryan continues to find space in pockets on the left. In general, Inter are finding it very easy to trundle to the edge of the City box.

Donnarumma flaps at a cross, and Savinho and Lewis work to clear it momentarily.

Do you think the players are coping without a hydration break?

Dimarco is fed by Diouf, with the right wing-back finding the left wing-back. He’s on the right side of the pitch too, oddly, but his left-footed shot is far from dreadful, but easily stopped by Donnarumma.

City have some pressure and Kovacic hits a group of defenders with a volley from outside the box. It’s meek stuff from Maresca’s men so far but obviously, too early to draw much from it.

City are looking to build from the back through the middle, but they are quickly crowded out. Inter come forward once more.

Diouf forces a corner on the right wing as Donnarumma clears a cross. It’s taken short, Inter switch the ball left, but Mkhitaryan overhits a pass to the byline.

Mkhitaryan receives the ball on the left, inside the box, in another dangerous position. Lewis had drifted  too far inside, but the danger passes when the forward is flagged offside.

Inter are keeping the ball calmly at the back, finding spaces between the pressing City attackers.

They break through and Donnarumma beats away a low shot from Stankovic.

Benjmain Pavard scores! Manchester City fail to clear their lines and Pavard, who started the move, is on hope to finish with the keeper stricken.

Divin Mubamba gets the opener! Semenyo beats his right-bacck and crosses to the six-yard box for Mubamba to tap in.

14. Wonderful work from Semenyo 👊He beats his man on the left to get to the byline, squares it across goal and Divin converts from close range 🎯🐝 1-0 ⚪️ https://t.co/pCDrkfriLY

Dimarco volleys wide but he too was offside, and then Martinez saves from Reijnders at the other end. It’s a free-flowing match so far.

Stankovic goes close with an early header after Inter win their first corner of the match. It’s an open game so far.

City win two early corners, but they are both cleared. A bright start for the Premier League side. Esposito then goes close at the other end, but he was offside anyway.

A recent on-pitch spat over the captain’s armband between Liverpool players demonstrated that these friendlies are not simply warm-ups.

If there are problems at the club, you can pick up on them here.

Welcome to Liverpool, Andoni Iraola!Row between Curtis Jones, Dominik Szoboszlai and Kostas Tsimikas has exposed the work the Spaniard must do to fix a dressing room where personal interests have taken priority.https://t.co/MosO6iCeLm

The fans are out in force in Hong Kong, where the Premier League continues to dominate attention.

Here’s what the former striker told Manchester City: “I’m looking forward to it. I’m not sure Enzo is going to change that much but some tweaks here and there.

“People talking about it being similar to when [Alex] Ferguson left but I don’t think it’s the same, they didn’t have the same infrastructure. He’s a top manager. He will want to put his own stamp on it.”

The biggest story in football right now is increasingly hard to ignore.

Gianni Infantino’s ludicrous plan was sunk almost as soon as it was announced, then he defended himself with such verve as to make himself look completely isolated and apart from the organisation itself, and now UEFA has said it is calling time.

The governing body says it has lost faith in the Peace Prize inventor, a problem which had been in the post for a while now.

The two London sides are facing off in their own pre-season friendly.

You can follow that live here, and find out which player has been sent off.

In their little costumes ahead of kick-off.

The venue in Hong Kong is decent enough and has started filling out. It’s a jaunty 26 degrees, 92% humidity, and raining too. It’s just like being in London during your worst nightmares, basically.

We’ll see how this continues, and if it does continue, over the coming weeks, but Phil Foden has the nod as captain for Enzo Maresca tonight.

Foden signed a new contract recently but has been well off his consistent best for some time now. Another poor season would put him in the frame for the exit door next summer, so this is a chance.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester City and Inter Milan.

The two sides meet  at Kai Tak Sports Park, Hong  Kong as their pre-season work kicks up a gear ahead of the new campaign.

City are still getting used to life without Pep Guardiola, the coach who left after a decade of high spending and high performance.

In his place is Enzo Maresca, who is not shy with the chequebook himself.

Ayyoub Bouaddi, the outstanding 18-year-old Moroccan international, should soon arrive from Lille when a fee is agreed, but Elliot Anderson and Jeremy Monga have already been signed.

City were runners-up last season, so Maresca is under pressure not just to keep things going without Guardiola, but to get the team back to the top of English football. That looks to be a tough prospect with Arsenal likely to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle in the coming days.

Inter, meanwhile, have swooped to pick up John Stones on a free transfer after his contract ended at the Etihad Stadium, and he is joined by Manuel Akanji, another former City centre-back whose loan turned permanent in the summer.

Inter won Serie A last season under head coach Cristian Chivu, and they are still one of the best sides in Europe.

While this friendly is likely to be played at a reduced pace, and will be disrupted by rustiness and substitutes, we could still learn a lot about both sides going into the new campaign, and there may be the odd surprise thrown up by a young player looking to stake a claim ahead of his senior colleagues this year.

#2212. Black November arrives at Celtic as prosecution's case against Martin O'Neill grows

An audio clip appeared online this week of former Republic of Ireland winger James McClean winding back the clock to life as an international footballer under Martin O’Neill.

Promoting his new book, McClean offered the opinion that the current manager of Celtic was never terribly big on tactics.

The game, he believed, came down to eleven versus eleven and good players were expected to take the initiative and solve any problems on the pitch.

Sending the likes of Henrik Larsson, Chris Sutton, Alan Thompson and Bobo Balde in to the trenches, the strategy seemed to work like a dream. Steve Walford and John Robertson ran the training and the set piece drills at Barrowfield and results spoke for themselves.

The issue with the Ireland O’Neill managed 10 years ago was a squad full of young English Championship players who expected to be coached on everything.

Their world, said McClean, revolved around tactics, tactics, tactics. Some struggled to get their heads around O’Neill’s old school ways or cope with the administration of a few truths.

A damning indictment on the modern footballer, Celtic fans seized on McClean’s pearls of wisdom, piecing them together with recent clues gleaned from the Parkhead dressing room.

Defender Cameron Carter-Vickers suggested that the tactics were all a ‘bit too random’. Callum McGregor offered the view that players with the wrong profile were being shoe horned into the unfamiliar positions.

Carter-Vickers could make a more constructive contribution if he could stay fit for five minutes and stop gifting goals to Falkirk in the opening minutes of games. The captain might also explain why Scott Tanser was allowed to gift through the midfield for Falkirk’s second yesterday or how he managed to miss a real chance to get his team back into the game at 2-0.

Putting that stuff to one side, supporters are compiling a case for the prosecution of Martin O’Neill. They no longer care what he did for Celtic 20 years ago or even last season.

Where their frustration is usually aimed in the direction of the board of directors more and more is now being channelled towards their 74-year-old manager.

Many accuse him of being a Dermot Desmond appointee who picks the wrong teams and leans on coaches who failed to cut the mustard at clubs like Wigan and Huddersfield.

While older diehards are uncomfortable with criticising the man who gave them some of their greatest days, the young crew are unencumbered by sentiment or history.

They would rather that O’Neill had sailed off into retirement after steering the team to a league and cup double in the summer. And there must be times when the man himself wonders if they have a point.

Everything Martin O'Neill said about Celtic's performance after defeat to Falkirk

The Martin O'Neill explanation that Celtic support won't accept after Falkirk

Martin O'Neill explains Jota omission before Falkirk clash

Had Scott Bain played for Celtic the way he did against his old club yesterday the Falkirk keeper would still be earning the big bucks at Parkhead.

After the man’s best performance in living memory it feels harsh to rain on his parade, but none of Bainarumma’s stops fell into the world class variety. As a team Celtic have become easy to play against and the attacking blueprint seems to consist of getting the ball into wide areas, throwing in a cross and hoping for the best.

When Camilo Duran is on form there is always a chance that might work. Yesterday the Colombian missed some glaring opportunities - thwarted by Bain - and, while O’Neill can’t legislate for the individual errors of strikers or experienced defenders like Carter-Vickers, he knows fine how football works.

After four wins in 10 games many now think he is a man out of his time and the trust and faith of the fans who once adored him is draining. Few buy the notion he pushed after the game that the Falkirk defeat was just one of those days. A pattern is emerging.

Between now and the end of December Celtic play 12 games. While games against Besiktas, Kilmarnock and St Mirren offer some home comfort, away trips to Dundee, Hearts, Toreense, Omonia Nicosia, Dundee United and Rangers must hold all the appeal of a one-day cruise through the Strait of Hormuz.

Come the January window the plan is to sign a physical, mobile central midfielder. They might even shore up a porous defence.

Regardless of how much they spend the most recent window - and plenty others before -  make it hard to harbour for fans to harbour much faith that they will spend the money well.

The £11million record signing, Kasper Hogh can’t buy a goal. Egyptian winger Haissem Hassan remains a talented enigma wrapped in a conundrum. They ended the January window scrambling around to bring in Joel van der Berg, Jordan Lotomba, Oliver Sorensen, Shim Mheuka and Landon Emanelo and they barely see a minute of first team action

Uniquely amongst modern football clubs Celtic see no need to hire a qualified Sporting Director capable of getting a handle on recruitment. A year since Head of Football Operations Paul Tisdale left the club they have yet to replace him. So much for aspiring to be world class in everything they do.

Before Falkirk O’Neill spoke of the need to give summer signings time to adapt to a new club.

While the demands and expectations at Celtic are on a different level, Falkirk made 17 new signings of their own. And, after a ropey start, John McGlynn has now secured his first ever victory over his old employer and won four league games in a row. Some new signings clearly settle in a little faster than others.

McGlynn’s restoration of Falkirk is a testament to the power of a good coach. Taking the  job in May 2022 the Bairns were a basket case. A League One club in the third tier of Scottish football they were losing money hand over fist.

There is nothing flashy or showy about the way he does things. Mention his name for the Celtic job and the very idea would be ridiculed because he is, essentially, a modest, working class man from Wallyford.

Yet those who say he’s not Celtic class should probably ask themselves a question now. What is Celtic class these days? What do the club aspire to be? Is being one point clear of Rangers the height of their ambition or do they want more? If so how do they plan to get there?

As a plc Celtic are duty bound to convene an Annual General Meeting before the end of December. This year all of these questions - over recruitment, ambition, the lack of communication and the strategy - deserve to be asked and​ answered

Martin O’Neill is one of the issues facing Celtic now. He is by no means the only one.

#2210. ‘Emotional’ Marink Reedijk enjoys post-match scenes as Hibernian book final spot

Marink Reedijk was touched by Hibernian fans’ emotional rendition of ‘Sunshine on Leith’ following their landmark 2-1 Premier Sports Cup semi-final win over city rivals Hearts at Barclays Hampden.

Jambos attacker Claudio Braga headed in from a corner only for returning striker Martin Boyle to deservedly level in the 19th minute before Jamie McGrath put the Hibees, bottom of the William Hill Premiership, ahead three minutes before the interval.

Hearts turned up the heat after the break but Hibs held out while retaining a threat at the other end to set up a final with Rangers at the national stadium on December 13.

It was the Dutchman’s first win as Hibs boss at the fifth attempt and Hibs’ first win against Hearts at Hampden after losing in 2006, 2012, 2020 and 2022 and the happy Hibees fans belted out the club anthem after the game.

Reedijk said: “I’m not always showing my emotions, but it’s really touching.

“So maybe it looks like I’m an ice King, so to say.

“Normally in Holland we say ice Queen, but therefore an ice King because I’m not a woman.

“But for me, it is really important that this happens and it comes close to my heart because this is what football is about.

“Guys who inspire people on the pitch with something people off the pitch and in the stands love to see. That is what football is about.”

Hibs midfielder Joe Newell admitted the scenes at the end of the game “will live with me forever.”

“That’s probably my favourite,” he said. “I’m probably getting emotional now, but it’s just seeing that at Hampden, it’s just incredible.

“We’ve been through a lot this season, obviously, already, the fans. So to give them that, it’s unbelievable. You can’t actually put it into words.

“It’s such a special feeling inside. A lot of the boys have probably seen it for the first time today.

“And if they didn’t know now how special the club is, they will do.”

Hearts boss Wouter Vrancken was “really sore and disappointed” after the defeat and believes their woes started when Tomas Magnusson and Calvin Miller had to come off in the first half, adding to a lengthy injury list.

He said: “It didn’t have to go this way because we had control of the game when it started.

“I think it started when Tomas was injured, that’s clear, and afterwards Calvin Miller.

“And those two changes – I am not pointing at the players who came in – but the changes took us off the rhythm.

“We were strong in the duels and second balls, then you lose these profiles, then it is searching again and hesitation and sometimes those hesitations give them too much space and you lose the game in those 20 minutes.

“We dominated the game again but it was just a pity that we didn’t get rewarded because we have had a lot of knocks already, also today, and you just hope they get rewarded.”

#2209. Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

United fought back after conceding an early goal against Atletico to secure their second win of pre-season.

They fell behind in the sixth minute when Arnau Ortiz’s cross into the box evaded everyone, including United keeper Tom Heaton before hitting the back of the net.

United got the equaliser their performance deserved when the impressive Shea Lacey showed his skill in the box and was fouled. From the resulting penalty, Bryan Mbeumo sent the goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

In the 72nd minute, Mbeumo got his second of the afternoon after he bundled the ball home after the United press forced Atletico into a mistake.

The Spanish side hit the post twice in the closing stages but United held on to win.

“We had a clear plan before the game, everyone stuck to it and made the game enjoyable,” Mbeumo said. “We work really hard during training for these games, the main goal is to be ready for the season starting. I have done great things on the right but also as a striker.

“I think I am more experienced on the wing but I enjoy playing as a striker. For an offensive player, it is always good to score for the team.”

And it is. All over in Stockholm as United come back from behind to win. A really good performance by Michael Carrick’s side.

Iker Luque shoots from distance. It looks good but flies over the bar. And that should be the final effort of the match...

Mendoza and Hjulmand both hit the post in quick succession. Heaton was beaten on both occasions. United were a bit fortunate there.

Now that they are behind, Atletico are starting to have a bit more possession and play on the front foot.

A slow second half comes alive as United take the lead. A slack pass in defence by Atletico is pounced upon by Fletcher. He runs to the byline, cuts the ball back to the unmarked Mbeumo, who taps in.

Another player, who has been tidy for United is Santos in midfield. He’s controlled the middle of the park, been safe in possession but also willing to fire a pass into the forwards.

Seven changes coming for Atletico. Typical pre-season move.

Mbeumo takes responsibility, waits for the keeper to dive and strokes the ball into the bottom left corner.

Dancing feet from Lacey in the box and Castillo brings him down. The referee rightly points to the spot.

Heaven is booked for a late tackle after Atletico threatened a counter-attack.

Amad can be very pleased after his first minutes of pre-season. He was very lively.

Atletico make three changes. I’ll get them to you shortly!

No time added on, so that is the end of the half. An intriguing 45 mins. United will feel they don’t deserve to be losing.

United fail to clear the ball and it falls to Arnau Ortiz, who forces a good save from Heaton. That would have been harsh on United.

Lookman has been very quiet for Atletico. Yoro has marked him out of the game but in truth, Atletico have given him nothing to work with.

Apart from the move that led to Atletico’s goal, they have barely been in United’s half. They are struggling to beat United’s press and keep the ball. United are losing but they are working very hard and playing well.

Great pressing by United leads to Amad winning the ball back. Yoro finds Lacey, who spins and goes down the right. He whips in a cross and Mbeumo rises to attack it but heads wide. Probably should have done better.

It is probably an easy comparison but Lacey has a bit of Phil Foden about him with his movement and touch. He looks promising.

Carlos Martín goes down after a coming together with Heaven. The United defender got his arm across and made minimal contact with Martín’s face but the referee falls for the play-acting and calls a foul.

An aggressive press from United as they look to deny time to Atletico. They are pushing for that equaliser.

Amad, Mount and Mbeumo all want it. Amad takes it and his low strike is deflected and looks certain to beat Oblak but the keeper reacts quickly to make the stop.

Santos punches a pass through the lines, Mbeumo combines with Mount and the attacker is brought to the ground on the edge of the box...

Nearly a quick reply by United. Amad sets the ball for Mount to cross into the box. The midfielder’s ball goes to the far post, where Shaw meets it with a thumping volley but Oblak stands his ground and palms the ball over the bar.

From the resulting corner, Yoro should do better with his header but his effort goes wide.

Early goal for Atletico. They take a short corner, Arnau Ortiz whips in a dangerous ball that beats everyone and drops in at the far post. Heaton never moved.

United dominating possession in the opening stages with Atletico happy to sit off and let the Premier League side have it. Even in pre-season, Diego Simeone has his side set up well to defend.

The visit to the Strawberry Arena means United are back at the stadium where they won the 2017 Europa League.

📸 Wayne Rooney, 2017 🏆#UEL | @ManUtd pic.twitter.com/HxZVn1mAEQ

Gianni Infantino is facing an ultimatum from Uefa: resign or face an emergency no-confidence vote.

It is understood all 55 of Uefa’s member nations would opt to oust Infantino in a vote of no-confidence if he refuses to step down. Uefa can trigger such a vote with just 43 member nations.

European football’s governing body announced a loss of confidence on Saturday morning and has demanded change after Infantino was forced to scrap his £15bn plan to sell a stake in the World Cup.

Uefa’s statement followed widespread opposition and a revolt within Fifa’s ranks that staff are calling “kill the monster”.

The Football Association backed Uefa’s stance, saying: “We fully support Uefa’s position. It is time for a full and robust review of Fifa’s leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart.”

Atletico: Oblak, Domínguez, Le Normand, Hancko, Ruggeri, Koke, Obed Vargas, Castillo, Arnau Ortiz, Carlos Martín, Lookman

United: Heaton; Yoro, Maguire (c), Heaven, Shaw; Santos, Mount; Amad, Lacey, Dorgu; Mbeumo.Substitutes: Bayindir, Mee, Vitek, Amass, Armer, Kamason, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Thwaites, Gabriel, Williams, Zirkzee.

Good afternoon and welcome to pre-season coverage of Manchester United against Atletico Madrid.

Michael Carrick’s squad continue their preparations for the new season with a trip to the Swedish capital, Stockholm, where they face Diego Simeone’s La Liga side.

Last week, United cruised to a 5-0 victory over Rosenborg but today will be their first real test. They are slowly starting to get players back but the likes of captain Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans will not be involved.

“I think we’re in a good place. I think there’s four weeks to go to the start and we’re gradually getting some boys back from the World Cup as we progress,” Carrick said.

“But I think a little bit of patience and time and trying to keep ahead and as I said, keeping everyone fit but moving forward is a really good direction to go in. And as it stands right now, I think we’re in a pretty good place. So, the boys will get better as we go.”

One player who will be looking to impress is Mason Mount. He has had an injury-hit spell at Old Trafford but is fit and ready to go for the season. He is also growing into a leadership role at the club.

He told BBC Radio Manchester: “You have different types of leaders, you have ones that are very vocal. I always want to see myself as one that leads by example and never stops working on the pitch.

“I’ve been captain previously years ago. I love the role especially with a lot of younger players on the pitch being able to speak to them and make them feel comfortable in the game and off the pitch as well. It’s a role that I really like and loved having it [the captain’s armband] in the second half.”

#2208. Revealed: Scottish journalist did not include Kylian Mbappe in his Ballon d'Or voting - separately, investigation launched into suspicious bets that returned £149,000 and predicted Harry Kane's glory

Published: 08:24 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 09:02 EDT, 31 October 2026

Kylian Mbappe was a shock top-10 omission from Scotland's Ballon d'Or vote as scrutiny continues to surround Harry Kane's victory, including the launch of an investigation into suspicious bets.

Kane and Mbappe were locked in a fierce race to be crowned the best player in the world and it was England captain Kane who just edged it at Monday's glitzy ceremony in London.

A full breakdown of how each nation's journalist voted has since come to light and it can be revealed that Scotland's voter did not put Real Madrid and France star Mbappe in his top 10.

The Scottish journalist, who was one of three reporters to leave Mbappe off his top 10, joined by colleagues in Greece and Ukraine, had Kane as his winner, followed by Lamine Yamal and Rodri, both of whom won the World Cup.

Fellow Spaniard Fabian Ruiz ranked fourth, with Erling Haaland, Dayot Upamecano, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Marc Cucurella, Ferran Torres and Lionel Messi completing his top 10.

Only two countries left Kane off the top 10 - Mexico and Ivory Coast - while four nations overlooked Yamal - Belarus, Cameroon, Croatia and Greece. Amazingly, the Greek journalist left out Mbappe AND Yamal, including William Pacho (3rd), Joao Neves (5th), Michael Olise (6th), Gabriel (8th), Marquinhos (9th) and Declan Rice (10th) instead.

Suspicious bets made around the Ballon d'Or has triggered an investigation from French police

Former winner Rodri got 10 first place votes - Croatia, Czech Republic, Guatemala, Iceland, Nigeria, Serbia, the United States, South Korea, Thailand and Vietnam - while six countries put Messi on top.

The bigger issue with the voting - as an overall event there were ample problems, as explained by Daily Mail Sport, who was in attendance on the night - was what has been described as suspicious betting.

An investigation by French publication 'Upside', as detailed by the Guardian, has explained that bets that triggered £149,000 in winnings has triggered an inquest by organisers France Football.

Police have been alerted and are looking in to allegations that 12 bets placed on Polymarket - an American cryptocurrency-based platform - were done so with, in the view of organisers, an alarming level of accuracy.

The identified accounts correctly predicted and bet on the eventual top five, leading to internal concerns at France Football that the result had been leaked or compromised.

Upside's findings, which are understood to have since been passed on to police, discovered 12 accounts created in the month of October that made a series of very similar bets. Seven of the accounts only placed bets on the Ballon d'Or market.

France Football go to great lengths to limit the number of people with knowledge of the results prior to announcements on the night. They made sure players and their entourages, including those of Yamal, Mbappe and Kane, were kept in the dark.

But, Upside's investigation has served up some alarming allegations that will now be further examined by French police.

#2207. O'Neill explains second Celtic star missed Falkirk match due to family bereavement

Martin O'Neill has confirmed Oliver Sorensen missed Celtic's match against Falkirk due to a family bereavement.

The on-loan Parma midfielder was not involved in the matchday squad for the trip to the Falkirk Stadium on Sunday, as Celtic fell to a 2-0 loss.

After the match, O'Neill confirmed the sad news that Sorensen was absent due to mourning a family bereavement.

Auston Trusty was not involved for Celtic as he grieves the tragic loss of his father.

O'Neill said: "We've had a couple of boys who are away, Auston Trusty is away at this minute.

"I think with his father dying and Oliver Sorensen had a family bereavement as well too."

Reflecting on the defeat against Falkirk, O'Neill said: "Yeah, naturally disappointing. I'm disappointed to have lost the game, first of all.

"But we had a lot of chances. A lot of chances. The goalkeeper was magnificent all afternoon. Yeah, but naturally we've lost the game, so it's very disappointing.

"They were very poor [goals], from our viewpoint. The first one, we hadn't cleared it, and the second one we've allowed somebody to just run through and pick a spot.

"But we had some really great chances, we just weren't able to convert."

#2205. ‘Obvious candidate’: Tony Cottee names who he wants as new West Ham manager over Scott Parker

West Ham are in the hunt for a new head coach following their decision to part ways with Nuno Espirito Santo. WHUFC are positioned in 8th place in the Championship table after 13 fixtures and they are in the play-offs along with Wolves, West Brom, Southampton, Birmingham City and Stoke City.

Howe, 48, cut ties with Newcastle United at the end of July after just under six years in the North East. He is now weighing up his next move in the game.

Cottee, who had two spells with the Hammers during his playing days, wants the Buckinghamshire-born man appointed at the London Stadium and has said on talkSPORT: “The obvious candidate, the stand out, the best manager available at the moment is Eddie Howe, whose done a great job at Bournemouth and Newcastle. Could he come to West Ham? I think he could. Does Eddie want it? I don’t know. Is he looking at bigger clubs? I don’t know the situation. Secondly, you could go for a West Ham connection. I’m thinking along the lines of Scotty Parker, Craig Bellamy.”

West Ham are expected to turn to Scott Parker as their replacement for Nuno. He played for WHUFC during his playing days and has managed the likes of AFC Bournemouth, Fulham and Burnley in the past.

As Cottee, Howe would be an eye-catching coup for the Hammers if they manage to get him. However, it appears they have turned their attention to Parker instead.

Howe would also probably have reservations about dropping into the second tier. He has worked at Premier League level for a large chunk of his managerial career.

He guided AFC Bournemouth up the leagues before Newcastle United came calling in November 2021 after their takeover. He then got the Toon Army into Europe during his time there.

Assuming a deal is completed for Parker, he will be under immediate pressure to get West Ham promoted. WHUFC’s proposed new boss has done it before with Fulham, AFC Bournemouth and Burnley so knows what it takes.

A move for Howe is unlikely, despite Cottee’s desire to see him join the Hammers. He is likely to get a position in the top flight at some point down the line after the work he did at Newcastle United.

West Ham lost 3-1 at home to West Brom last time out in a result that proved to be the final straw for Nuno. They have slipped down to 8th and are clinging on to the final play-off spot amid pressure from the likes of QPR and Sheffield United below them.

They are back in action on Wednesday night as they aim to return to winning ways. They face a trip to South Wales to take on Cardiff City.

#2202. Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running

Teenage sensation Max Dowman was the star of Arsenal’s first pre-season match, as he scored one goal and assisted another in a 4-1 victory over Girona.

Dowman, 16, was joined on the scoresheet by new signing Christos Tzolis, who struck with a low effort in his first game since his £34m move from Belgian side Club Brugge.

Established attackers Kai Havertz and Gabriel Jesus also scored for the Premier League champions, who were largely comfortable against opposition from the Spanish second tier.

Here are four things Telegraph Sport learnt from the match:

It was this time last year that Dowman first announced his remarkable talent to the wider world. Then only 15, he sparkled in pre-season and made it clear to Mikel Arteta that he was ready to impact matches at the highest level.

A year on, Dowman is now an established first-team player. He is the youngest ever Premier League winner and the competition’s youngest ever scorer, and he looks set to make even more of a mark this season.

In this friendly against Girona, Dowman created Arsenal’s opening goal with a gorgeous defence-splitting pass for Havertz. He did so after receiving the ball under pressure and spinning into space. Dowman then scored Arsenal’s third with a powerful low drive from the edge of the box.

Dowman is in competition with Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke for a place on the right wing, which means this summer represents a huge opportunity for the teenager. After playing for England at the World Cup, Saka and Madueke will both miss most of pre-season.

Dowman, therefore, has a serious chance of going into the new campaign as the starting right-winger. The Community Shield on August 16 must be a target in his mind.

“We know what he’s capable of doing,” Arteta said. “We want to be more consistent in terms of the performances and the actions that he can deliver, but I think today he had a really good game.”

Arsenal are close to completing a deal for Newcastle United captain Bruno Guimarães but, for now, their only outfield signing of the summer has been Tzolis. This was the Greek winger’s first match in front of supporters and he immediately demonstrated why Arsenal were willing to pay £34m to buy him from Club Brugge.

With Tzolis, it is all about the final product. Goals and assists. He struck 22 times for Club Brugge last season, and registered 29 assists.

How did he produce such impressive numbers? The answer could be seen in his first-half goal against Girona. Receiving the ball on the left wing, Tzolis quickly accelerated towards the penalty area and unleashed a low shot. It was perhaps a more direct approach than Arsenal would usually have seen from Leandro Trossard, the player Tzolis has replaced, and it caught Girona off-guard as the ball deflected into the net.

“I’m very pleased with him,” Arteta said. “First of all, the way he has adapted to the club, to the team. The connection he’s already generating with the boys. I think you’re going to love the player.

“A player who’s very direct. He’s got the goal between the eyes. He has a lot of similarities with Leo [Trossard] in a lot of the things that he can do and the spaces he can occupy. And then the work rate that he has... He’s a boy that comes with so much hunger. He wants to prove himself, it’s a dream for him. And we are here to help him.”

Havertz was one of the few Arsenal players who benefited from playing at the World Cup. His injury issues mean that, unlike most of his team-mates, he did not end the 2025-26 season in a state of exhaustion.

After returning to the pitch in the spring, Havertz enjoyed an impressive end to the campaign for Arsenal. He then performed well at the World Cup, scoring three goals for Germany.

He remains one of Arteta’s favourite players, not least because of his versatility. He started in attack in the crucial end-of-season games in May, but played in midfield against Girona. His low finish, from Dowman’s pass, represented his eighth goal in his last 12 matches for club and country.

Girona’s goal, scored by Arnau Martínez, was perhaps the only alarming moment of this comfortable pre-season victory. Martínez was unmarked from a left-wing corner when he powered a header into Arsenal’s net.

For a group of players who pride themselves on their set-piece prowess, this was a disappointing moment. It also perhaps showed Arsenal’s reliance on their two first-choice centre-backs, William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães, when they are defending crosses into their box.

Gabriel arrived at Arsenal’s pre-season training camp a few days ago, so he should be in good shape by the start of the new campaign. Saliba, though, will be missing for months with a back problem.

Without Saliba’s height and power, will Arsenal be as effective from set-pieces in the opening chunk of the campaign? Coventry City, Arsenal’s opponents on the first night of the season, will undoubtedly look to test the champions in these situations.

The reigning Premier League champions are handed the Costa Brava Trophy, which is half-heartedly lifted into the air by White. There will be far bigger trophies on offer to Arsenal in the upcoming campaign.

Arsenal have cruised to a routine 4-1 win over Girona, with Havertz, Tzolis, Dowman and Gabriel Jesus all finding the net. Arteta will be delighted with his side’s professionalism and ruthlessness.

Meslier takes too long on his goal kick, gifting a corner to Girona. However, the delivery from the hosts is so poor as it flies harmlessly out of play. That sums up Girona’s difficult evening.

There is another round of substitutions for both sides.

Two more changes in the offing...↩️ Jesus, Copley🔛 Agustien, Julienne🔴 1-4 🔵 (85) pic.twitter.com/3qt6N63qzq

🔁 Últim canvi al Girona:➡️ Stuani⬅️ Pyshchur

Once again, Meslier makes a pivotal stop on his Arsenal debut. Martin clips an exquisite pass over Arsenal’s defence to the onrushing Ruiz, who is through on goal. The striker takes the chance first time, but Meslier is there to make another crucial save.

Arsenal’s makeshift line-up, which is full of Hale End graduates, is holding firm, with Girona evidently struggling for attacking inspiration. If Arsenal can see out this victory without any injuries, then it would have panned out exactly how Arteta would have wanted.

Girona carelessly give possession away in defence, allowing Nelson to dribble towards the penalty area. The winger floats a cross into the box, which is met by O’Neill, but the forward’s lofted header hits the top of the bar.

There is cooling break in this second half to give both sets of players a quick breather. It’s been a professional performance from Arsenal, who now have various academy prospects on the pitch. Can any of them follow in Dowman’s footsteps and make an eye-catching impression in this match?

Girona make another flurry of changes, giving the youngsters from the club’s academy an opportunity to impress.

🔁 Més canvis al Girona:➡️ Gibert, Holmes, Izan, Misehouy i Jastin⬅️ Arnau, Fran Beltrán, Francés, Bryan i Minsu pic.twitter.com/fb7aVKloFx

Kabia gets to the byline and intelligently pulls a cross back to Gabriel Jesus, who curls a first-time strike narrowly wide of the far post as Arsenal search for a fifth goal.

Meslier showcases his magnificent reflexes, making a world class save to deny the recently-introduced Ruiz from close-range after he latched onto Martinez’s dangerous delivery.

Both sides make numerous changes to their line-ups to manage minutes and give the younger players some game time.

A flurry of substitutions...↩️ Arrizabalaga, White, Tzolis, Nwaneri, Dowman, Vieira, Mosquera, Calafiori, Lewis-Skelly🔛 Meslier, Nelson, Kabia, Ibrahim, Copley, Clarke, O'Neill, Harriman-Annous, Ogunnaike🔴 1-4 🔵 (61) pic.twitter.com/GDXL0JRzkT

🔁 Canvis al Girona:➡️ Krapyvtsov, Antal, Badia, Iván Martín, Abel i Pyshchur⬅️ Gazzaniga, David López, Van de Beek, Lass, Àlex Moreno i Vanat pic.twitter.com/3T6Pb9d9fG

Dowman was the breakout star of pre-season last year, when he was only 15, and he has started this campaign in similarly thrilling fashion. One assist, one goal. As you would expect, he looks bigger and stronger.

Arsenal overturn the ball in midfield and it breaks perfectly into the Brazilian’s path. Gabriel Jesus is one-on-one and makes no mistake, applying a devastating finish to make it 4-1 and put the result beyond any doubt.

The 16-year-old prodigy now has a goal and an assist. Dowman picks up the ball in the right attacking pocket, palms off Moreno, who bizarrely throws himself to the ground holding his face, before firing a resounding effort into the bottom corner. He’s such a talented footballer and looks at home in Arsenal’s first team.

Out of nothing, Girona have pulled a goal back. Kim whips a corner into the box, with the unmarked Martinez slamming a magnificent header into the top corner, leaving Kepa rooted to the spot. Arteta will be furious with his side’s complacency there.

🎯 El gol d'Arnau pic.twitter.com/Op6oX3LBzK

The team known as “Set Piece FC” looked alarmingly vulnerable at that Girona corner. Perhaps this is simply the reality of life without William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhaes. The good news for Arsenal is that Gabriel is back with the squad and should be ready to go for the start of the campaign. The bad news is that Saliba’s back injury will rule him out for months. Will that lead to more sustained vulnerability over the opening chunk of the season?

Girona have sent a host of players out to warm up. They’re playing in their fourth pre-season match, with their league campaign due to start on August 16 against Leganes.

We are back under way for the second half.

That was a straightforward half for Arsenal. Arteta will be pleased with Havertz’s showing in his 33 minutes on the pitch. After missing so much of last season through injury, it has been a good summer for Havertz so far. He scored three goals in Arsenal’s final six games of 2025/26, and then netted four times for Germany in June.

The 2009-born playmaker was Arsenal’s standout player in that first half. Dowman’s confidence and class on the ball has been brilliant, with his expertly-crafted assist for Havertz’s opener an obvious highlight.

Arsenal are in complete control here in Spain thanks to first-half strikes from Havertz and Tzolis.

A dominant first-half display in Girona 🙌 pic.twitter.com/ZprG2xLYyj

Dowman dribbles into the penalty area with ease, drifting past a couple of defenders before he is apprehended by Moreno. He goes down, but there is very little in the challenge.

Arsenal are in cruise control here. Girona are chasing shadows. Unsurprisingly, there’s a real gulf in class and quality between the two sides.

Once again, Dowman dances away from Moreno. The youngster sets up White with a reverse pass, but the Arsenal captain’s disappointing cross drifts out for a goal kick.

Tzolis registered 22 goals and 29 assists for Club Brugge last season. He is an end-product machine, and that goal was a little indication of how he racks up such eye-watering numbers. After receiving possession on the left wing, he was so quick to shift the ball onto his right foot and fire the shot at goal. He describes himself as a “direct” player and that was evidence of it.

There are three early changes for Arsenal, with Gyokeres, Havertz and Hincapie taken off for Gabriel Jesus, Vieira and Salmon.

We're making a triple substitution...↩️ Havertz, Hincapie, Gyokeres🔛 Vieira, Salmon, Jesus🔴 0-2 🔵 (32) pic.twitter.com/NtpnUsfAY6

The new winger is one-on-one with Martinez and darts inside, before firing a low effort into the bottom corner. It took a slight deflection, leaving Gazzaniga with no chance. Tzolis has looked lively and slotted into Arsenal’s attack seamlessly so far.

Tzolis is slipped into the penalty area from his left-wing berth, but instead of shooting, he tries to find Gyokeres with a pass. Girona surround the Swede before Dowman’s follow-up strike is blocked.

Since their goal, Arsenal have assumed real authority of this encounter and look like the far superior side.

Girona captain Martinez slams a powerful long-range effort at goal, but it fizzes wide of the bottom corner. Kepa seemed to have it covered regardless.

Arsenal are hunting for a second, with Lewis-Skelly picking out Havertz with a floated pass. The former Chelsea man is inches away from teeing up Gyokeres for a second, but Gazzaniga is there to make a goal-saving interception. Dowman has also been heavily involved in these early stages, providing the assist for Havertz’s opener.

After his extraordinary breakthrough campaign last year, Max Dowman has a huge opportunity this summer. With England wingers Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke not returning until later in pre-season, Dowman has a chance to take ownership of the right wing position ahead of the Community Shield. His assist for Kai Havertz, a lovely measured pass after an excellent piece of skill in midfield, was a sign that Dowman means business.

Dowman drifts inside and pops up in the right channel, wriggling past Moreno, before threading a delightful pass through to Havertz. One-on-one, the German calmly slots a close-range effort into the bottom corner, giving Arsenal a well-deserved lead. So much credit must go to Dowman, who has started this game excellently.

Girona have some sustained possession to take the sting out of the game then burst into Arsenal’s penalty area, with the ball attempted to be pulled back to Van De Beek. The visitors have good numbers defending and comfortably deal with the danger.

Tzolis floats a free kick into the box, which Gyokeres meets at the back post. The striker directs the ball back across goal towards Calafiori, whose close-range header is caught by Gazzaniga.

It also appears that Havertz and Nwaneri have been tasked with quite free-roaming attacking midfield roles, with Lewis-Skelly positioned as a one-man holding pivot. It’s a strong but experimental line-up from Arteta.

After suffering an injury at the end of last season and missing the World Cup, White returns to action here this evening and wears the armband. He will look to support Dowman, who appears to be starting on the right wing.

It’s been a confident start from Arsenal, who are stroking the ball around in a very assured manner. Havertz looks to pull the strings by firing a low cross towards Gyokeres, but the delivery is scrambled clear by the Girona backline.

White leads Arsenal out onto the pitch to face Girona, who boast the likes of Van de Beek, Gil and Moreno in their starting XI.

Talking earlier this week, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta sent out a determined message to other clubs by outlining their ambitious transfer plans.

“A lot is happening,” Arteta said. “We all know about the context of this transfer window. From ownership to the board, the sporting director and myself, we know that we want to take this club to a different level.

“That is going to require a better squad, better individuals. We have identified where we have opportunities to grow and to improve and to evolve our game and what is going to be needed to achieve that. Hopefully very soon we can start to put things in a very concrete way.”

Arteta also believes that last season’s Premier League title has served as added motivation for his squad to improve and hit new heights.

“This has to be the start and this has to be the standard,” he said. “Excellence has to be our standard and this has to drive to attack the future. The way we behave daily with more and more determination and ambition, because we’ve shown that we’ve got it. Now we have to show that we belong to this level and we want to increase and take this football club to a different dimension.”

It had been a relatively quiet transfer window for Arsenal, who have recruited just goalkeeper Illan Meslier and winger Christos Tzolis.

However, Arsenal are now moving very bullishly, closing on Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimarães, while also targeting Real Madrid’s Vinícius Júnior.

Sam Dean has the full breakdown of a potential deal for the Real Madrid star and how Arsenal are prepared to continue flexing their muscles in the transfer market in what would be one of the biggest moves in Premier League history.

It was January 2025, with Arsenal earning a hard-fought 2-1 comeback victory in the Champions League courtesy of first-half goals from Jorginho and Ethan Nwaneri.

Since this European encounter, Girona have been on a seriously downward trajectory, enduring lowly 16th and 19th finishes in La Liga, with the latter ensuring relegation to the Segunda Division, where they’ll play in the upcoming campaign.

August 5: Arsenal vs Real Betis (Dublin, Ireland)

August 9: Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund (London, England)

August 12: Arsenal vs Como (London, England)

August 16: Arsenal vs Manchester City (Cardiff, Wales)

Mikel Arteta’s side will then begin their defence of the Premier League title on August 21 when they host newly-promoted Coventry City on August 21.

Arsenal are closing in on one of the statement signings of the summer, with Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimarães getting closer to joining the Premier League holders.

This deal means that Christian Norgaard is expected to leave and seal a move to Everton for around £7m.

As previously reported by Telegraph Sport, Guimarães has been Arsenal’s top target for weeks. It is believed that he will cost around £80m.

Sam Dean has the full story via this link.

🔵 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 🟡©️ White with the armband✨ Nwaneri floating in the middle🆕 Tzolis from the startAnother pre-season test awaits, LIVE on The Arsenal 📺 Presented by @deel 🤝

Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

#2201. ‘All of a sudden’: Sheffield United in strong position ahead of next three fixtures, says EFL expert

Sheffield United have risen up to 10th in the league after their first 13 fixtures and they are three points off the play-offs behind West Ham in 8th. SUFC won 1-0 at home against Wrexham last time out with Ben Brereton Diaz getting their goal.

The Blades are back in action on Tuesday evening with an away trip to Deepdale to face rock bottom Preston North End. They then face struggling Charlton Athletic and Watford.

Maxwell has delivered his verdict on the South Yorkshire outfit on the Not The Top 20 Podcast on YouTube: “Maybe the most impressed I’ve been with them this season (against Wrexham). That is quite a lot bar to clear I will say. (Romelle) Donovan looked good. I think increasingly (Michael) Cooper in goal, (Japhet) Tanganga and (Liam) Kitching at centre-back, (Sydie) Peck and (Kalvin) Phillips in midfield, it’s quite a nice spine.

“All of a sudden they’re up in 10th Sheffield United having had what felt like a really poor start to the season. They’ve got Preston next away and then Charlton away, after the break Watford at home so 10th right now with three fixtures on paper against teams right down at the bottom.”

On his day, Sheffield United goalkeeper Michael Cooper is one of the best players in his position in the division. He is then backed up on the bench by the experienced Adam Davies.

The Blades have been solid defensively so far in this campaign. Cooper has kept five clean sheets along with Stoke City’s Viktor Johansson and Birmingham City’s James Beadle, with only Swansea City’s Lawrence Vigouroux keeping more.

As Maxwell has alluded to, Japhet Tanganga and Liam Kitching have formed a solid partnership in the heart of defence. The latter joined from Premier League new boys Coventry City in the summer and he has made a positive impression.

Sheffield United have useful full-backs like Femi Seriki and Harrison Burrows who like to get up and down the flank. Further up the pitch, Kalvin Phillips, Sydie Peck and Oli Arblaster are all good options to have in the middle of the park.

Patrick Bamford is a proven goal scorer up top for Wilder’s side. They also have dangerous attackers including Brereton Diaz, Romelle Donovan, Tom Cannon and Tyrese Campbell at their disposal as well so the competition and depth is decent.

Despite not being able to spend much money in the last transfer window, Sheffield United still have a strong squad. SUFC also have an experienced manager in Wilder.

There is no reason why the Blades can’t push for the play-offs this term. They have a nice blend of youth and experience in their ranks.

They will need to be at their best to get a win against Preston North End, regardless of the Lilywhites’ position and poor form. No game is easy and Wilder will be aware that it could be a potential banana skin for his players.

#2200. La strigliata di Hoeness, il "parlate pure": Bayern, Lennart Karl zittisce le critiche in Champions

Una rete, un'esultanza emblematica e un bel macigno tolto di dosso. Lennart Karl è tornato a brillare nelle notti di Champions League, con la maglia del Bayern Monaco, dopo un'astinenza dal gol che durava da quasi due mesi. La rete siglata ai danni dell'Atletico Madrid questa sera, su autentico scippo di uno sbadato Le Normande nella propria area di rigore, ha spalancato la porta di Oblak e il trequartista tedesco non ci ha pensato due volte ad azzannare la palla poi buttata in porta.

Quale miglior modo per rispondere alle critiche? Ma il gol realizzato questa sera al Metropolitano - solamente il secondo centro stagionale dopo quello contro l'Elversberg in Bundesliga - ha sbloccato una partita piuttosto scorbutica e tesa nella tana dell'Atletico Madrid. Un contributo enorme per strappare tre punti d'oro che proiettano così i bavaresi in ottava posizione al momento, a quota 8, a -1 da Barcellona e Aston Villa che hanno già disputato il quarto turno di Champions. L'esultanza eloquente, con il gesto delle mani come a voler dire "parlate, parlate" mentre lui dimostra i fatti sul campo, è stata un modo per spedire un messaggio a chi lo ha additato ultimamente di scarsi risultati.

In un'intervista sibillina al quotidiano tedesco Welt am Sonntag, il presidente onorario del club bavarese Sebastian Hoeness aveva parlato così del 18enne: "Ho intenzione di avere una conversazione seria con lui. È molto lontano dall'essere una superstar: i giovani giocatori hanno bisogno di umiltà". Una tirata d'orecchie che non era passata inosservata: "I giovani giocatori hanno anche bisogno di pressione. Non so se faccia bene a Lennart Karl essere protetto eccessivamente tutto il tempo".

Il classe 2008 arriva da una stagione, la scorsa, da autentica baby rivelazione e talento cristallino dell'Academy del Bayern Monaco. Scoperto e lanciato da Vincent Kompany, nell'arco di 1984 minuti tra tutte le competizioni (Champions League, Bundesliga, Coppa di Germania e Supercoppa) è arrivato a toccare vette da 9 gol e fornito 8 assist alla prima stagione in prima squadra con i bavaresi. Questo prima dell'infortunio subito in allenamento, ad una settimana dal Mondiale poi saltato. Ha impiegato il suo tempo per ritrovare la forma migliore e forse è ancora sulla via del recupero, ma questa rete all'Atletico Madrid potrebbe averlo sbloccato definitivamente.

#2199. Celtic handed fresh agony as star who got away rewrites Eredivisie record books

Sizzling Sondre Orjaester tore up the Eredivisie record books on Sunday and handed Celtic an unwanted reminder of the winger who slipped through their grasp.

The Norwegian wide man was the star of the show as FC Twente demolished Excelsior 9-0, chalking up an astonishing FIVE assists in the rout. The remarkable haul is the highest assist tally recorded by a player in a single Eredivisie match this century and underlines the stunning form that has made Orjaester one of the hottest properties in Dutch football.

It's another painful "what if?" moment for Celtic as the Premiership champions continue to search for answers in a difficult campaign.

The Parkhead club kept close tabs on the former Sarpsborg flyer and pushed to land him during the January 2025 transfer window. But despite significant interest, a deal could not be agreed and Orjaester remained in Norway before eventually making the move to Twente.

Read more: Miffed Martin O'Neill bites back in Celtic BBC interview exchange

Celtic instead turned to familiar ground, bringing Jota back to Glasgow in a £10 million deal. However, the Portuguese winger suffered a serious setback when he picked up a long-term injury against Dundee United in April 2025.

That left the Hoops back in the market for reinforcements and, by the close of the summer transfer window, Michel-Ange Balikwisha and Sebastien Tounekti had arrived in a double deal worth around £10m.

Orjaester, meanwhile, was flourishing in the Netherlands.

The 22-year-old previously opened up on why he decided against a switch to the Scottish champions, insisting the style of football on offer elsewhere was a better fit for his development.

Speaking to De Twaalfde Man, he said: "I don't think the type of football played there suits me best.

"The Eredivisie has proven to be a very good platform for young players like me, and there are a lot of technically skilled players there.

"I didn't have much time to think about whether I wanted to go to FC Twente.

"Of course, I knew they were narrowly eliminated in the Europa League last season against Bodø/Glimt. Everyone I spoke to about the club talked about the fans and how Twente played."

While Celtic continue to wrestle with their current issues, Orjaester is producing the sort of numbers that justify the hype which surrounded him. And after rewriting the Eredivisie record books with a five-assist masterclass, the Norwegian has shown exactly why so many believed he could have been a star in green and white.

#2198. Man United boss Michael Carrick appears to ignore Lisandro Martinez after defender sent off for deliberately elbowing Wesley Fofana

Published: 10:04 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 10:21 EDT, 31 October 2026

Michael Carrick could not even look at Lisandro Martinez after the Manchester United defender's moment of madness saw him sent off away at Chelsea.

Martinez, not looking at the ball as a corner was whipped in, went in with his elbow on Wesley Fofana's throat, only a minute or so after picking up a yellow card for pulling back Morgan Rogers.

A VAR review was recommended and Martinez, who was in the headlines earlier this month for calling out the United hierarchy for letting Carrick and the players down, was shown a second yellow card and given his marching orders.

It was a ridiculous decision by Martinez to make the challenge he did on Fofana and Carrick elected not to even acknowledge his centre back as he trudged down the tunnel.

Cole Palmer scored the resulting penalty, given away by Martinez, to make it 2-0.

Lisandro Martinez (left) got ignored by boss Michael Carrick (right) after his sending off

Martinez made a ridiculous decision to lead with his elbow, fouling Wesley Fofana in the box

Director of football Jason Wilcox, explicitly called out by Martinez after a 2-0 defeat in the Champions League to Atletico Madrid, watched on alongside CEO Omar Berrada as Martinez's dire decision making took the game away from Carrick's side, who had been the better team in the first half.

'You can't keep changing, changing, changing the manager,' Martínez said in his Madrid rant. 'What about other areas? [looks up] I can't say more.

'It is easy to say the coach, easy to say the players but also we have to see other areas [points up].

'He [Carrick] does his best. Every season is different. You can't stay with what you did last season.

'The teams knows how you play, they know every detail, if you don't change next season is a big problem.

'Last season we did everything, we created the base to create an amazing team.

'It is annoying, disappointing coming here and I am not seeing my team trying to get an amazing result here.'

But he cost his team dearly away at Chelsea, not just with his defending for the opening goal by Rogers, where Martinez and centre back partner Harry Maguire looked incredibly slow, but also for the reckless foul on Fofana that saw Chelsea awarded a result-sealing penalty.

Martinez had a lot to say in Madrid but he was the key person to blame at Stamford Bridge

Martinez was fined for his comments made in Madrid and he sat down for a pow-wow with the hierarchy to thrash out any differences and to get back on the same page.

Yet, at a time when results on the pitch needed to see huge improvement, not least after the Stretford End booed the players off after the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth last weekend, Martinez let his team-mates down on a day where they looked the better side for 45 minutes.

The expectation is that Martinez will leave at the end of the season and it could even be as early as January with no guarantee that United trigger the additional year option they hold on a contract that expires at the end of the season.

#2197. PSG, 20 gol in 4 partite di Champions: media di 5 a gara e 14 turni senza sconfitte

Il PSG continua a viaggiare a ritmi altissimi in Champions League. Con il 6-0 sul campo del Villarreal nella quarta giornata della League Phase, i parigini hanno raggiunto quota 20 gol in quattro partite, per una media di 5 reti a gara.

Il bottino nasce da quattro vittorie su quattro: il 6-1 allo Slovan Bratislava, il 4-2 sul campo del Manchester City, il 4-2 al Barcellona e, appunto, lo 0-6 di Villarreal. A fronte dei 20 gol realizzati, la squadra ne ha subiti soltanto 5, ed è salita a 12 punti. Un dato colpisce più di altri: in tutte e quattro le gare i parigini hanno segnato almeno quattro reti, mantenendo anche la porta inviolata contro il Villarreal. Numeri che certificano il momento di forma della squadra e la continuità di rendimento rispetto alla scorsa edizione.

Il successo di Villarreal ha portato anche un primato storico: il PSG è arrivato a 14 partite consecutive di Champions League senza sconfitte, un risultato mai raggiunto prima dal club, che stabilisce così il nuovo record. La serie era iniziata nella scorsa edizione con l’1-1 contro il Newcastle e ha attraversato le sfide con Monaco, Chelsea, Liverpool e Bayern Monaco, fino alla finale con l’Arsenal: finita 1-1 e vinta dai parigini ai calci di rigore, che ha consegnato al club la Champions League. Nelle prime dieci gare sono arrivate sei vittorie e quattro pareggi, compreso quello con l’Arsenal, poi risolto dai tiri dal dischetto, a cui si sommano i quattro successi di questa stagione.

#2196. Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds

Leeds United came from 2-0 down at half-time to beat Liverpool 4-2 at Soldier Field in Chicago as Andoni Iraola’s side were undone by sloppy defending in the second period.

Liverpool’s dominant first-half display was underlined by goals from Luke Chambers and Florian Wirtz. However, Daniel Farke’s men replied with four strikes in 25 second-half minutes through Sean Longstaff, Brenden Aaronson and two alarmingly similar goals from Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

🎯 "CALVERT-LEWIN ARRIVES!" pic.twitter.com/CaHOeXQn7E

🤩 "Calvert-Lewin makes it FOUR!" pic.twitter.com/mEEi882OWi

Liverpool centre-back Chambers, 22, who spent last season on loan at Charlton Athletic, opened the scoring on seven minutes, pouncing on a Dominik Szoboszlai corner which had been flicked on at the near post by Milos Kerkez.

Jeremie Frimpong, serviced by a wonderfully flighted cross-field ball by Trey Nyoni, then set up Wirtz to make it 2-0 five minutes before the break, but on the hour Leeds began their recovery when Aaronson scored following a mistake by Kerkez – who gave up possession to Ethan Ampadu in his own half.

GOAL! Aaronson pulls one back! 2-1 pic.twitter.com/tdy17cITSd

Ampadu’s long throw was flicked on to Calvert-Lewin to level the score, then minutes later Curtis Jones’s carelessness allowed Longstaff in to put Leeds in front.

🔥 "LONGSTAFF! WHAT A TURNAROUND!" pic.twitter.com/G9LvLIk0Mi

And it was a familiar story five minutes from time when Ampadu’s throw again prompted chaos in Liverpool’s back line, allowing Calvert-Lewin to steal in front of Jones and seal victory.

Liverpool return to Anfield for friendlies against Monaco and Como before they begin their Premier League season away at Newcastle United later this month.

Leeds have matches against RB Leipzig, Manchester United and Augsburg before their league campaign gets under way at Nottingham Forest.
